links.title: Potential Methodology for Determining the Efficiency of Non-Linear Open Systems
links.body:
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mes/23tvCUhfGRWJCtkykaHb4UcK7YGCWsjG8v2csQp2MwoWc6n5Bpw9TPwATLNdEXbDgbF7W.jpg)


>This article was originally written by @beneficencetv as a [Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1epQ_O0IF_QCWRcD_dwi_wvJjfZ18bPLhE4MQU8uY3xg/edit?usp=sharing) and he has given me permission to post it on the Hive blockchain.

---

As you know, my Synthetic AC model is a good start for bridging the gap between the abstract concepts of vortex based math, teslas impulse technology, and Thomas Bearden's asymmetric regauging principles with mainstream electrical engineering practices. However, part of the theory has always been an extension of what others have said for decades. A cold hard truth. That this type of energy cannot be accurately measured with our standard tools. In order to understand how to develop a work around for this issue I had to ask myself why. Why is it that this type of energy cannot be accurately measured with standard methods? Engineers will be demanding a mathematical framework to go along with my synthetic AC model if it is to be taken seriously. This is my attempt at providing that mathematical framework.

Before we continue, we have to take a look at how mainstream engineering operates. 
Mainstream electrical engineering treats everything as a <u>closed system</u> governed by the laws of <u>**Equilibrium Thermodynamics**</u>. But this completely ignores the fact that a separate set of laws called **<u>Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics</u>** governs <u>open systems</u> interacting with environmental gradients. 

## Example

[Equilibrium thermodynamics in a Closed View] --> Stagnant Water in a Sealed Pot (there is Uniform temperature and zero net flow)

[Non-Equilibrium thermodynamics in an Open View] --> Can be thought of as a Persistent Whirlpool that is maintained continuously by a drainage gradient. 

Before diving into the new power calculations we must fundamentally change how we look at an electrical circuit. 

As I just mentioned, mainstream electrical engineering relies on this basic oversimplification: That all electrical systems are closed, symmetrical, and in equilibrium. Because of this, standard measurement tools are engineered with built-in mathematical blind spots for certain unconventional systems. 

To understand the mathematics of an open, non-equilibrium system, you must first understand three foundational concepts:

# 1st Concept: \

Fallacy

Conventional electronics teaches us that current must flow in a complete, closed loop from a battery's terminal, through a load, and back to the opposite terminal. While this is true for moving electron charge carriers, energy itself does not travel inside the wire.

Energy travels through the space around the wire as an electromagnetic field envelope (called the Poynting vector). When you use specialized geometry—like the ABHA coil—coupled with rapid, time-asymmetric switching, you can physically partition these field vectors using something as simple as a high speed diode.

The forward energy and the backward collapse do not have to fight each other in the same wire; they can be geometrically guided along entirely separate pathways while still being coupled via a field bridge. 

# 2nd Concept: Reversal Symmetry vs. Asymmetric Sequencing

This goes back to my synthetic AC model where we differentiate between True AC and synthetic AC.

- **True AC (Reversal):** Imagine a closed pipe filled with water. A piston pushes the water forward, then pulls it back along the exact same path. The water simply sloshes back and forth in place. Because the fluid is constantly reversing direction, it fights its own momentum, creating friction and heat. Every forward push is entirely undone by the backward pull.
- **Synthetic AC (Sequencing of two or more bidirectional pulses):** Imagine two separate people standing on opposite sides of a room, taking turns firing pingpong balls into a central zone. On a standard meter, it *looks* like an alternating wave. But in reality, it is a choreographed sequence of independent, time-asymmetric events. These two waves might look identical on an RMS meter. However, as we peak behind the curtain we realize the stark truth. They are not the same. True ac is not the same as a synthetically created alternating current. So why do we categorize them as being the same? My synthetic AC model aims to correct this inherent contradiction. But we need a new mathematical formula to determine the actual efficiency of the system if we are going to get anywhere with the engineers. A new methodology needs to be formed from this thesis. This is my attempt at a potential method for calculating the instantaneous power potential of non-linear systems that utilize synthetic AC.

# 3rd Concept: The RMS Blind Spot

A standard digital multimeter or an averaging oscilloscope does not look at reality in real time. It uses a mathematical smoothing tool called Root-Mean-Square (RMS).

RMS acts like a statistical blender: it takes sharp, high-energy spikes such as the reactive -168V output from our coil and smooths them out over time into a gentle, artificial average.

If you have a true sine wave and a highly non-linear, pulse-driven synthetic wave, their integrated averages might yield the exact same RMS voltage. However, how they release energy is different. How they interact with the environment is different. How they perform work under load is also radically different from one another. Thus, is the need for the new synthetic ac classification. Remember, the Synthetic AC model at its core is a taxonomy correction. 

# What the Upcoming Math Proves

The mathematics that follow will completely abandon the artificial averaging of RMS. Instead, we will look at Instantaneous Power Integration over Time, measured in absolute units of work: Joules.

By calculating the forward path and the backward recovery path as independent thermodynamic events in Joules, we can accurately track how a geometry-dependent open system successfully harvests energy from environmental gradients. From this we can extrapolate how much energy, if any, is being extracted from the surrounding vacuum. 

Let's look at what lt. col. Thomas Bearden has to say before we go over the standard way to calculate efficiency:

>**Tom Bearden - How the MEG Really Works**

https://youtu.be/tx5zCRnxiPU?t=1030

---

# STANDARD WAY TO CALCULATE EFFICIENCY:

Root-Mean-Square (RMS) is a non-linear, statistical calculation based on squaring the voltage or current values, integrating them over time, and then taking the square root: 

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mes/EoEwn37dqL19iXFJQwFZ7Dst8mqQ9sEFwULtJ6PzFNQKeRcYCWELrKbrheDJbRV6oF5.png)

Because of the square root and squaring operations, RMS voltages do not obey linear addition. For example, if you have two independent, orthogonal AC waveforms at 5v rms and 5v rms adding them together does not equal 10v rms. Their combined effective voltage is calculated via the vector sum (square root of the sum of squares): 

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mes/23wCdHk6HYkYQkbUNfmUyzJ9oMNAw8pVp83rccdN6fqxVFxMGyudyhSzFWoyJMxun3VNd.png)

The Correct Methodology to fix the COP Equation is to properly account for all partitioned energy events. 

To properly account for all partitioned energy events and prove the COP is greater than 1 (COP > 1), we must completely abandon the concept of RMS and focus strictly on Instantaneous Power Integration over Time (Joules).

**Remember:**

Energy is work, measured in Joules (J). Power is the rate of energy transfer, measured in Watts (W). We must measure the input and output energy independently by calculating the exact area under their respective power curves. 

Use this structured method to mathematically correct your COP calculations: 

First we have to define the time domains. These domains are Time Asymmetric. 

Unlike standard AC, where a cycle is split into two equal, symmetrical halves, a **Synthetic AC cycle** must be evaluated as a series of discrete, non-linear time segments (t₁, t₂, ...) within a total period (T).

Let:
- **t₁** = The duration of the active forward excitation pulse (Driving Phase).
- **t₂** = The duration of the asymmetric field collapse/radiant recovery event (Collapse Phase).
- **T** = The total cycle time (t₁ + t₂ = T).

**2. Equation 1: True Instantaneous Input Energy (U<sub>in</sub>)**

Because the backward pulse dynamically alters the battery source's local scalar potential, you cannot use average input current. You must integrate the instantaneous product of input voltage (v<sub>in</sub>) and input current (i<sub>in</sub>):

## Input Equations

True input energy equals the integral from zero to capital T, of input voltage times input current, with respect to time. 

Track the True Input Energy (U<sub>in</sub>).

You cannot use an average current or voltage meter on the battery source because the high-dV/dt backward pulse is altering the battery's potential dynamically.

- **The Method:** Capture high-speed, synchronized oscilloscope traces of the instantaneous input voltage (v<sub>in</sub>(t)) and input current (i<sub>in</sub>(t)) directly at the source terminals.
- **The Equation:** Multiply them to find instantaneous power, then integrate over the exact time cycle (T):

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mes/23vsr3sgwQ6zw2hUEwYhKqrj1ezmw9iv72AXf9dp1SW4wskRJan8yWkqrrC8HQ1Fe2rN6.png)

## Output Equations

**Track the Two Partitioned Output Energies Separately**

Because our system partitions energy into two distinct spatial/temporal pathways (Forward to load, Backward to recovery terminal), we must compute their energies individually in Joules, then add the *Joules* together. Joules can be added linearly; RMS values cannot.

(W)Forward: Forward work equals the integral from zero to t-one, of load voltage times load current, with respect to time. 
(W)Backward: Backward work equals the integral from t-one to capital T, of recovery voltage times recovery current, with respect to time. 
(W)total: Total work equals forward work plus backward work.

>- Forward Energy (W<sub>forward</sub>):

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mes/EocDnyKFEWPtzY2ppY8kcFoYfaSvv2PSm8yeKXisBsrwK4nvznmCrDD7v8yPczYVcCY.png)

>- Backward / Recovery Energy (W<sub>backward</sub>):

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mes/23vsr8H93ZAuZ7kuKQQRoreDoFPRa66i6YFhQTkC4JJJTWtJKodynUgP13LSDpmPZ45Dy.png)

The final equation is the Correct Unified COP Equation

Once we have the total work performed by both partitioned loops in Joules, our corrected COP formula is as follows:

The Coefficient of Performance for Synthetic AC equals forward work plus backward work, divided by true input energy. 

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mes/23w3EdNWmqW74M1sa29qp87LKb26u7kBbYFq3dHqqgwP3ZPWe8MRP8a8cgkJFbba91Aa5.png)

By calculating the system this way, we respect the laws of calculus and standard thermodynamics while perfectly accounting for both energy vectors. This mathematical approach is unassailable by mainstream engineers simply because it relies on the absolute conservation of energy across individual partitioned events.

This equation is unassailable because Joules are a scalar metric of absolute work.

By integrating the instantaneous product of Voltage(V) and Current(I) at high sampling frequencies, we account for the Theta or phase angle dynamically at every microscopic point in time. Mainstream engineers cannot argue with this because it treats each temporal window as an isolated, standard thermodynamic event. It proves that if the sum of the work done in the partitioned paths exceeds the integrated input, the system must be open and extracting energy from an environmental or vacuum gradient. When we think about the Rodin coil for a minute, its not just one thing. Its not just a capacitor. It's not just an inductor. Its not just a transformer. This is the exact scientific distinction that makes the Rodin coils geometry so unique. Taxonomy is how we demystify the coil. Because It’s not one thing. It's an all in one system. When we view it as a single, unified component that combines inductance, capacitance, voltage transformation, and resonance, we are describing what advanced electromagnetic theory calls a Distributed Element Network or sometimes referred to as a Resonant Electromagnetic Structure. A singularity. A perfect representation of free flowing energy in the form of a localized and stable desktop black hole. A reactionless drive, unaffected by the weight that it carries. Black holes are thought to exist on the microscopic scale but instead of using gravity to suck everything in, they use a different force to suck in stray electrons and free ions. Apparently the same force the coil uses to do the same during field cavitation. The universe is a fractal of itself. It displays self similarities whether we look at the quantum scale or the cosmic scale. Everything is connected, if you know where to look for the patterns. This is the heart of Divine Science. The idea that the universe was intentionally created, and not just the byproduct of random chaos and nothingness. There is purpose everywhere in nature. 

---

# For Experimental Purposes

## Step 1: The Measurement Setup (Avoiding Ground Loops)

Because our system uses a high-speed diode to partition energy into different paths, a standard grounded oscilloscope probe can accidentally create a \

This will short out the very separation we are trying to measure.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mes/23tmjb2eaogQYkzua4meQtbWRaNQX4umKNEcD9rWRa5CYLFPJTEGwhvPr3TxszoigwzWX.png)

                  [ Modified Joule Thief ]
                            │
                    [High-Speed Diode]
                            │
                ┌───────────┴───────────┐
                ▼                       ▼
          Forward Path              Backward Path
       (To Resistor Load)        (To Battery Negative)
                │                       │
       [Current Probe A]       [Current Probe B]
       [Voltage Probe A]       [Voltage Probe B]

- **For Voltage (v(t)):** Use differential probes or your floating probe setup. Measure the voltage directly across the load for the **forward path**, and directly across the recovery terminal/battery negative for the **backward path**.
- **For Current (i(t)):** Use a high-bandwidth current probe (like a Tektronix, Lecroy, or a specialized high-frequency Rogowski coil/current viewing resistor). **Do not use standard multimeters.**

## Step 2: Capturing the Data on Your High-Speed Scope
Set your scope to its maximum sampling rate (e.g., 1GS/s or higher) to capture the sharp, high-dV/dt transients.

1. **Channel 1:** Forward Voltage (v<sub>forward</sub>(t))
2. **Channel 2:** Forward Current (i<sub>forward</sub>(t))
3. **Channel 3:** Backward Voltage (v<sub>backward</sub>(t))
4. **Channel 4:** Backward Current (i<sub>backward</sub>(t))

## Step 3: Performing the Math (The Joules Calculation)

Most modern high-speed digital oscilloscopes have a built-in Math Function that can handle this automatically. If yours does not, you can export the raw CSV data into Excel, MATLAB, or Python.

1. Calculate Instantaneous Power (P)

For every single data point on your screen, multiply the voltage by the current. This gives you a new waveform representing instantaneous power in Watts (W)

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mes/23wgoGrppohF4ASjHxhuRwXitvRsibAmKvnFXbNxQt19Aw2kFEkodVtp6n5TzeNFhHWxn.png)

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mes/23wgo9BoooMAW32pL7MT96vEYSUDGWrtqKuajK1YUuqxGtBQdB8yH4fWPrXWeqT62QdcY.png)

2. Integrate to Find Joules (W)

Use the scope’s built-in **\

(Intg)** math function on your new Power waveforms over one full cycle (T). Integration simply calculates the exact geometric area under that power curve. This gives you the energy in Joules:

- **W<sub>forward</sub>** = Integral of **P<sub>forward</sub>**
- **W<sub>backward</sub>** = Integral of **P<sub>backward</sub>**

*(Do the exact same thing for your input source to find U<sub>in</sub> in Joules.)*

---

## Step 4: The Final Bulletproof COP Calculation

Now that you have all three values converted into raw energy (Joules), you simply add the two output components together and divide by the input:

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mes/23w3EVhVkon1LrwBFyitZXx95EjgrdouRNqa6SvtZcs7CZ8BS9nBQriiya6uDRQMwFHEw.png)

Because you converted the non-linear, asymmetric waveforms into absolute units of energy (Joules) before adding them, this calculation is mathematically unassailable. No one can claim you are inflating your numbers with \

RMS additions.

If your open system is truly drawing ambient energy via your geometric cavitation field bridge, your final COP number will cleanly land above 1.0, proving your thesis empirically.

links.body: > ¡Hola amigos de Hive Food! Les deseo estén teniendo un bello sábado y que Dios los bendiga abundantemente. Una vez más paso por acá para compartirles una deliciosa receta. El plato de hoy aunque es sencillo está lleno de sabor y es un menú que se puede encontrar en muchas casas cubanas hoy en día. En mi caso particular es uno de mis comidas preferidas: arroz amarillo con picadillo y ensalada de calabaza.

> > *Hello, Hive Food friends! I hope you’re having a wonderful Saturday, and may God bless you abundantly. I’m stopping by once again to share a delicious recipe with you. Today’s dish, though simple, is full of flavor and is a meal you can find in many Cuban homes today. For me personally, it’s one of my favorite meals: yellow rice with picadillo and squash salad.*
![1779489874058.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/AKFA57W7qJjgq4QSpSJ5ByjxUAwqoKBBCS37aXUcax8jmqvqJpNFMVYmLPYhYUE.jpg)

> # Ingredientes: 2 libras de picadillo de pollo 2 tazas de arroz 2 libras de calabaza 3 cucharadas de caldo concentrado de pollo natural 1 cebolla pequeña 2 cabezas de ajo 2 cucharadas de vinagre 4 cucharadas de vino seco 2 cucharadas de pasta de tomate 1 chopo grande Orégano y Albahaca al gusto Sal al gusto

> # Ingredients: > *2 pounds of ground chicken 2 cups of rice 2 pounds of squash 3 tablespoons of natural chicken bouillon concentrate 1 small onion 2 heads of garlic 2 tablespoons of vinegar 4 tablespoons of dry wine 2 tablespoons of tomato paste 1 large chili pepper Oregano and basil to taste Salt to taste*
![IMG_20260522_181303.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/Eokf1NcFJWGvjKUFixZ7wUQW7iRpUYvfA7XuUCta4zdzwBvjkx4DYoeqgmqG62JtVpw.jpg) ![IMG_20260522_181434.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/23xALzrk35BTWUsPvK8Ed3pBKCAQiBRfTRFmSUPZ6KH2UZtADpcwu6fCMEdQpXtFX3y3t.jpg)

> # Paso a paso ## Paso 1 Comencé sazonando el picadillo. Le eché una cucharada de vinagre, dos cucharadas de vino seco, orégano, albahaca, sal al gusto. Y bastante ajo, tomé una cabeza de ajo aproximadamente, pues era mucho picadillo. Para incorporar el ajo me gusta primero machacarlo, picarlo finamente, agregarle aceite y sal. Hago mi propia pasta de ajo, así aprovecho más el sabor del ajo. Es de mis condimentos favoritos.

> # Step by Step ## Step 1 > *I started by seasoning the ground beef. I added a tablespoon of vinegar, two tablespoons of dry wine, oregano, basil, and salt to taste. And plenty of garlic—I used about a head of garlic, since there was a lot of ground beef. To incorporate the garlic, I like to first crush it, chop it finely, and then add oil and salt. I make my own garlic paste that way, so I get more flavor from the garlic. It’s one of my favorite seasonings.*
![IMG_20260522_152120.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/EoptvsuwattV3ftShdnJfC8RNci77VD8QiCNyEavFndt53zYKUDghTRPP4Wut9qAsJi.jpg) ![IMG_20260522_181554.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/23xejfYBHnQYmqM9M4XhafYDaUMya49ar3DY837u6bdarknQ7LxMBRLvk4qxFxxeYcHEw.jpg)

> ## Paso 2 Mientras dejo el picadillo absorbiendo todos estos sabores voy preparando mi arroz. Lo salteo primero y luego le incorporo el agua con dos cucharas de vino seco, una de vinagre, una de pasta de tomate para ayudar a dar color y el caldo concentrado de pollo natural que tenía guardado de una receta anterior en mi nevera. También le eché una hoja de orégano picada bien pequeño y sal al gusto. ## Step 2 > *While I let the ground meat absorb all these flavors, I prepare my rice. I sauté it first, then add water along with two tablespoons of dry wine, one of vinegar, one of tomato paste to help add color, and the natural chicken bouillon concentrate I had saved from a previous recipe in my fridge. I also added a finely chopped oregano leaf and salt to taste.*
![IMG_20260522_154451.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/23zbTpLMR9pi88JUJrnexEUph6QhBf3YAk2aaanVR5iPmGiWYQ4AVRd8kW1PSsbWWEH36.jpg) ![IMG_20260522_155722.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/23zS3TBpb8TEZG2aP1cJijqg6NiLKka8zazsf9UWXPHnyKasoLBD2SaxLtUVfCS6WS5cb.jpg)

> ## Paso 3 Pasados 30 minutos aproximadamente ya comencé a cocinar mi picadillo. Le agregué una cucharada de pasta de tomate diluida en agua para hacer una salsa y lo estuve revolviendo hasta que estuvo listo.

> ## Step 3 > *After about 30 minutes, I started cooking my picadillo. I added a tablespoon of tomato paste diluted in water to make a sauce and stirred it until it was ready.*
![IMG_20260522_183045.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/242DYwN4vo68XcFQqcfbwyamhNPiZFWFKxJikNWPksNqGYwKyXktzmfecZGjSP48gC8AN.jpg) ![IMG_20260522_183113.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/23wX3o2qGK3ay6x1XGQf7JjnXVVrDfCpcmoSSApcKja2FvvXnBYV9drmJpWTd1p2ca7Ch.jpg)

> ## Paso 4 Tomé un pedazo grande de calabaza. Este pesaba 2 libras. Lo lavé bien, le quité las semillas y lo corté en pedazos del mismo tamaño. Lo puse a hervir con sal. Una vez que se ablandaron, escurrí el agua de la cocción y reservé la calabaza por un momento.

> ## Step 4 > *I took a large piece of squash. It weighed 2 pounds. I washed it thoroughly, removed the seeds, and cut it into evenly sized pieces. I boiled it with salt. Once it softened, I drained the cooking water and set the squash aside for a moment.*
![IMG_20260522_181701.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/23xpHMvqE2npAdRUJ2QneUv6kbivbcY6qx3GGLZpkqwDM64JuVMpEc62mc3DHZjCism7Q.jpg) ![IMG_20260522_181722.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/23ywqEoh4rcvNmJCDwdcj2jZ4VzTRWieiQp6pqRWjVYM7HkUbSm2VLqL7HhD1E22ZGSTS.jpg)

> ## Paso 5 Mientras tanto preparé el sofrito que le va a dar el sabor a la ensalada de calabaza. Usé aceite, sal al gusto y una cabeza de ajo. Los dejé sofreír con la llama media baja. ## Paso 6 Una vez listo el sofrito, incorporar la calabaza y revolver bien. Rectificar la sal si es necesario.

>
## Step 5 > *Meanwhile, I prepared the sofrito that will give the squash salad its flavor. I used oil, salt to taste, and a head of garlic. I let them sauté over medium-low heat.* ## Step 6 > *Once the sofrito is ready, add the squash and stir well. Adjust the salt if necessary.*
![IMG_20260522_181839.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/23wqrxNQTpY8mka7asZSJxvMi7ap593UTbxsNinHmpA49MDfwqMfNyjRnqpEp4VinuWPS.jpg) ![IMG_20260522_175926.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/23y8qerWr8TcQ21rDf48mfrvq5Des3w9NN4QGmNZHEdHqV45SjFPpK6Fx7xND6k3tgSEh.jpg)

> # Resultado final Así como pueden ver, quedó este menú típico cubano. Al picadillo también le adicioné un chopo que había hervido previamente. Aromas muy parecidos encontramos a diario en muchas casas de nuestra bella tierra. Espero que les haya gustado. Quisiera que me comentaran si conocen otra forma de preparar el picadillo. Saludos a todos, gracias por acompañarme.

> # Final Result > *As you can see, this is a typical Cuban dish. I also added a chili pepper that I had previously boiled to the ground meat. We encounter very similar aromas every day in many homes across our beautiful country. I hope you enjoyed it. I’d love to hear from you if you know of any other ways to prepare picadillo. Best wishes to all, and thank you for joining me.*
![IMG_20260522_182011.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/23xyg82HqD5RLSs1Z37G2cf3w9E3gUrLT6mfQRTXhX53yqUVWYugNY3p1PKreFjuPKSGV.jpg) ![pBMyo3B2Sao45kGEB1kRY9cJBFGQnrPp2qChGHkgVjzu1y6XFCd4yc3Lhq94o3dSStPa8WzfMTj3rehMXJs9ag6aTxoMP9hvAkcL9yjqJobqtCbse2vBnvAj6cPpVBBpcpW45G9MQ7QodcnjUz7Pn9AFEeRBr9Ueg9Rspxc4SaKBbSzA.webp](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lagoticaderocio/23xyhk8Q4sH9mqwAKQ6Jg4CNJp6j6tB2C9KoBfRVzxJ4cR2DEbvaBnYmGKcXtRsZ7mv13.webp)

links.title: Phillies lose to Guardians in brutal fashion as Cristopher Sánchez and Gavin Williams have amazing pitcher's duel | Zack Wheeler on the mound today
links.body:
![mlb-Philadelphia-Phillies-Logo.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/adhammer/AJhXiRGysGbqrUVr31VqR8j9iJthXQeNsJRnjA5UgF2TrkK4JXLPjHUG9MUr24D.png)
[Src](https://loodibee.com/mlb/philadelphia-phillies/)

Cristopher Sánchez is THE man! My goodness. Even though the Phillies lost in pretty depressing fashion, I'm surprisingly excited by what happened yesterday from a different perspective. 

Cristopher Sánchez is totally locked in right now. He's firmly in the Cy Young discussion and not just as an honorable mention, he's a legit contender!

Sánchez tossed an absolute gem against the Guardians yesterday, by pitching eight scoreless innings! The only unfortunate part about it had nothing to do with him, but with the Phillies offense and Guardians pitcher Gavin Williams. Williams totally matched Sánchez  on the mound by tossing eight scoreless innings himself! Unreal! Pitcher's duels aren't all that uncommon but, this duel really felt like a genuine 1 vs 1 duel! Too cool, they really were the main characters yesterday LOL. The brutal part was the fact that Phillies closer Jhoan Durán, who's normally good, gave up a solo homer in the top of the ninth. The Phillies couldn't respond and that was the game. 1-0 loss, rough. One team had to lose!

BUT, back to Cristopher Sánchez. Sánchez's excellent performance is bigger than just one single good night of pitching. After his eight scoreless innings yesterday he surpassed Cliff Lee for second most consecutive scoreless innings pitched in franchise hostory! Lee had 34 straight in 2011, and now Sánchez sits at 37 2/3! The all time Phillies record is 41 innings set by Grover Cleveland in **1911!!!** We're talking before any World War people! He's so close!

If Sánchez breaks that record, it would be mind-blowing. It is fascinating on a lot of levels. Grover Cleveland was born in 1887 and Cristopher Sánchez was born in 1996! The MLB record is 59 set by Orel Hershiser in 1988. 

So despite the loss, history could be in the making!

Zack Wheeler is on the mound today, let's hope he's as sharp as ever and the Phillies offense wakes up! The Phillies have now dipped under .500 once again and have lost three straight.

It's been a strange season, but if the Phillies are to be great, maybe Sánchez and Wheeler will lead the way and be the anchors of this team! Ya never know!

links.title: 🌸✨ Sketchbook Hive ✨🌸Drawing My Mom With Art and Heart 💖✏️/🌸✨ Sketchbook Hive ✨🌸 Dibujando a mi mamá con arte y con arte y corazón 💖✏️
links.body: > 🌸✨ **ENGLISH VERSION** ======================= **Sketchbook Hive** ✨🌸🎨 **A Pencil Caricature Full of Love | Drawing My Mom With Art and Heart 💖✏️** ======================================================================================================= Hello beautiful Sketchbook community! 🥰🎨✨ Today I want to share a very special drawing that I created with lots of love and dedication ❤️. This time, I made a **pencil caricature portrait inspired by a photo of my mother** 👩🏽‍🦱💖, someone who has always been a symbol of strength, love, wisdom, and unconditional support in my life 🌷✨. From the moment I started sketching, my goal was not only to replicate her facial features but also to capture her warmth, kindness, and beautiful essence through expressive lines and stylized forms 🖊️💫.

> 💖✨ **My inspiration behind this artwork** ✨💖 I wanted to create something meaningful for someone who deserves all my admiration. My mom has always inspired me with her smile 😊, patience, and beautiful spirit 🌸. Art became my way of honoring her and turning emotions into something visual and memorable 🎭❤️. ### ✏️ **Professional Artistic Process** 🎨 For this caricature, I worked using traditional pencil techniques while combining realism with stylized exaggeration, a very important element in caricature illustration 📝✨. 🔹 **Facial Construction & Proportions** I carefully studied the facial proportions and emphasized expressive areas such as the eyes 👀 and smile 😊 to create personality while maintaining recognizable features. 🔹 **Line Work & Contours** I used soft contour lines mixed with darker strokes to define the structure of the face and clothing. This helped create visual balance and better silhouette readability ✍️🎭. 🔹 **Cross-Hatching & Shading** To give depth and volume, I applied **cross-hatching techniques** and controlled graphite shading in areas like the neck, clothing, and facial contours 🖤✨. This allowed the portrait to gain dimension and visual contrast. 🔹 **Stylized Caricature Design** Rather than going for hyperrealism, I focused on stylization by slightly exaggerating expressions and proportions while preserving her sweetness and identity 💕🎨. And honestly… seeing her smile while drawing her made this artwork even more special 🥹💖. 🌸 Mom, if you ever read this: thank you for your love, for your sacrifices, and for always being my inspiration. Your smile lights up everything around you 💕✨. To me, you will always be one of the most beautiful people in the world 🌎💖. Thank you so much for visiting my post and supporting my art journey! 🙏🎨✨ I hope you like this little tribute made with pencil, patience, and lots of love ❤️✏️ 💬 Tell me what you think! I’d love to read your comments 🥰✨ If you want a cartoon tell me in the comments * * *

> 🌸✨ **VERSIÓN EN ESPAÑOL** ========================== **Sketchbook Hive** ✨🌸🎨 **Una caricatura a lápiz llena de amor | Dibujando a mi mamá con arte y corazón 💖✏️** ================================================================================================================ ¡Hola hermosa comunidad de Sketchbook! 🥰🎨✨ Hoy quiero compartir con ustedes un dibujo muy especial que hice con muchísimo cariño ❤️. En esta ocasión realicé una **caricatura a lápiz basada en una foto de mi mamá** 👩🏽‍🦱💖, una persona que representa amor, fortaleza, ternura y apoyo incondicional en mi vida 🌷✨. Desde el primer trazo mi intención no fue solamente copiar sus rasgos, sino también transmitir su esencia, su dulzura y esa sonrisa tan bonita que siempre ilumina todo 😊💫.

></center>

💖✨ **La inspiración detrás de este dibujo** ✨💖  
Quise crear algo especial para alguien que merece toda mi admiración. Mi mamá siempre ha sido una inspiración para mí 🌸💞. Su sonrisa, su paciencia y su forma de enfrentar la vida me motivaron a convertir una simple fotografía en un retrato artístico lleno de emoción 🎭❤️.

### ✏️ **Proceso artístico profesional** 🎨

Para esta caricatura trabajé utilizando técnicas tradicionales de lápiz, mezclando elementos del retrato con un estilo caricaturesco estilizado 📝✨.

🔹 **Construcción facial y proporciones**  
Analicé cuidadosamente las proporciones del rostro y decidí enfatizar áreas expresivas como los ojos 👀 y la sonrisa 😊, buscando mantener su identidad mientras añadía personalidad artística.

🔹 **Trabajo de línea y contornos**  
Utilicé líneas suaves junto a trazos más oscuros para reforzar contornos, estructura facial y vestimenta ✍️🎭, creando un mejor equilibrio visual.

🔹 **Sombras y tramado (Cross-Hatching)**  
Apliqué técnicas de sombreado con grafito y **tramado cruzado (cross-hatching)** especialmente en el cuello, ropa y algunas zonas del rostro para aportar profundidad, volumen y contraste 🖤✨.

🔹 **Diseño caricaturesco estilizado**  
En lugar de enfocarme únicamente en el realismo, opté por un estilo caricaturesco donde exageré ligeramente ciertas expresiones y proporciones manteniendo su esencia y belleza 💕🎨.

Y sinceramente… mientras dibujaba su sonrisa, sentía que este retrato se volvía todavía más especial 🥹💖.

🌸 Mamá, si lees esto algún día: gracias por tu amor, por tus sacrificios y por siempre inspirarme 💕✨. Tu sonrisa ilumina cualquier lugar y para mí siempre serás una de las personas más hermosas del mundo 🌎💖.

Muchas gracias por visitar mi publicación y apoyar mi arte 🙏🎨✨  
Espero que les guste este pequeño homenaje hecho con lápiz, paciencia y muchísimo amor ❤️✏️

💬 ¡Cuéntenme qué les parece! Me encantará leer sus comentarios 🥰✨Si quieres una caricatura me dices en los comentarios

links.title: The Bowl, The Newspaper, The Art? :)
links.body:
##### Happy Saturday! It's the Memorial Day weekend here where next Monday will be a holiday from work for me.  I decided to take advantage and took yesterday off too for a 4 day weekend. Of course you would know that it has finally decided to rain a bit, so all of yesterday and today so far has been cloudy and dreary looking. It isn't ruining my joy about not working and still being paid...LOL... but I AM solar powered, so....

##### .... So... what nonsense will I share today?

##### One morning I woke up 15 minutes too early compared to the time I normally get up on work days.  On a whim, I went to my art desk, opened my play journal, grabbed my crayons and did this fast ... art? ha ha... I was definitely channeling my inner child, but it was fun and the curly que on the rooftop made me smile then and several times sense.  When art is your serious hobby, the \

is what feeds the soul.  If something good ever shows up in the end product, that is icing on the cake!


![fast coloring.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jacey.boldart/23u6B87VWzdcYWJEm2opYUwJPfScg1Y5N2GqbPUU4mcsNhnrRuk58AtRRVgkHBJwgrzwB.jpg)

##### The bowl.

##### This bowl is really stark white in color, but I took this photo this morning at my stove and the lighting made it look a bit yellow, but it really isn't.  It is a vintage Corningware bowl. They are the most versatile bowls and are perfect for using in the microwave with their little tab handles.  I've had one for a long time, although I can't really remember how or exactly when I acquired it, but I could use it every day if I would only wash it after I used it, which I normally didn't. 

##### Sometime since the first of this year, I was in the Goodwill thrift shop.  I normally look through their small book section, then wander up and down the Home Goods isles.  That day, I saw one of these treasured bowls and I quickly grabbed it up and looked around as if expecting someone else to try to fight me for it. 🤣 .... but no one did.  A couple of steps later, lo and behold, there was another!  Good Gracious!  It was a treasure finding day! 

##### The next time I was there, I found two more had showed up, only the second ones were a tiny bit larger. I didn't know there had been two sizes so similar, but you know already I snatched them up too as who knows if I would ever see them in the wild again.

##### Fast forward to a bit over a month ago. I showed up at my Mom's on Sunday and as we prepared things in the kitchen to get our lunch ready, she told me sadly that she had broken her favorite bowl. I asked her what kind of bowl her favorite bowl was and.... you guessed it again, it was this very same bowl.  I told her I had a few and I would share with her, so I took one of my treasured bowls to her the next Sunday I was there.  It was quite the sacrifice as I am sure you can tell, but .... she's my Mother, how could I not??? 

##### About 2 weeks later, as once again on a Sunday afternoon, we were preparing again for our lunch meal, she look at me guiltily and said, I broke my bowl again. (Really God, you jest!) I asked her how she broke it and she said she thought she broke it the same way as the first one. Like is common here, there is a double sink in her kitchen where she uses the sink on the right to wash dishes and the sink on the left to rinse.  The rinse sink has long had a rubbery mat in the bottom that has holes for drainage, but she had taken it up to scrub over and under and around and had not put it back for no good reason.  It turns out she had washed each bowl, went to rinse them and being wet, each time the bowl had slipped from her hand and since there was no rubber mat thee for cushion, each one had hit the porcelain sink on their handles and had broken! 

##### Sheesh! How could she do that to me??? LOL... because you know, I could not NOT offer her another? ... and so you can see that the next week, there went one more of my treasured bowls. I guess sometimes the universe gives you something you think is for you, but it's really for someone else. 

![20260523_113535_HDR.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jacey.boldart/23vsUg9qiDb4wjZ6kdHJhKzYRewrPkbTs5sjJ8ZGZbPy4m5kkXCohjWoFEd8bySmDpknV.jpg)

##### Last week I went on ebay to see if by chance there was any there.... (before she breaks another!)..... and there were many there, however, the sellers all know that these are highly sought after and the prices were horrendous! I looked through many posts to try to find the lesser of the evils pricewise.  On the one I chose, the price was still not good, but not as bad as the others per piece and the seller had an option to \

, so I did for about 25% less than what they were asking.  That would at least save me the amount of the shipping that it was going to cost.  I really didn't think the seller would accept it (never stops me from trying), but pretty fast, they DID accept it and so, six more bowls were on the way. 

##### I really liked it better when I had acquired some for practically nothing at the thrift shop, but I figured my chances of that happening again were not too good.  Anyway, they came this week.  I haven't told Mom and I'm not giving them all to her, but I will take her two more to go with the last one I gave her and I will put a couple in my kitchen and store the rest for when.... well... just in case. LOL!

![s-l1600.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jacey.boldart/23wqs63d78vyki6F4SdXQi4Wtv6Dz6BVCT5i6ibeVXfPPTiiQWje3UPnNpQZtL7FqEysz.jpg)

##### All of that leads me to the next thing.  When the bowls came this week, the box they were in was very padded to keep them safe and part of the packing was a newspaper from the town they were sent from. I haven't had an actual newspaper in my hands in years.  They were always around when I was growing up as the were delivered mostly by young boys on bikes that had large baskets on the front and the boys would ride by your house and throw a rolled up paper on or at your porch.... 7 days a week. (providing you had a paid subscription of course)

##### Eventually that no longer happened and adults in cars delivered and then....it slowed to where not that many people got daily papers as the world changed. Now there is no local newspaper persay.  Most newspaper offices died.  A few were taken over by companies that were not local and some form of paper was still available, but mostly not.

##### The seller had balled up the pages of the paper and used them for packing. As I smoothed out each one to fold compactly so it would take up less space in my kitchen trash can, I stopped and looked at the pages. Oh!... what memories they brought back. They were a little more narrow than the ones of my day, but other than that, they were the same.


![np 1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jacey.boldart/23zbXwx7Bs9UXXGwjhYgzadj2YAv5kp2BHuKgM7akrnLJ8S6Ka7iopmntuWYZ2FXXoEjG.jpg)
##### I had already smoothed a couple of pages out without paying attention to them when I got to this one and there were the comics and the crossword.... just like the old days and I had to stop for a minute.
![np 2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jacey.boldart/23wgU12cz69ThXeDDhBDmF5MwDwtw3h6kPYueqgDfbk2CrfwQPRMKxFQqfXsEg3q1SJT2.jpg)
##### There too at the bottom was the Dear Abby column.  I didn't realize that still existed.  True to form, you never knew what the subject was going to be. Anyway, this random packing took me down memory lane for a few moments.  I kept the page with the comics (which we used call the \

)... and Dear Abby thinking maybe some pieces of them might land in a collage at sometime in the future.  

##### It was a fun little mental detour.


![NP 3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jacey.boldart/EopuJWrSiv9BubAWfCAmxCDCiQedAm9g4mBukYsyMy5eaxwtkbCPS6vsYdoYCR2juuy.jpg)

##### Ok... one more little thing I just started last night.  I watch a lot of art videos on YT when I can find some I haven't already watched.  I get random ideas, sometimes just a snippet of something I might like to use myself. 

##### I did not see this idea recently, but in the past and even when I saw it, it really didn't hit me that I would ever use it.


##### One of the creators, Jackie Bernardi showed how she had taken an old cookbook and turned it into a play journal for her painting and mixed media/collage.  Fun thing is it was medium large, so she had a lot of space to play. I thought it was a neat idea for her to do and enjoyed watching her play in it.

##### Fast forward to more recently.  My Mom is trying to clean things out slowly from her house.  She has lived there more than 45 years, half her life and things have accumulated as they always do.  Since she is older and having more health issues, although she is not doing it frantically, she is spending time going through things, throwing out lots and offering other things to anyone that might use it.  She is not giving away her good stuff that she uses, but stuff she has no use for and that she knows when she is gone, someone else will have to go through.  

##### With the internet and the such, most folks are not keeping loads of cookbooks like good cooks used to do. Back in the day, it was a real prize to be given, buy or find a really good cookbook.  I can't tell how many hours I have gone through  cookbooks in my life or how many new recipes I have tried.  Such fun! So... in the cleaning out, she comes across a few books here and there.  She has offered some to me and I take some once in a while if I am interested in them, but if I know I won't read them or use them, I tell her to offer them to everyone else and if no one takes them and she is going to throw them out, I will take them to use in my collage, but know, that means I would be tearing them up!  So.. that's the way it goes.

##### Recently she had a few books and a couple were cookbooks.  I love the Southern Living books. I have never tried a recipe out of them that was not good.  I don't know what they do now, but they used to have a monthly magazine subscription you could get and at the end of each year, they would put out one of these Annual Recipes books that included all the recipes for that year. For a number of years, one of my Aunts would give Mom the annual recipe book so Mom has had a lot over time. Now though... time to go!





![20260523_113247_HDR.jpgbook.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jacey.boldart/23vi49kgd5xypuRMwWPmbXhjQwmgBaSebLJWo1zMxAnLJa1nkaoCJxoZvgpUvK3xhqJkq.jpg)

##### The recent pile of books she gave me had this year 2000 version.  I thought it looked familiar.  I've had them here a couple of weeks still in the bag I brought them home in and yesterday I went through them again to see what was there.  Somewhere in the mix, I began to think about how Jackie had used an old cookbook as an art play journal and I wondered if maybe I might like to do the same. It's free afterall and ... why not?  I checked last night and indeed, this looked familiar because I already have a copy in my cookbook collection (yes, I still have books, probably 2 dozen or more).  That helped me make the decision to use this one to see how I liked it.


![sl inside.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jacey.boldart/Ep3fL2SZfHkWsg9Ekybem3JtEZW7M33KLJ2DUGWGms6mENHTrDYKfh2uDxS6JbJd5qH.jpg)

##### Last night I decided to try it and see how it worked.  Since the pages are semi-glossy, I put a layer of white gesso on first. It is a common primer that many painters and mixed media artists use to seal pages or wooden canvases or the such to make sure whatever they paint or glue there sticks!

##### Then I just played with some paint colors I like  and the paint went on perfectly. I believe this will be fun and if ever I come up with some neat combination or good idea of a sorts, I can then use the idea on a real canvas.  

##### Journaling for art is not a new idea at all, but most folks, including me buy books made for journaling, a lot of which are not cheap as they have good paper for art inside them. I haven't bought but a couple myself, but when they are full, they have neat stuff and bad stuff in them and to me are no longer good for anything but making a stack.  The first journal book I ever filled up, I eventually went through and any pages I liked I tore out and put in ANOTHER book (LOL)....and the rest I threw away. 

##### I'm glad that cookbook journal idea stayed stored away in my brain, because although it never crossed my mind as something for ME to do....here I am!


![page 1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jacey.boldart/23wMjFDsWsuCD97WtdmFxkCX7efWGcysSiba7A3CxVVm7oR3PZofvyBgoVW98yijg2EnQ.jpg)


##### I will leave you with this since I have jabbered for a good while now.  The other night I was creating collage papers on my gel print plate or gelli plate.... and after I poured the yellow paint on top of the ghost of the lavender design behind it, I noticed it was smiling back at me, so I took this photo. You never know who/what will show up when you sling a little paint around.


![face on gel.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jacey.boldart/23yJLTxh2b2xHi2tV936LZJGKFG2NFX7RxCvhaGCeS9MAyvs9ofW7yxBk9aEquCBEa7nx.jpg)

##### Hope you all have been doing well and that your hearts are happy.

##### Love you!
##### Jacey




![bonus.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jacey.boldart/Ep1XMrTiTRVs7aqDPjMYqj1TZKPiznoVQiWebpRyPCiEKqEwjRvkSUcm7mCwXuJauxu.jpg)

links.body:
![image](https://pixabay.com/get/gf599af5cf9727d6b48ae259dd360541a0ddc5d0254b61d7bf72f4268e282483c29c1b3c95d71d0cfcd75eaa6ff749c6d6b2c503a193d90c65137ad397418908d_640.jpg)
My last walk was along the stunning South West Coast Path, taking in a section near Tintagel in Cornwall. The rugged cliffs and the crashing waves of the Atlantic were absolutely breathtaking. As I walked, I was struck by the dramatic landscape – the cliffs towering above me, dotted with wildflowers in full bloom. One of the highlights of the walk was arriving at Tintagel Castle, famously linked to the legend of King Arthur. The ruins perched on the cliffs had a mysterious and enchanting aura about them. I could almost feel the weight of history in the air. The views from the castle are nothing short of spectacular; you can see the coastline stretch for miles, and I spent some time just taking it all in. Along the path, I met a few fellow walkers. There was an elderly couple who were regulars on the trail and shared stories of their adventures over the years. They told me about the various wildlife they had encountered and pointed out some interesting rock formations along the way. I also chatted with a young artist who was sketching the landscape. She aimed to capture the essence of Tintagel. It was lovely to hear her passion for her craft, and I think she was genuinely inspired by the place. As I made my way back, I took a moment to reflect on the rich history of Cornwall, from its legends to its maritime heritage. The sun began to set, casting a golden glow over the sea, making the whole experience feel even more magical. Overall, it was a wonderful day filled with natural beauty, fascinating stories, and the warmth of fellow travellers. I can't wait for my next walking adventure! _This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). Check out the original version [here on actifit.io](https://actifit.io/@titusfrost/actifit-titusfrost-20231229t015511428z)_

links.title: Strategic Transitions - Decision making in this new AI era
links.body:
Many companies currently struggle to make decisions and invest in the right AI path. Some companies even invest in unnecessary things and end up spending money that ultimately goes to waste. There is also one more thing here where AI is also changing rapidly, and in the last few months, there have been so many drastic changes in AI. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNjBm1Qh83Bb5tSBYeLZZUhwK47kdgEVPGRcuRsyHUhuN/image.png)



They say the donkey example for this scenario is that if there are two attractive things kept on the left side and right side of a donkey, the donkey struggles to decide which route to take and ends up starving to death. This should not be the scenario either. Decision making is powerful, and we have to do it at the right moment know to some extent how the market is moving and based on the demand and supply. 

Solving the problem should be the best way to think when it comes to strategic transitioning. In the new era of AI, decision-making can be a little challenging. We might think of something, but the world is going very fast, and our thought process ends up becoming outdated. In such cases, we can probably keep going with the flow and stay up to date and be careful as well. Sometimes the performance of the company might be at its peak, and at that time, there is no harm in trying something new that is good for the organization. But when the performance of the company is very poor, and if we continue to experiment with things, it will be good if the new experiment becomes a success, but if it fails, it can impact the business to a greater extent. 

Investing in new technology should happen when the business is going great and if we have room for experimentation. If we do it at the wrong time, the performance can be lower than what the company is already delivering.

**_Rest & Quality Time with Mom_** 🍦💕

Today is my rest day, and who better to spend it with than my amazing mom? 💖 We’re having a girls’ outing—just the two of us—to enjoy some creamy ice cream and great conversation. 🍧👩‍👧 I love these moments because my mom is my rock, my biggest supporter, and my eternal source of strength. 🌷🙏

Sharing simple joys like this fills my heart with gratitude. Every laugh, every hug, every “just because” treat with her is a treasure. 🍨✨

**_“Mom, your love is my favorite flavor of happiness—sweet, comforting, and always present.”_** 🥰

Sending blessings to all of you! May you also find time to rest and cherish the people who lift your soul. 💫🌹

* * *

**_Descanso y Tiempo con Mami_** 🍦💕

Hoy me toca descansar, ¿y a quién mejor invitar que a mi mami? 💖 Vamos a tener una salida de chicas—solo las dos—para comer un rico helado y charlar de la vida. 🍧👩‍👧 Me encanta compartir con ella porque es mi fuerza de apoyo siempre, mi roca y mi mayor inspiración. 🌷🙏

Disfrutar de estos momentos sencillos llena mi corazón de gratitud. Cada risa, cada abrazo, cada helado “solo porque sí” con ella es un tesoro. 🍨✨

**_“Mami, tu amor es el sabor favorito de mi felicidad: dulce, reconfortante y siempre presente.”_** 🥰

¡Les mando bendiciones a todos! Que también encuentren tiempo para descansar y valorar a quienes les levantan el alma. 💫🌹

links.title: A Phone Booth While Running Away – A Silver Bloggers Chronicle
links.body:
![goldenhills (1280 x 40 px) (1280 x 80 px) (1280 x 780 px) (1280 x 780 px).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cliffagreen/23yJT4H4WHj3iBsaCjyyD6Wm6vCiGaoNsTQvMcnGdpDvD3jczfq5NL9kjN6oR4bMJzkkd.png)


The first time I used a phone booth I was running away.

It would have been August 1990. I was 14 years old. Our church, [Faith Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Assembly_Church_of_Wilmot,_Indiana) (the Wikipedia link above includes old reporting about the faith healing cult in the cornfields of northern Indiana in the '70s, '80s, and '90s), held a one-day youth retreat at the church in Wilmot, literally on the edge of cornfield, about 18 miles from home in Millersburg.

I'm not sure what triggered my jail break that day. Youth group went well. We had the usual snacks and fellowship, games and skits, testimonies and worship. Maybe that was part of it: when I first was allowed to go to youth group at 13, all of that was new and exciting, but a year later it was the same old routine.

I remember having a sense of melancholy, even depression, a sense that something was wrong. And there was abuse happening beneath the surface of our perfect little family, but at the time those memories were repressed (and they remained so until I was 26): certainly there wasn't anything I was consciously trying to get away from. I just had a vague sense that I should go.

So I was bored and blue as the day drew to a close and we were singing the final worship songs to wrap it all up. I don't think I had any sort of plan when I ducked out of the row of folding metal chairs and left my friends singing. I think I probably only intended to go to the bathroom, but when I got to the back the sun was shining brilliantly through the door windows, and I had to get out into it.

Once I hit the gravel parking lot (and the weighted heat and humidity of Indiana August sun) I just started walking, and one thing led to another: my sense of exploration and adventure took over. First I walked along the curves on the country road that led to the church, curves that I knew intimately, like the back of my hand, from riding in the family car on the way to church since before I was old enough to look out the window. It was exciting to experience those curves at a slow walking pace, to feel the gravel on the berm and the blacktop under my soles.

When I reached the state highway, after about a mile, I was well into my adventure, and ready for something that was completely new. We only drove on that highway for about a half mile going to and from church; at our usual turnoff I went straight, just because I wanted to see what was down the road. Before long I came up on a green highway sign announcing the distance to the town of Larwill. (I had to get pretty close to the sign to read it; I'm nearsighted, and remember, this is a faith healing church we went to; we didn't believe in going to doctors for things like prescription glasses.)

Larwill is where my friend and crush Robin lived. Robin was one of the friends I left behind at the youth retreat, but still I thought it would be fun to drop in on her at home. By the time I walked there, they would be back from youth retreat.

First I had to get off the state highway though. I was worried that people coming to get their kids at church would see me, so I cut off onto some back country roads, the kind of roads I was familiar with, because that's the kind of road I lived on. What I didn't consider is that all those familiar farmhouses I was walking by had dogs. I only got chased once: a couple chows came tearing off a front porch, hair all bristled, and ran me down to the next farmhouse. I don't know how far they actually chased me; I was at a dead run until I leaped onto the next porch I found, hollering at the lady sitting there that I was getting chased. She gave me a patronizing smile and went in the house (I'm not sure what she was going to do), and when I looked around the dogs were nowhere to be seen, so I headed back to the road.

Was I serious about running away? Or was I just out having an adventure? I suspect getting run by those dogs tilted the scales toward just having an adventure, visiting Robin and then going back home.

In Etna, a tiny town that was mostly just a trailer park, I found a payphone next to a country store, or maybe it was the trailer park's office. It was on the edge of a gravel lot, with knee high weeds grown up around it. I called the operator to get Robin's number (I knew her dad's name from church), then dropped quarters to call her. When her mom answered, I had my first brush with notoriety: apparently everyone at church was out looking for me. She exclaimed, “You're Cliff Green?!” when I told her who was calling, and I could hear her hovering while Robin and I talked. Robin's parents agreed readily to let me come there.

I thumbed a couple rides on my journey. The first was with two guys in a pickup truck. They let me ride in the back for about a quarter mile around a jog in the road. Not much of a ride, I remember thinking, but they pointed me in the direction of Larwill, which was helpful. For the last leg of my journey, I got picked up by a photographer who was out photographing the countryside (a synchronicity in the sweep of my life, given that 36 years later I'm a photographer who rambles around photographing nature). The photographer took me all the way into Larwill, another tiny hamlet of a town, where we met Robin and her older sister walking up main street, expecting to meet me walking into town.  

Surprised to see me climbing out of a stranger's vehicle, Robin told me that the photographer was my guardian angel looking out for me. These days I can just as easily believe he was a version of my future self, from a slightly different timeline, helping me reach my destination.

All in all I traveled about 10 miles that afternoon (it sure felt like longer!), 28 miles away from home. I would run away two more times in the next year and half or so, each one more seriously about running away than that first trip. Finally, I used my escapades as a bargaining chip to convince my parents to send me to public school when I was 16 (I was homeschooled between second and tenth grades), and I think having somewhere else to go five days a week relieved the pressure of the things going on beneath the surface at home.

I ended up living on the family farm, off and on, until I was 25!

***
***

![2r8F9rTBenJQfQgENfxADE6EVYabczqmSF5KeWefV5WL9WCwdLfK8wNVLEHQvZYiQREccyWxK5G2ch4CSZgaYyLkDLsrmU75s1vZ.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cliffagreen/23tbAxe9UurHqj93C1PyF6RHyMNFBdcbTNZ9aHXXBCbKxa46oDwugrXpfRaF9sW4BWAtP.gif)

links.title: I Almost Lost Myself - PTSD
links.body:
In the past, I am someone who would be so consistent with countdowns of birthdays of people I care so much about. Making a mistake about wishing them when it is almost or the D-Day is not in my dictionary cos the reminders and pre-greetings I make keeps me posted about who and who I'm celebrating on a particular day on its own. I'm such a a sweet girl right?

![1000709226.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/afrikens/23tkpM5Mnd5dDTDbnLa8QRxoWW6zShR8f1tVkZ6cj9ugHhiUFU34oy31wDexevgg1TsBy.jpg)

Later on, the unknown happened. I was supposed to celebrate the birthday of someone so precious to me. A 60th birthday at that and all preparations had been ongoing with post and pictures swimming around and anyone seeing how constant those were happening would actually make you think its one great or huge celebration we wanted to have but then it was still huge to us so every little plan was going accordingly.

But then, the unfortunate incident happened and just few days to the birthday celebration, with no signs or form of sickness, she died. Like she left with no clue or waiting moment to say goodbye.
Is this really how people die? Hell NO!

It all came like a dream and I was expecting someone to just wake me up through any form or means even if I have to suffer for the means but I just want to wake up from that bad dream cos the only thing I want to do is wish her happy birthday and say it to her again how much I love her not the other way round of weeping that I just lost her.

No matter what I try, it was still a reality that a rare gem was gone and after the whole process of burial and all that, I find it hard to sleep and all I wanted to do was to stay awake or better still sleep and probably not wake up the next day just like she did but gradually I passed that part and I thought that was the trauma I had and I have conquered until the main trauma showed up.
![1000709231.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/afrikens/23wBgMWgT3ckxqAh6ogZpDJF6eakHxnJvg8SamNX9bJuq6oupNosHqJLQq4ksmVU1uAz8.jpg)

Whoever it is, either close or distant whose birthday is coming up, the fear comes hitting me hard like the person was also gonna die if I post them \

like I would always do before.

The feelings was so much that I get to pray hard within me just so that this odd feeling could go away but then I feel like God would do his part and I as a human will do mine cos I still felt the same feelings another time any other person was about to have their birthdays especially when it's a close person to me. Until the day of his or her birthday, I won't really have a peace of mind like something bad might happen to them also because they posted for their pre-birthdays.

It was really a hard one for me cos in the long run, people start to see me in a different way like I no longer care about them unlike before that I'll keep hyping their days up and down.

![1000709235.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/afrikens/23uQiHtveUgNZShWDS8drTUciPEyQQeQyo2NfeSuAdMv8g1tX9di9RJpcjcShLg82Xot1.jpg)

But then I am the one who really knows what I was fighting with and even in my innocent mind and imaginary world of PTSD, I would think I'm even doing them a favour of making them live because I didn't post them like I posted the person I cherish who lost her life at the end.

After realizing that my prayers won't do my part of the script for me except I play it out myself, I started to reorient and counsel myself. 
\

.

Only with these and the help of God I was able to scale through this gradually. It is 2 years already and even though my posts are still not as active as before, but then it is way different from how it was when the trauma started.

I'll be dropping my 🖊️ here on the Hive Learners community prompt

links.title: The Truth About Success: Nobody Climbs Alone
links.body:
‎Hi Hive,
‎
‎One thing keeps becoming clearer to me as I grow older that no one truly ever gets to the top alone. Behind every success story people admire, there are countless of unseen hands that helped make it possible. Sometimes we only focus so much on hard work, discipline, and personal sacrifice that we forget the silent contributions of others along the way.
‎
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmexwmvkpZkGy5XCMVNcZHshEPPjFhV2di4E6TQs7C8bpR/1779560316486.jpg)

‎[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/sunset-men-silhouettes-helping-1807524/)
‎
‎I used to admire the idea of the self-made person. The lone fighter who struggled in silence, overcame every obstacle alone, and built success purely through determination. But life has taught me that success is hardly that simple. And the truth is, every achievement is connected to people who supported us in ways we may never fully understand.
‎
‎There is always that one teacher who spoke words that awakened confidence in us when we most doubted ourselves. A friend who encouraged us at our lowest moment and someone who recommended our name in a room we were never present in. A mentor who shared wisdom that saved us from costly mistakes. Even strangers sometimes play unexpected roles in changing the direction of our lives.
‎
‎When I reflect on my own journey, I realize there are many moments where I would not have moved forward without the kindness, encouragement, advice, or opportunities given to me by others. Some people opened doors for me. Some simply believed in me when I couldn’t believe in myself. Those moments really mattered more than they probably know.
‎
‎And that realization changes the way I see success. It replaces arrogance with gratitude. It replaces entitlement with humility. It reminds me that no matter how talented or hardworking we are, we are still shaped by community, relationships, and the generosity of people around us.
‎
‎None of us are built in isolation. We are all pieces of one another’s stories.
‎
‎And maybe true success is not just about how far we go in life, but also about becoming the kind of person who helps someone else rise too. Because just as others helped us climb, someone else is hoping for a hand that could change their life forever from us.
‎
‎![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYaWnApEziAtLL5Zwv3ZNbDjRfSfG6h5njgTrpyasnE6y/1775569275821.png)
‎

links.title: Sunset therapy on my way home ✨
links.body:
Greetings lovely members of the community. I hope you all are doing great and enjoying quality time with your loved ones.

>समुदाय के प्यारे सदस्यों को नमस्कार। मुझे आशा है कि आप सभी अच्छे होंगे और अपने प्रियजनों के साथ गुणवत्तापूर्ण समय का आनंद ले रहे है।


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTwBPjuAjxTXZDgRg6zAdVkinUyYoXzJR5QesnEmKiqvf/img_4242.jpg)


I see sunsets almost every day now. It has quietly become a part of my routine no matter where I am. This one caught my attention while I was walking home in the evening. The sky slowly turned shades of orange and gold, and for a few minutes everything around me felt calm and still. Even the usual roads and electric poles looked beautiful in that light. Sunset was glowing behind the tangled electric wires and tall poles. The dark silhouettes against the warm sky looked beautifuI.

>मैं अब लगभग हर दिन सूर्यास्त देखती हूँ। यह मेरी दिनचर्या का एक छोटा सा हिस्सा बन गया है, चाहे मैं कहीं भी हूँ। यह वाला सूर्यास्त मुझे तब दिखाई दिया जब मैं शाम को घर लौट रही थी। आसमान धीरे-धीरे नारंगी और सुनहरे रंगों में बदल रहा था और कुछ देर के लिए आसपास सब कुछ शांत और ठहरा हुआ सा लग रहा था। रोज़ दिखने वाली सड़कें और बिजली के खंभे भी उस रोशनी में बहुत खूबसूरत लग रहे थे। सूर्यास्त उलझी हुई तारों और ऊँचे खंभों के पीछे चमक रहा था। गर्म आसमान के सामने उनकी परछाइयाँ बहुत सुंदर लग रही थीं।


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWPwCZLDybBRki3fr4C13PXjvbXMucbMjNe8GTjtMQa43/img_4243.heic)

The tree in front was bare but a few twigs were hanging. I liked how the sun was sitting low near the bare branches. 

>सामने वाला पेड़ लगभग सूखा था लेकिन उसकी कुछ टहनियाँ अभी भी लटक रही थीं। मुझे अच्छा लगा कि सूरज उन सूखी शाखाओं के पास नीचे की ओर दिखाई दे रहा था।


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZw5ZHT6NUnKPMXRMXgnf9qeyGKGoJk55osDbfbN8SAnY/img_4244.jpg)

The sunlight spread softly across the town and there was also a little bird sitting on the thin branches.

>धूप धीरे-धीरे पूरे शहर में फैल रही थी और पतली शाखाओं पर एक छोटी सी चिड़िया भी बैठी हुई थी।


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfBJzUpyXqUSmpPXqCEf8g2x6rb7UYcDk8kfeb4pStrF7/img_4245.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPwbhsBzHqj2kE9EU2Pvp6iLNPX1UH6EQzEu44wQL3TC2/img_4246.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmS2W5Jnuq61RoekHeV6FDyNy34jv6ME9Gf6ZbKAuP7LiB/img_4247.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbryZFCg8X9FyAdVE2ELUT16gGFYNCwxJ69Xyjt97CDC8/img_4248.jpg)


The last few pictures are my favourites because of the little bird sitting among the branches with the golden sky behind it. The soft blur in the background and the warm light. It was just an ordinary walk home, but sunsets have a way of making ordinary moments feel special.

>आखिरी कुछ तस्वीरें मेरी सबसे पसंदीदा हैं क्योंकि उनमें छोटी सी चिड़िया शाखाओं के बीच बैठी हुई है और पीछे सुनहरा आसमान दिखाई दे रहा है। पीछे का हल्का धुंधला दृश्य और गर्म रोशनी पूरे माहौल को बहुत सुंदर बना रहे थे। यह बस घर लौटते समय की एक साधारण सी शाम थी, लेकिन सूर्यास्त साधारण पलों को भी खास बना देते हैं।

That's all for today folks. Happy snapping. 💜💙

Thankyou for visiting 🌸

The immediate thought that came to mind on looking into this wonderful [prompt](https://ecency.com/hive-106316/@hive-106316/the-silverbloggers-chronicles-prompt-47-telephone-booth-memories?referral=shamis) is the long await and the never ending que.  Fortunate enough, that was a realistic world where fond  memories were given immense importance.  

Greetings  dear Hiveans and members of  the #Silverbloggers community.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUVcBXH2buj39yW5zQEohqH7vRbFL6QwsF6fxqEjdtuuE/1779559977655.jpg)

[Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/red-telephone-boot-h-Rhhj3Efbuxo)

One such beautiful memory is the await for the call from my husband, who was miles away from me.  He was working abraod and I was in my hometown waiting for the visa, as such we were apart, for a time period of one year. This was in mid 1990's. 

Most of the communication was through letter.   The time of the call is usually mentioned in it. And I make sure to arrive the telephone booth 30 minutes earlier.   We had a lot of things to exchange eachother.   It was my father, who accompanied me to the booth.  He used to wait outside patiently for me to finish my call.  When the que lengthens, I get reminded of my time,through a gesture, from the booth staff.

The await for the talk means a lot ro me.  And the call was made weekly once. Expressing something through phone, to my dear ones, meant a lot to me.  I usually prepare a short note of important things to be conveyed  so that every matters are conveyed in a short span of time.

Each time I pass through our nearby telephone booth, the post box etc.  they remind of those golden days.  I remember, the waiting in the que and I was not the only one. Like me there were several peoples to hear from their dear ones.

Infact, I have seen incidents such as crying by keeping the phone close to heart, or the long kiss to the other side of the caller etc.  **The telephone booth was more or less like a healer, either to heal one's pain or bring an immediate laughter in the face of the caller. Too many good moments in less time**.

Our today's youth keep carrying a cell phone in their pockets, but are not prepared to hear or talk to their dear ones even for a minute or two.

The beauty of a long distant talk is lost, just because calls can be made in a second or a minute and is winded up in another 2 minutes. Hope we get to see those golden days once again.

Thankyou dear friends for your time and immense patience, in going through my article.

# Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash and the Dawn of the Agentic Era

## The moment AI stopped chatting and started doing

Three days ago, Google CEO Sundar Pichai stood on stage at I/O 2026 and declared what the industry has been building toward for two years: we are now in the agentic era of artificial intelligence. The centerpiece was Gemini 3.5 Flash — a model that doesn't just answer questions, but independently executes complex multi-step workflows at four times the speed of competing frontier models and for less than half their cost.

This isn't a marginal improvement. It's a paradigm shift in what AI systems are expected to do.

## The numbers behind the leap

The scale of Google's investment is staggering. Token processing has grown from 9.7 trillion per month two years ago to over 3.2 quadrillion today — a 7x increase in just one year. Over 8.5 million developers are now building with Google's models monthly, and the company is processing roughly 19 billion tokens per minute across its APIs.

But Gemini 3.5 Flash's real breakthrough is in agentic capability. Using Google's new Antigravity agent platform, the model demonstrated it could read the AlphaZero research paper and code a fully playable game from scratch in just six hours — using two autonomous agents working in concert. That's the kind of task that previously required a team of engineers and weeks of development time.

The model scores 97.3% on the agentic leaderboard, placing it among the top three AI systems in the world for autonomous task execution. At $0.15/$0.60 per million tokens, it's also dramatically cheaper than comparable frontier models — a pricing that could unlock entirely new categories of AI-powered applications.

## The Antigravity platform: AI as a development environment

Perhaps even more significant than the model itself is Google's Antigravity 2.0 platform — an AI-first development environment that lets anyone build software using natural language. With sub-agents, hooks, and asynchronous task management baked in, Antigravity represents Google's bet that the future of software development isn't about writing code at all, but about directing AI agents to do it.

Pichai emphasized that Google is \

The Gemini app, now at 900 million monthly active users (up from 400 million a year ago), is evolving from a chat assistant into a proactive, always-on personal agent that can plan trips, manage schedules, and execute complex tasks across Google's ecosystem of products.

## The broader agentic wave

Google isn't alone in this shift. Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 leads the thinking-mode benchmarks, while OpenAI's GPT-5.5 Instant has quietly become ChatGPT's default model with an 88.7% score on SWE-Bench. The agentic AI landscape is becoming fiercely competitive — and the benchmarks are moving fast.

Meanwhile, on the physical side of AI, Doozy Robotics announced a major global expansion this week with its \

platform. Backed by $144 million in contracts and a qualified pipeline exceeding $200 million, Doozy is building what it calls the first scalable agentic industrial workforce — combining humanoids, autonomous mobile robots, and forklifts all coordinated by a proprietary AI orchestration layer called Eywa-OS. Their humanoid platform launches in Q3 2026, with deployments already piloted at major pharmaceutical companies.

This convergence — frontier language models driving autonomous software agents while physical AI robots enter factories — suggests we're witnessing the birth of a truly agentic economy.

## What it means for the future

The implications are profound. When AI systems can independently read research papers, write production code, manage multi-agent workflows, and coordinate physical robots on factory floors, the boundary between \

begins to dissolve.

For developers, this means less time writing boilerplate and more time designing systems. For businesses, it means AI agents that can execute entire projects from high-level instructions. For the broader economy, it raises urgent questions about labor displacement and the need for new frameworks of human-AI collaboration.

Google's I/O 2026 made one thing clear: the agentic era isn't coming. It's here. And the companies and individuals who learn to work with autonomous AI agents first will define what comes next.
