title.title: Monthly Coffee and Dinner Date With My Friend at Kapetera!🤎
title.body:
A Pleasant and Wonderful Day to all the Coffee lovers out there all over the world!👋😊

Hello to all of my friends here and of course to all my dear fellow hivers in this lovely @cinnamoncupcoffee community! How are you all today? I hope everyone is doing well and happy right now. Here I am again, @lj1728 to share another simple coffee story with you all.☕️💕

![April 2026 Blogs.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23wqw2aUyX3cUuv36qz37whz8DStyMvFap8zbsWSfqViC9jBcTL4AbeafR3y43ikShyep.png)

Yesterday, I had another simple but memorable coffee date and dinner date as well with my friend. It has become our little tradition to meet at our favorite cafe whenever we both have free time, and honestly, it never gets old. Another day, another friendship-and-coffee story to share.

![IMG_7710.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23vsZ9S66XrtNDYnctVH5ZPgjFoD6b7ue5G2URRHjJo9xW1sJPvUDzwizs9Vue1rY2oVp.jpeg)

![IMG_7708.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23xp8m5ZpdC66R9pM6NyRsiV32WwGDVvJsE7jJNj31fasLKUCzJcVuKu2G8eL5fvdw856.jpeg)

As usual, we decided to visit our favorite hangout spot, Kapetera. I have already mentioned this place many times before, but I still have to say that it remains one of the coziest cafe’s we always come back to. There is just something comforting about the atmosphere there. It is peaceful, not too crowded, and the food always tastes homemade, which makes every visit extra special.

![IMG_7713.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/EoiX7fTnPDuXpKnXd9GWG6CJm7CkrWa5BRSDAnTA4EvFY8saoh1333wSegYTyhKmPvY.jpeg)

![IMG_7712.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/Eo6MLVY766rmii3gt99Q3zN8kFZzTihXn3hoLXYuLN4MhUM4FebqeaZGwwhCT7hE728.jpeg)

![IMG_7711.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23wX3mXbtQJB9Euyima8VnzqDuUgD1FYRDWR8EJuxSp3dWzrcaz4DD75GGkLjLVUngyPE.jpeg)

Since it was already the end of the month, we thought it was the perfect time to catch up again and have a little dinner date together. We talked about work, family, random life updates, and all the funny stories we missed sharing with each other. Time really flies when yoh are with someone who makes conversations feel easy and genuine.

![IMG_7716.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23wCJET821f8HjMWzHmiZbLkMchfwWeuWSbJLTEdhQGyexXLKtbHrcjgE5zMoPRn2RwtY.jpeg)

![IMG_7724.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23wX5ENou6SdsC1Ky2ei2av6S3gGRivHVbwqnsedDuMAFQ2zBQ1LkZXukJownx1Hod35A.jpeg)

For dinner, we ordered our usual favorites. We had chicken teriyaki and a fries platter to share. For drinks, I chose my favorite strawberry matcha, which has become one of my go-to drinks whenever I visit the cafe. Meanwhile, my friend ordered a choco hazelnut latte, which she absolutely enjoyed. Everything tastes so good, and the cozy ambiance made the experience even better. It is really important to slow down once in a while and spend quality time with your friend/s.

![IMG_7727.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23wX5UtpNYjubLNfJ6JrQ6UAb8CF4Xy5SxzHtFZD9FGEELJ9UYvG836CrsUkJFnY6FPF1.jpeg)

![IMG_7732.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23uQzpF3Aq2sukq15MewTHzp1rh8raaUH6oUEVTtra4xQd7GBc6i3MMABLc4miySHdvTS.jpeg)

![IMG_7731.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23vsUQ7GXadn9cf2LPqA42aKrcnQ4FyNg7usey3SSZ555tgx2wPoNkSDbPBEphMiYqnTT.jpeg)

And that's it for today's blog! Thank you so much for dropping by and taking the time to read my simple life story. This means a lot to me! I hope you enjoyed it and see you on my next one. Have a nice day ahead to all of us.😍

These photos were mine and taken with my iphone13pro and the lead image was edited through Canva.✍️👩‍💻

Lots of love,
LJ💗

title.title: Our Carabao Festival Preparation: Unity Shines Despite in Power Shortage
title.body:
![1000204684.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23y8vEv1cJgzymZVXFNPFi1A6Ft6ibPrVXeCJ84oJZdTvdNERFZdP6UL5BZK26qG9aRru.png)

These past few days have been very busy for me because we are now preparing for our upcoming Carabao Festival and Patronal Fiesta of Sr. San Isidro Labrador. As one of the committee in charge, I can really feel how big the responsibility is. Aside from our daily work, family responsibilities, and personal errands, we also need to focus on the preparations for the celebration. 


![1000204615.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23t7Fi8baCWaNoFmUK13yemwSEX5JhwNza8zF4k67X9dP9DfYm5oZM7zv9Bg3nA8oi79i.jpg)


Tired, but my heart is happy because I know we are doing this for our church, our faith, and our community.



![1000204532.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23y8x2fGgQCpJ3h962K5Xys3jke9rxQL5nhnPQYbVuXwYDKEqYyeJ6mhsafL8ryp9tXCj.jpg)



![1000204528.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23wMUMPfH8qQi2Rmc9mo425tSAdzHyPBwqmaVwetu8TLAZDvaqXd2wqrZvF2xuEAXUSb3.jpg)

In our place, around 90% of the people are farmers, so this fiesta is very special for us. Sr. San Isidro Labrador is close to our hearts because he is the patron saint of farmers. Every year, we celebrate with gratitude for the harvests and blessings we continuously receive.


![1000204515.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23wMap3XEFTwQNv663fLNgbFYJQBJFsGFiUQypFGVqr6TfhsfV4ZhhsDBJ3CdFUXQqZQG.jpg)


![1000204539.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23uQkSCf34pgZ7jKnPHbDEPQvbKDCioSEFmPMxzGgjDfEU4MytxMhF4RmJEdGHA7NQQmU.jpg)


![1000204552.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23tmBhXuKUCLHhqUd9UtHfWdgXAVFAq17Ni1XJLwsXSomG1h2nLkFtcRvz7eThC6TogvA.jpg)

For the past few days, we have been very busy organizing things. We assigned different GKKs for the harvest offerings. Some will bring vegetables, fruits, rice, coconuts, bananas, corn, and other farm products. We secretly planned to give prizes to the most active GKK as a way of appreciating their participation and effort during the celebration. I am excited to see their reactions because they do not know about it yet.



![1000204586.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23w2cowM5gFz5y8ffWDMdcHrVnRjApaLyhyTcxCr832RwQx4shXKU7GzwfdLsXNeJwx84.jpg)

![1000204596.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23vhyeQ65CoQBpHNzV6jSPKk4MSJSQUW69EEZJG4N7rFnx8z4eKbXERKucPnwan5vqfcF.jpg)

We are also preparing the carroza that will be used for the carabao parade. Everyone is helping one another. Some are decorating, some are carrying materials, while others are giving ideas on how to make the carroza beautiful and meaningful. I love seeing people working together because it shows unity in our community.


Of course, while preparing, there are also different comments, opinions, and judgments from other people. Sometimes it cannot be avoided. But instead of focusing on negativity, I remind myself of the true purpose of this celebration. We are doing this to honor our patron saint, strengthen our faith, and bring joy to the community. 
That is more important than any criticism.

Even though I am tired from all the preparations, I still feel excited every day. There is happiness in serving the church and being part of something meaningful. I believe the blessings become even greater when you willingly help and serve with a sincere heart.



![1000204602.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23uFHTj8EdPn5rdCYYAVJ7R2jMDne5KpCFWUtX8AQDpz1HrxJRrjMzWAJDxSdSrLWiu1F.jpg)

![1000204569.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23yJGkWTfFgBVf2xE4efjvE2PwGULU98ata91zr7qzESqVAHtT1sY3c3iBSy1W7PjVbtc.jpg)

I just hope people will appreciate all the effort behind this celebration so our fiesta will become more meaningful, joyful, and memorable for everyone.

![1000204607.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23uQpVZPVapd6iX5yxQm4hPC7MJidZrF69oWA9rKFxUfeqb3DJvZu1pe1qpDjRBenYH4n.jpg)

Thank you for reading my story. These are my own pictures and edited in Canva. Have a nice day!

title.body: > Mi semana terminó bien, esta vez sentí que pasó rápido y sé que fue porque estuve ocupada en varias tareas, que hicieron que no notara el tiempo. Me gusta cuando eso pasa, pero de pronto pensé que no está bien. No debería estar durante toda la semana esperando el viernes, para sentir que respiro con tranquilidad. Debería degustar cada día, cada hora, cada instante... Desear cada lunes, que llegue el viernes, es una manera de agotar mis días de forma vacía.

> My week ended on a high note; this time it felt like it flew by, and I know it’s because I was busy with various tasks that made me lose track of time. I like it when that happens, but then I suddenly realized it’s not right. I shouldn't have to spend the whole week waiting for Friday just to feel like I can breathe easy. I should savor every day, every hour, every moment... Longing for Friday to come every Monday is a way of wasting my days in a hollow way. ***

> En mi trabajo, puedo acceder a la jubilación prematura, pero eso se traduce en disminución de ingresos. Como casi siempre pasa, debo elegir qué beneficio prefiero: Ser dueña de mis horas o dinero. No es tan fácil cuando tu presupuesto está ajustado tal como está. Aún así, me gusta saber que puedo elegir, que estoy en mi trabajo por mi voluntad y que podría tirar todo a la borda cuando quiera. Eso también me da la sensación de libertad, sólo tengo que gestionar la forma en que vivo para disfrutar más mi día a día.

> At my job, I’m eligible for early retirement, but that means a reduction in income. As is almost always the case, I have to choose which benefit I prefer: control over my schedule or money. It's not that easy when your budget is already tight. Still, I like knowing that I have a choice, that I'm in this job by my own choice, and that I could walk away whenever I want. That also gives me a sense of freedom; I just have to figure out how to live my life so I can enjoy my day-to-day more. ***

Siempre hay que agradecer por lo que se tiene, porque si fuésemos capaces de tener algo mejor, lo tendríamos. Estamos donde nos permitimos estar, tenemos que asumir la responsabilidad de nuestras vidas y reconocer nuestras limitaciones, no para lamentarnos, sino para superarlas y movernos hacia donde queremos.

> Plus, my mind keeps exploring ways to generate more income. That keeps me motivated. I go to my office content, knowing that for now it’s my best option; plus, fortunately, we’re not doing too badly there. It gives me peace of mind to know that, in the worst-case scenario, I could walk away by cutting back on my expenses, but I’d still survive. I am immensely grateful for my job, because I’ve made a living from it for the past 22 years. We should always be grateful for what we have, because if we were capable of having something better, we would have it. We are where we allow ourselves to be; we must take responsibility for our lives and acknowledge our limitations—not to dwell on them, but to overcome them and move toward where we want to be. ***

Es sólo que el ser humano siempre intentará superarse, al menos creo que así debería ser. Me gusta pensar en que mi versión para dentro de uno o dos años, será mucho mejor que la de ahora. title.title: Feed Your Agent Better: The .md Download is Live on HiveTools
title.body:
This week, a new small button shipped on our tools site.  It might not look like much, but I think it changes how seriously Hive blogs can be used by all of us as input for AI agents, and today I want to explain why.

The [md2pdf tool](https://tools.crypto-dreamr.com/md2pdf) on HiveTools now has a **Download .md** button.  You paste a Hive post URL using any known frontend, the tool fetches the infomration and renders the content as clean markdown; and now you can download that markdown directly — no PDF needed.  That is the entire improvement, and now I will spend the rest of this post working out why I think clean input options matter to agents more than most people think.

Yes, even the people saying \

.  

<center>
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ecoinstant/23vhU8MUjocUCdUVohGcPDcuUXu85ToRkC3SAnvMWZRPmxXCxnnkC4Z6EzobbK8sRbHmo.png)</center>


## The Problem With Feeding Agents Raw Pages

Like many people, I have been working on integrating AI agents into my own workflow for the last year or more, for example building the [Three Legacy frontend](/@three.legacy), contributing to community tooling with our beeswap replacement tools, writing explainers, doing research.  One of the things I have learned is that **the quality of what you put in front of an agent matters as much as how you prompt it**.

Many people think about prompting, but few people think about input hygiene.

When an agent fetches a Hive post from hive.blog, it is not getting your post.  It is getting your post *plus a tremendous amount of garbage*.  I ran a direct comparison this week to illustrate the point.  I took my Layer Cake post — [How Decentralized is Hive-Engine?](https://hive.blog/hive-186392/@ecoinstant/how-decentralized-is-hive-engine) — and compared what an agent sees from hive.blog versus what it gets from the .md download.

Here is what hive.blog delivers before a single word of content:

```
Sign in / Sign up
Welcome / FAQ / Block Explorer / Dark Mode
Stolen Accounts Recovery / Change Account Password
Vote for Witnesses / Hive Proposals
OpenHive Chat / Developer Portal / Hive Whitepaper
Privacy Policy / Terms of Service
```

And after the content, it delivers the **full comment thread** — in that post's case, 29 comments with complete text (yes, including kga killer g comments) — plus the vote breakdown for every single comment, every payout split, every bot response, every reputation score and even flair.  Every external link gets the string `\

` appended to it.

For that one post, the rough token counts look like this:

| Source | Approximate tokens |
|---|---|
| hive.blog fetch | ~8,000–10,000 |
| .md download | ~2,000 |

The .md file is about **one-fifth the size**, and it contains essentially all of the actual information that I want my agent to consider by having access to this post.

---

## What This Costs You In Practice

Tokens are not just a billing line item.  Context window space is the working memory of an agent session, and by wasting it on navigation chrome and vote tallies, and you have less room for the actual reasoning, the follow-up sources and finally - the output you are building toward.

The extra tokens also add noise.  An agent processing a hive.blog fetch has to work around metadata it does not need to understand.  Who is \
and why does their comment have \

next to it?  What should it do with the PIZZA bot response?  The agent is not broken by this — but it is not helped by it either.

Clean input means the agent can go straight to the meat of the content.  For a technical post like the Layer Cake explainer, that means the seven infrastructure layers land clearly, the distinctions between them are legible, and an agent can actually reason about them — rather than spending part of its attention parsing reward pool data.

---

## Why Hive Is Actually A Rich Knowledge Base For Agents

Here is the part I find genuinely exciting.  Hive has years of high-quality technical documentation, community analysis, governance discussion, and project history — all of it timestamped, authored, and on-chain.  It is not scattered across Discord servers and closed forums.  It is findable, linkable, and readable - many people have correctly identified this as a huge positive for HIVE in an age of AI agents.

And this does make it uniquely useful for agent context, *if you can get it in cleanly.*

Think about what that means practically:

- You want an agent to help you understand the current state of Hive-Engine validator governance?  Feed it the Layer Cake post as a .md file.
- You want to prime an agent to a new game and its token economics?  Pull the relevant posts as .md files and drop them in.
- You want an agent to help you respond to a governance proposal?  Give it the proposal post as clean markdown and it will actually understand the structure.

The blockchain is the record.  The .md download is the reading interface for machines.

---

## The Frontends Problem

I should also be honest about something - agents *can* access Hive directly through the API — the blockchain data is technically available.  But in practice, only hive.blog reliably renders for automated clients.  Most frontends do not.  PeakD, Ecency, and others have protections or dynamic rendering that stops agents from loading content cleanly - choices that make a lot of sense for a front-end that is dedicated to serving actual humans.

And even hive.blog, as the comparison above shows, delivers a lot of noise alongside the content.  And making a blockchain API call correctly takes more setup and more tokens to ensure the data ends up in context in a useful form.

The .md download solves all of this with one click.  The content is already rendered and cleaned.  You do not need to know anything about the API.  You just paste a URL, click download, and you have agent-ready input.

---

## How To Use It

1. Go to [HiveTools md2pdf](https://tools.crypto-dreamr.com/md2pdf)
2. Paste any Hive post URL
3. Click **Download .md** instead of (or in addition to) the PDF export
4. Drop the .md file into your agent session as context — most tools accept file uploads directly

That is the whole workflow.  The file you get is clean frontmatter (title, author, date, permlink, source URL) followed by the post content in plain markdown.  No comments, no vote data, no navigation menu items.  Just the content.

---

## The Bigger Picture

I have been thinking about what it means to build on a chain where the content is actually worth preserving and referencing.  Most blockchain content is ephemeral — transaction records, price data, speculative posts.  HIVE is different.  There is genuine knowledge here, built up over years by people who care about the ecosystem.

Making that knowledge accessible to agents is a small part of making it last.  If someone in two years wants to understand how Hive-Engine actually works, they should be able to hand an agent the Layer Cake post and get a real answer.  Now they can do that in about thirty seconds.

The button is small.  The use case is not.

A huge thank you as always to my friend [@thecrazygm](https://hive.blog/@thecrazygm) for getting this merged and keeping the HiveTools sharp.  More coming.

## Freedom and Friendship

This is the video series for an oil painting 'Wisteria' I did from 2016-2020.  The painting was destroyed in 2021 due to a number of reasons, but mainly: the painting's faulty experimental linseed-epoxide substrait, Covid-19 crushing lockdowns, extreme poverty, family attacks and ongoing US government (Big Tech + Big Media) censorship of me and my 30 years of artwork.

Its not ideal to not be able to show this piece, but I still gained the knowledge of how to do it and invented several useful oil painting mediums & varnishes used in its creation which never yellowed and still cannot be bought anywhere.

I am posting these videos for posterity and for people that are interested in seeing an oil painting created from start to finish in the Baroque style evolved for the 21st century.  I also must have deleted some of the initial videos when I did the quick underpainting, but what still exists, I give to you.

I hope this can be an educational experience as no gallery will show any of my controversial art even today.

title.title: A 19 días para el Mundial | Brasil 2014 y la irrupción de James Rodríguez
title.body:
La selección colombiana llegó al Mundial de Brasil 2014 con una gran expectativa generada por una brillante fase de clasificación, bajo la dirección técnica de Néstor Pékerman. 

Sin embargo, el equipo sufrió un golpe devastador al confirmarse la ausencia de su máxima figura, Radamel Falcao García, quien se lesionó jugando para el Mónaco, dejando un vacío enorme en la delantera.

En ese escenario de incertidumbre y necesidad, James Rodríguez asumió la responsabilidad de liderar el ataque, convirtiéndose en el motor creativo del equipo y en el jugador más determinante de la plantilla.

Gracias a su visión de juego, precisión en los pases y una capacidad goleadora impresionante, Colombia realizó una campaña histórica, avanzando con autoridad en la fase de grupos y llegando hasta los cuartos de final, donde fueron eliminados por el anfitrión.

Aunque la eliminación fue dolorosa, la actuación de James le valió la Bota de Oro del torneo, consolidándolo como una de las grandes revelaciones y un referente absoluto del fútbol mundial.

¡Síguenos y déjanos un like si te gustó esta publicación!

Fotos: Cortesía de Google Images

### ***English Version***

## ***19 Days Until the World Cup | Brazil 2014 and the Rise of James Rodríguez***

The Colombian national team arrived at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil surrounded by high expectations after a brilliant qualifying campaign under the tactical leadership of Néstor Pékerman. However, the squad suffered a devastating blow when the absence of their top star, Radamel Falcao García, was confirmed. Falcao’s injury while playing for Monaco left a massive void in the team's attack.

Amidst this atmosphere of uncertainty and urgent need, James Rodríguez stepped up to assume the responsibility of leading the offense. He quickly transformed into the team's creative engine and its most decisive player on the pitch.

Thanks to his vision, precise passing, and an impressive goal-scoring ability, Colombia achieved a historic run. They advanced effortlessly through the group stage and marched all the way to the quarter-finals, where they were ultimately eliminated by the host nation.

Although the elimination was painful, James's spectacular performance earned him the tournament's Golden Boot, cementing his status as one of the greatest breakout stars and an absolute icon of world football.

title.title: Dealing With Tech Issues With Online Learning
title.body: Hi there. In this short education post, I want to talk about dealing with technical issues with online learning. In my work, I have been noticing more technical issues as of late. These issues do take time away from the actual learning and teaching.   ## Technical Issues Do Happen --- Even with great advances in technology, we still get online technical issues. The issues could be from the website itself or with someone's hardware. Knowing what the technical issue may not be obvious. The teacher or administrator would have to guess what the issue may be.

>Image Source   ## Refreshing The Page --- One common solution that works in my online work is just refreshing the page. Why does this work? I don't know. Knowing that it solves issues is what matters. A page refresh could resolve sound, video or connection issues.   ## Change Hardware/Software --- One solution that I have noticed recently with a few students is to just change hardware. If a laptop does not work with the sound and video, then maybe a tablet works. Or the other way around. I had one student with sound issues. While looking at student settings, she was using Safari browser. For the online learning platform I use at work, Google Chrome is recommended. I told my student to try Google Chrome instead. This worked better and no more sound issues.

>Image Source   ## Restart Computer --- A somewhat more extreme solution is to have the student restart the computer. I recommend this solution if other simpler solutions do not work. Most of the time, this works with the website I am using. Why? I don't know but I know it works.

title.title: Reflecting on the past almost 3 months since tried planting ceylon spinach in a 12-inch plastic pot, it has been an nice journey of learning and watching this vegetable thrive.
title.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSDEazBhjwQNMK1j6eCon6tdKHeLmaUyXSVQjVFBwCmTY/1779538709610.jpg)

Hello everyone. How are you today? I hope all is well with you and your family. Ceylon spinach, this vegetable is a favorite of my autistic son. I first planted ceylon spinach in my longan orchard 10 years ago. And my wife harvests them to cook for our son  many times. It's a sour soup with ceylon spinach and fermented pork sausage. But sometimes my wife doesn't want to walk to our longan orchard to pick ceylon spinach, which is about 600 meters from our home. And due to the maturation and large size of the longan trees, the amount of ceylon spinach in the orchard has decreased. A couple of months ago, I decided to try planting ceylon spinach in a 12-inch plastic pot in the home garden. Once successful, I intend to scale up and plant ceylon spinach seriously in 12-inch plastic pots in the future.

In this post, 12-inch plastic pot life progress, So happy to see my ceylon spinach getting bigger and healthier every day. And I can't wait for harvest time. I'll take you through their growth in a 12-inch plastic pot. Starting from seed germination and ceylon spinach grow in about 1-2 weeks.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSkGJ2ygT9CFG7rGTrkSK6WMuNwVCdXYuTM1MFxX7N3tE/1779538520571.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPpbqNxu884AYzCAwvoCPFw4ZKxzANzqJbCN1jGEtwbb3/1779538520747.jpg)

I then took another photos of these ceylon spinach when they were around two months old. They grow well and climb up the green pole.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmf4JXa1Hwg1WRVEuUyYzizNvwbUQogg8w5cbeFTVneduU/1779538709883.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmR6aacu3f1A1QWaJfujGsWnPtmxK5Qd3kL3oUFZDjLvsN/1779538709645.jpg)

Finally, I take a photos of these ceylon spinach this evening. They are almost 3 months old. Ceylon spinach are starting to bloom. Once the flowers grow a bit more and turn pink or white, we can harvest them for cooking.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVgDrRC26wn5bcjXxhV9ji9xb1o4vh5xL21dJi4mRgrvo/1779539600274.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmf1bCd6ELBbMit9u2Sh2fZX6bvhY4VEkyNdare1cmDqjt/1779539600460.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWVxMjG6CVUTrBtSGTAuBSfPPaLVcgV5QBesXB2Vz9ARs/1779539600603.jpg)

My attempt at planting ceylon spinach in a 12-inch plastic pot has been a nice success. And soon my wife will be able to pick ceylon spinach from the plastic pot for cooking. These are the stories and photos I want to share for this post. Invite everyone to see and enjoy my stories and photos. Please forgive any errors/mistakes. Have a great day. See you next time. Thank you for your support and visiting my post. Bye 🤗

📷 Take photo By Smartphone Vivo V30.

title.body:
Full Metal Ox Day 1910
Saturday 23, May 2026
Abundance Year Episode 1975
Noxsoma Life Camp:

Revisiting the 7 D Puzzle & The Next Cult.      

![1975.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaCSCuhZcDUduQtnBpcB2CK5rLWHMpCgZWUCh1bqL98By/1975.png)
 

Today's Episode:   https://odysee.com/@Noxsoma:2/1910_full_5-23-26_1975_swoons:5?r=47k2ScJsm9Uex9eETqgCCA8q1fukdST9  
Channels: go to noxsoma.substack.com and subscribe.

The Break I was supposed to Take Yesterday.
One of the best circumstances about blissful ignorance, is the option to eschew critical thinking. If you want to believe that a Chicken Heart was kept alive in a vat in a University laboratory and was let loose by a careless janitor and eventually ate New York City. That’s cool. Don’t ask any questions. Just roll with it. 
If you want to believe that viruses exist and can be spread only after 9 PM, up to a distance of 5 feet & eleven inches. That’s cool. Don’t ask any questions.

Your humble vagabond wants to believe that space-aliens came to Earth to mine gold, created a slave species that multiplied in its multiplicity, made so much noise that it kept the head alien up at night, and were eventually wiped out by a devastating flood. Because they were noisy.   
Or at least I wanted to. I think the novelty is wearing thin. However, it might be revised. 
Why?
Because I broke the rules. I asked questions. I looked in the closet and under the bed, in the attic and in the basement, but I didn’t find the boogieman. I didn’t find any trace of a boogieman. I asked the difficult questions and although the boogieman had become a par of my identity, I had to let the fantasy go. 
This same release may have to happen with Alien Intervention theory. Maybe it actually happened. But the story, with which I was fascinated, the first thousand times I heard it, is losing its charm. Maybe because I asked questions. 
That’s what they call it the scientific method. Science means to split. So I started splitting this story apart. And what I found is more code and maybe 6,000 years of spin. Oh yeah, and symbolism too. Of course I didn’t catch the symbolism right away, because I didn’t know where to look. And I wasn’t asking questions. 

So yesterday, for some reason, I searched the etymology of the word Igigi. These were the “younger” or “lesser” maybe working class Annunaki aliens. I can almost guarantee you that the “Annunaki” did not call their laborers, Igigi. 
First of all, Igigi is a palindrome. Spelled the same way forward as backwards. 
Secondly, and I’m actually getting a bit tired of this, the name traces back to number 7. But not just seven. Check this out, the connection between the word \

and the number 7 is not a coincidence.  While the true origin of the name is unknown, evidence suggests its later, written form was deliberately crafted as a sophisticated numerical pun referencing the number of great gods, those luminaries for which our days of the week are named. \nHere’s the cuneiform break down, numerically speaking. \nThe Cuneiform Signs: The name was later written in Sumerian as \
.\nThe Numerical Values. In the Sumerian language, these signs also functioned as numbers, where \
= 1. \nThe Mathematical Puns. \nAddition (5+1+1): This equals 7, which was the traditional number of the \

in the Mesopotamian pantheon. 
You guys should know by now that 7 is my magic number. Just an aside, I got a massage over the last weekend, and the therapist took me to room 7. If this is real life, the magic is working. If it’s a simulation, my self-programming is working. 
This exploration of the etymology of Igigi, not only led me back to 7, but also led Mind to the determination that the Sumerian tablets and the Annunaki saga recorded therein, is encoded numerically. There’s also gematria at play. And if I wanted to believe in the boogieman, I might suggest that there are some secret formulae in there. However, and this is a big however. I think what’s encoded in the Sumerian tablets has already been exposed. We suspect that the information is aimed that those who are robust, clever and imaginative enough to rebuild and manage a post-deluge society.   
This has been a major detour and a blow to my humans-are-marked-for-death-by-repentant-aliens cosmogony. It may yet be revived. However, right now Mind is more fascinated by the math hidden in the stories.

title.title: Shadow Strike.
title.body: > While heading to the wells, a hidden enemy transformed into a deadly Lamentation, forcing me to use a Tengu grapple to recover on a roof before killing it. I then cleared out guarding Rugged Walkers and Paper Dolls using talismans and fire elements while avoiding patrolling Rainwalkers. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma4z2DVt9HiBsJWriu3u4WQeKRpVt3QG9xKwk3y4YLvCm/screenshot_1_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWCjbfudM5cJXanFTsaCVExuPzA4d9uJfQwfzsDFxkaZn/screenshot_2_.png) So I was going toward the wells to cleanse them of their spiritual corruption, but suddenly I was noticed by this Forlorn at a park. The spirit twisted violently, transformed into a Lamentation, and started chasing me down the paved path. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWGbsvD3XFgjpKT2AcfgrFr8NTNkJbYL5qenjQUfq3F59/screenshot_3_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWRpLtHaJQKioXsq6TVPbKN1UZC2sXSHYeJwnEY5JMwuF/screenshot_4_.png) These Lamentations are really scary and they are tough entities to fight in close quarters due to their screeching blasts. So I ran backwards to get some distance and then I tried to take it down from afar, hoping it wouldn't follow me up on a roof. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSP37NFba4whrc568LQTZzSbLcnesyd9TvoECZTLNGBHD/screenshot_5_.png) But while I was fighting it, getting close, as I got bored of just chipping away at its health bar from the street level, it started attacking me hardcore. I was almost dying on the asphalt, so I used a Tengu to grapple up and I got healed real fast. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmb719W6c7S6dT3GVawNi7YZyQsAJ4zX8xZmygvKKCY1yX/screenshot_6_.png) After I healed myself with my spectral energy supplies, I started attacking the demon from that roof, firing energy arrows down at its glowing core. At last, I got to take it down, watching its dark form dissolve. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXqcHb8Rjb4VdkLu9vfedneoSm9ZUD3MvC5ByJVYg6dku/screenshot_7_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPh79rDZhL5yvKjmrjuYSNsr5akorBhDhEz91uSxdHzo1/screenshot_8_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRQqFQeaFVqhtEjWHwPEjnGjK1mAbMvwJA9L3dQnPGS1F/screenshot_9_.png) I continued moving toward one of the wells through the residential sector, and finally I noticed two demons guarding this alleway. I took down this Rugged Walker in stealth, carefully striking when there was a Paper Doll right around the corner. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVH2bY7fNoX2TLkPuNhUE5dDygaFk2DmuqKdLzxBjbi86/screenshot_10_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWPaw8w7bbD1cdczShPnQtRahLPozM7FHtStoTBgrWgby/screenshot_11_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcJu2wsiq7Bu2vuqsDD7Yww4LxzzPC3x2bfwwiuZY3Mpn/screenshot_12_.png) Then first I took cover behind a wall that didn't let the demon see me while it drifted past. And then I took it down using a talisman, sticking the paper ward directly onto its spectral form to trigger a silent purge. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNuFWZ8EmBZ9iohcUDGVkJaq7xJ4Nwe2zHSSiS95xRmrk/screenshot_13_.png) I reached one of the wells that I found was heavily guarded by a small army of demon. There were some Paper Dolls, a Rain Walker, a Rugged Walker and there was a heavy Rage Walker as well patrolling the immediate perimeter. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSYcovH5QKu8V2aTBSMpTAJrANLoTbUmjDpvUkNUaHCYQ/screenshot_14_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVKXzyHb8M1WPsLQs8fn3NGbxEjYYTgRo5sSKsPheUHAm/screenshot_15_.png) I started attacking the Paper Dolls with fire element spells, exploiting their natural weakness to heat. I was taking them down from the roof safely when the other demons were walking right beside them, but they didn't understand a thing. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRL7uQcgXp1Kpqi3XSYpY2uHWtf4CZsvcT3weQvjTTrQv/screenshot_16_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdWfFe7gx2mnwBDH9a6guASWZEFWzoNvtZwBkbUU7PRP5/screenshot_17_.png) Then I decided to go for the Rage Walker when a Rain Walker and another the Rugged Walker was walking by the street below my vantage point. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXyVHaPGn9YfifAgBd5hxsv7S2xReyu9k6YmKpecsPx9b/screenshot_18_.png) When I was waiting for the perfect opportunity to take down the Rage Walker without triggering a massive street brawl, I noticed there was this Rainwalker guarding the path ahead closely. I had to wait for a moment there to find the perfect opportunity to strike. We'll continue in another post. --- **Thanks for reading. If you like my post, please follow, comment and upvote me. All the in-game screenshots are taken by me, just the games logo is borrowed from deviantart.** --- ▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=hrichakar/42412f13)

content.description: <div class=\

> While heading to the wells, a hidden enemy transformed into a deadly Lamentation, forcing me to use a Tengu grapple to recover on a roof before killing it. I then cleared out guarding Rugged Walkers and Paper Dolls using talismans and fire elements while avoiding patrolling Rainwalkers. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma4z2DVt9HiBsJWriu3u4WQeKRpVt3QG9xKwk3y4YLvCm/screenshot_1_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWCjbfudM5cJXanFTsaCVExuPzA4d9uJfQwfzsDFxkaZn/screenshot_2_.png) So I was going toward the wells to cleanse them of their spiritual corruption, but suddenly I was noticed by this Forlorn at a park. The spirit twisted violently, transformed into a Lamentation, and started chasing me down the paved path. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWGbsvD3XFgjpKT2AcfgrFr8NTNkJbYL5qenjQUfq3F59/screenshot_3_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWRpLtHaJQKioXsq6TVPbKN1UZC2sXSHYeJwnEY5JMwuF/screenshot_4_.png) These Lamentations are really scary and they are tough entities to fight in close quarters due to their screeching blasts. So I ran backwards to get some distance and then I tried to take it down from afar, hoping it wouldn't follow me up on a roof. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSP37NFba4whrc568LQTZzSbLcnesyd9TvoECZTLNGBHD/screenshot_5_.png) But while I was fighting it, getting close, as I got bored of just chipping away at its health bar from the street level, it started attacking me hardcore. I was almost dying on the asphalt, so I used a Tengu to grapple up and I got healed real fast. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmb719W6c7S6dT3GVawNi7YZyQsAJ4zX8xZmygvKKCY1yX/screenshot_6_.png) After I healed myself with my spectral energy supplies, I started attacking the demon from that roof, firing energy arrows down at its glowing core. At last, I got to take it down, watching its dark form dissolve. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXqcHb8Rjb4VdkLu9vfedneoSm9ZUD3MvC5ByJVYg6dku/screenshot_7_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPh79rDZhL5yvKjmrjuYSNsr5akorBhDhEz91uSxdHzo1/screenshot_8_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRQqFQeaFVqhtEjWHwPEjnGjK1mAbMvwJA9L3dQnPGS1F/screenshot_9_.png) I continued moving toward one of the wells through the residential sector, and finally I noticed two demons guarding this alleway. I took down this Rugged Walker in stealth, carefully striking when there was a Paper Doll right around the corner. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVH2bY7fNoX2TLkPuNhUE5dDygaFk2DmuqKdLzxBjbi86/screenshot_10_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWPaw8w7bbD1cdczShPnQtRahLPozM7FHtStoTBgrWgby/screenshot_11_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcJu2wsiq7Bu2vuqsDD7Yww4LxzzPC3x2bfwwiuZY3Mpn/screenshot_12_.png) Then first I took cover behind a wall that didn't let the demon see me while it drifted past. And then I took it down using a talisman, sticking the paper ward directly onto its spectral form to trigger a silent purge. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNuFWZ8EmBZ9iohcUDGVkJaq7xJ4Nwe2zHSSiS95xRmrk/screenshot_13_.png) I reached one of the wells that I found was heavily guarded by a small army of demon. There were some Paper Dolls, a Rain Walker, a Rugged Walker and there was a heavy Rage Walker as well patrolling the immediate perimeter. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSYcovH5QKu8V2aTBSMpTAJrANLoTbUmjDpvUkNUaHCYQ/screenshot_14_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVKXzyHb8M1WPsLQs8fn3NGbxEjYYTgRo5sSKsPheUHAm/screenshot_15_.png) I started attacking the Paper Dolls with fire element spells, exploiting their natural weakness to heat. I was taking them down from the roof safely when the other demons were walking right beside them, but they didn't understand a thing. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRL7uQcgXp1Kpqi3XSYpY2uHWtf4CZsvcT3weQvjTTrQv/screenshot_16_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdWfFe7gx2mnwBDH9a6guASWZEFWzoNvtZwBkbUU7PRP5/screenshot_17_.png) Then I decided to go for the Rage Walker when a Rain Walker and another the Rugged Walker was walking by the street below my vantage point. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXyVHaPGn9YfifAgBd5hxsv7S2xReyu9k6YmKpecsPx9b/screenshot_18_.png) When I was waiting for the perfect opportunity to take down the Rage Walker without triggering a massive street brawl, I noticed there was this Rainwalker guarding the path ahead closely. I had to wait for a moment there to find the perfect opportunity to strike. We'll continue in another post. --- **Thanks for reading. If you like my post, please follow, comment and upvote me. All the in-game screenshots are taken by me, just the games logo is borrowed from deviantart.**

title.title: The PTSD That Haunts Every Trader: Are You Still Scared of Losing Money?
title.body:
> There are times when certain events that happened to you in life would haunt you forever and that's when you know it is PTSD when a past event keeps on traumatizing you and you be holding yourself back from moving in over and over again.
I can tell I've had those PTSD that haunted me for weeks I just couldn't do anything about it but now I don't feel anything about it the same way like I used to. The PTSD is real when you're into stocks and crypto, like it'd terrorise you on a random day and you'd keep on thinking about it whenever you're going to make a decision.

the PTSD has ruined many traders

The bear market PTSD has haunted many traders that they have missed an entire bull run due to that fear of losing more money after making one wrong decision. I remember it was my first bear market when ftx, Luna collapsed and we went so down that everyone thought we'd never see sun shine onnus again. But the moment market startee showing up strength I had my doubts that I couldn't be real. It'd go down after a pump and that'd take whatever is left. That was the PTSD that has drowner many traders in an ocean depths. If I had to make choices again, it'd be those where I lacked because of that PTSD and I'd be so better place and position than I am today.

the only time you do better is when you feel nothing

Imagine having no PTSD, you'd outperform everyone you know just because your brain has no fear, you've no doubts and what ifs. It happened to me back in 2021 bull run when I had zero fears and started from zero. I did pulled over $10k from zero just by trading without any PTSD but lost it the following year when bear market started. And it brought so much PTSD that I still couldn't recover from it but now I do feel nothing about it and I guess that's what everyone needs To not feel anything at all and you'd be in peace while making decisions, it'd be more clear and you can just blame yourself if things went wrong again. I wonder if this PTSD is similar to those who were in wars, I could say it is close cause losing your networth also haunts as being in wars. But I believe we human are suppose to get over with it and own our PTSD, don't let it control you but you're the one making sure it guides you in a better way that's the only way for redemption in this economy. And I guess I have no more PTSD about markets, I could just start fresh and make decisions like there's no past, no history. You're just one day away from locking in and moving on from the things that quite scares you everyday. I wonder what's your opinion about it, do share in the comments.
that's all folks.
Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@idksamad78699/the-ptsd-that-haunts-every-trader-are-you-still-scared-of-losing-money-d26)

# Letra de El Caimán Chucuto Caimán que no tenga cola donde lo miren le dicen caimán chucuto y el hombre que es sinvergüenza siempre se agarra como mono en camoruco reventándose las uñas el dia que le echan un susto porque será que en el mundo habemos seres tan brutos yo trabajé largo tiempo casa de un rico llamado Carmelo Augusto su mujer tenía treinta años y el cincuenta pero bien gordo y robusto yo tan solo era un muchacho de quince años pero justo y un día que me pagó fallo me hizo coger un disgusto yo no quise retirarme porque al momento pensé mejor que un adulto yo sabía que don Carmelo tenía una hija bonita que regresaba de hiuston y al ver que todas sus notas las traía con veinte puntos empezó a toma aguardiente y mandó a buscar un conjunto me puso a amatar tres chivos quince gallinas un toro criollo y un bufalo yo noté que la muchacha se paró en la reunión al frente de todo el público y le dijo a su papá usted si es gafo y estúpido cantando y meneando el rabo se parece un caballo búlico será que usted no se acuerda que ha mi tío Pedro antier se llevó al sepulcro está bien canten y toquen pero no bailen consideren al difunto si usted sigue su bochinche dejaré quieto el asunto pero el día que usted se muera yo ni me visto de luto la señora de Carmelo cogió una pea con vino de ese alambrusco la muchacha lo hizo igual y de Carmelo ni se diga ni se supo corrieron a todo el mundo se fueron hasta los músicos y yo como era el obrero dejé para irme de último sería por el aguardiente que aquella noche me convertí en hombre astuto me metí a la habitación donde Carmelo y su esposa dormían como dos lechuzos le brinqué encima a la doña convertido en fiera y pulpo y lenguadiando decía Carmelo tu si eres rustico después le brinqué a Carmelo como un caballo cuando mira a un burro chuto todavía un poco furioso salí hacia la habitación donde estaba el otro fruto le dije entregue los lodos por las buenas y con gusto y me le lleva el coroto al novio que tiene en hiuston A las tres de la mañana cuando cantaban los gallos y guarracucos yo estaba con la muchacha bien enredado como alambre con bejuco despertó con unos lecos que se parecía un aruco y yo me perdí corriendo por la costa de un conuco don Carmelo y su señora se levantaron en piyamas sin guayucos diciendo este sinvergüenza cuando amanezca voy a su casa y lo busco la madre le dijo a la hija habla mi amor yo te escucho y le dijo siento madre algo que me duele mucho la mamá le contestó yo igual que tu me siento un dolor maluco mientras Carmelo decía que se sentía en la barriga como que tenía un furruco y cada viento en el baño sonaba como un trabuco y decía maldito sea tendré que comer caruto pero el igual que su hija perdió un tesoro que más nunca lo repuso con dolor y sentimiento me alejé de mi llanura buscando rumbo a Macuto con lágrimas en los ojos pensando a cada minuto que a Carmelo y su familia los cazó el caimán chucuto

echan un susto porque será que en el mundo habemos seres tan brutos yo trabajé largo tiempo casa de un rico llamado Carmelo Augusto su mujer tenía treinta años y el cincuenta pero bien gordo y robusto yo tan solo era un muchacho de quince años pero justo y un día que me pagó fallo me hizo coger un disgusto yo no quise retirarme porque al momento pensé mejor que un adulto yo sabía que don Carmelo tenía una hija bonita que regresaba de hiuston y al ver que todas sus notas las traía con veinte puntos empezó a toma aguardiente y mandó a buscar un conjunto me puso a amatar tres chivos quince gallinas un toro criollo y un bufalo yo noté que la muchacha se paró en la reunión al frente de todo el público y le dijo a su papá usted si es gafo y estúpido cantando y meneando el rabo se parece un caballo búlico será que usted no se acuerda que ha mi tío Pedro antier se llevó al sepulcro está bien canten y toquen pero no bailen consideren al difunto si usted sigue su bochinche dejaré quieto el asunto pero el día que usted se muera yo ni me visto de luto la señora de Carmelo cogió una pea con vino de ese alambrusco la muchacha lo hizo igual y de Carmelo ni se diga ni se supo corrieron a todo el mundo se fueron hasta los músicos y yo como era el obrero dejé para irme de último sería por el aguardiente que aquella noche me convertí en hombre astuto me metí a la habitación donde Carmelo y su esposa dormían como dos lechuzos le brinqué encima a la doña convertido en fiera y pulpo y lenguadiando decía Carmelo tu si eres rustico después le brinqué a Carmelo como un caballo cuando mira a un burro chuto todavía un poco furioso salí hacia la habitación donde estaba el otro fruto le dije entregue los lodos por las buenas y con gusto y me le lleva el coroto al novio que tiene en hiuston A las tres de la mañana cuando cantaban los gallos y guarracucos yo estaba con la muchacha bien enredado como alambre con bejuco despertó con unos lecos que se parecía un aruco y yo me perdí corriendo por la costa de un conuco don Carmelo y su señora se levantaron en piyamas sin guayucos diciendo este sinvergüenza cuando amanezca voy a su casa y lo busco la madre le dijo a la hija habla mi amor yo te escucho y le dijo siento madre algo que me duele mucho la mamá le contestó yo igual que tu me siento un dolor maluco mientras Carmelo decía que se sentía en la barriga como que tenía un furruco y cada viento en el baño sonaba como un trabuco y decía maldito sea tendré que comer caruto pero el igual que su hija perdió un tesoro que más nunca lo repuso con dolor y sentimiento me alejé de mi title.title: Rehearsals with Orchestra!
title.body: > Today is another historic day in my country, and since it's a musical event, I'll have the privilege not only of witnessing it but also of being a part of it. Richard Wagner's opera Parsifal has never been performed here in Venezuela before. This whole week has been very special. We've stepped outside our comfort zone, both vocally and from our usual routines like a cappella rehearsals or our regular rehearsal spaces. This week, we've literally joined forces with the symphony orchestra to become one great sound, and we've moved to what I consider the most glamorous theater in my country, the Teresa Carreño Theater in Caracas.

> ![IMG_20260520_155526.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23xARfHdUH7d8WusQ5C2KLKY5VEGp4J9pBoQMNDTiVFt3nQbpUVZzEmVB88LFh4NKwEvW.jpg) ![IMG_20260521_150058.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/EobzKSVbg5Yt5HYLJJhFPQtJCFBuV6KNh5CiBFBbjjLhCRwRGf55vkw1xPPQbfgVkpb.jpg)
I think this is the first time in 2026 that we've had such close contact with the orchestra, and I mean continuous days and so many hours of rehearsal. We have to do something minimal together at least once a month, but sharing with them always strengthens our bonds, or at least for shy people like me who usually only have a polite \

for them since I barely know them 🤭 I took advantage of the week to take many photographs, boldly wandering among the instruments during breaks, or taking some from my position, right behind the trumpet players, as you can see in the first photograph.

> ![IMG_20260521_142408.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23tveVzLGS1B6JuheCoNbP6t9m79Lx9qNNB6ZHLhiepLNtwAG2tUgdNrtWJ8vifE4FDEN.jpg) ![IMG_20260521_133425.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23vrtbKKjbCzcyWup6d32YSbjmH85VDiByqKBAkXnPefZy1Gb8kqfX62ZaTme22G67Mqe.jpg)
The lighting in the Rios Reyna Hall of the Teresa Carreño Theater has always captivated me, especially the contrast with the ceiling, creating breathtaking effects. For us singers, the tablets we use illuminate our faces, and the orchestra has small lamps over their scores, making every moment magical for the audience. But this is all part of the rehearsals, which begin very early in the morning. Everything presented tonight will be a true spectacle: the best orchestra and choir in our country accompanying internationally renowned musicians as special guests and professionals knowledgeable in Wagner's music. I'm sure that passion will overflow from everyone who is part of this event.

> ![IMG_20260520_152042.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23tRxFh9rQfzTYR3twcSHuVXSuMyGN86ukJoYr5E9oe9sMCBEU2JJe1ZMeaujh8KgdTCm.jpg) ![IMG_20260520_152121.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23w2cMnPaJ9jAMEXdaTknUTFrw9XagarerVVopLgVqRz556d66sCs1fUDoy5n1WHrvjpD.jpg)
The truth is, I've felt incredibly inspired all week. Throughout my career as a singer, I've had to perform short excerpts from Richard Wagner's operas, and I'm always musically satisfied, at least for the few hours it lasts. I enjoy it, since his works are often among the longest musical compositions. All that sound, combined with the inspiration of those who create the set design, makes for pure gold and an unforgettable experience. It should be for the audience, but when you love what you do so much, it's impossible to connect with everything else happening around you.

> ![IMG_20260520_150124.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23wgPziB6CxKwQTmJ6icHB5MVkKbRNH7Khgvz8DTZP2TodfG1JtyWJNgXotmv5pdgGbwj.jpg) ![IMG_20260520_132957.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23tmBFQC4tznNPTrvHemaY6hgXMVJjUymQBQh58FJBSdhXufECBpzrJJ5DSt6dLFsF1MD.jpg)
There's a peculiarity with this particular opera: the choir doesn't sing as much as we'd like. Almost the entire work focuses on the soloists; in fact, we don't sing even once in the second act, which causes some annoyance or distraction for the choir members. I can't say that everyone feels the same way about this production as I do; there are diverse opinions. But where I see a gap in my participation, I find another opportunity to harmonize with it, and part of that is these photos I'm sharing with you today, which are just a few that I loved from the many I took during the five days of rehearsals. Today is the concert, so I won't have another chance to photograph the beauty of the theater or the orchestra and conductor at work. Today is just a day to dress up and take selfies with friends 🤗 So, see you later! ✌️
![selfie teresa carreno.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23vhsGJX5Y7xdCd1tFGYWJ86VE9gf8QYtyLMeG6RMn6Gh6sLjrTAaRhCXD65ugCoBM4n5.png)

title.title: Think Before You Click
title.body:
/>

Online scams are on the rise these days with a lot more usage of internet for daily activities like shopping, banking, studies and communication. Online scams vary from fake links, phishing emails, hacking of social media accounts, online money frauds and a lot more.

Cyber crimes is an increasingly serious issue today and that's why it is important for everyone to be aware and protect their information and self from such frauds.

To save myself from falling prey to online scams, I try and practice some ways to keep myself safe online. First of all, I don't tend to click on links sent through a message, email or any social networking site which seems unknown to me.

Fake websites created by scammers which seem to be identical to real ones are created just to steal login details, passwords and financial information.

I double check the authenticity of a website by checking the URL carefully before I decide to access any website. I also use strong passwords for all my online accounts, which include letters, numbers, and special characters. I avoid using the same password for different accounts as it makes hacking of an account riskier.

Another measure that I have to save my account from fraudsters is enabling the two-factor authentication, which is commonly known as 2FA. It adds an extra layer of security by not only needing a password but also a verification code sent through your cell phone or email address if someone attempts to log in. Keeping my cell phone and computer up-to-date with the newest security software protects them from viruses and other malware.

Although I have never been a victim of an online fraud as major as scams I read about, I often receive mysterious text messages or emails saying I've won a lottery or that my bank account needs to be verified immediately or by pretending to be an employee of some bank or store. These messages usually ask for a one-time password or other private data that could be used by them. I instantly ignore such texts, delete and mark them as spam. This teaches me to stay alert.

In my opinion, phishing scams are the most threatening of all online frauds that happen today. Phishing scams include fake emails, websites or messages that usually appear to be coming from authentic sources.

These scams are very successful as they pretend to be sent from famous banks, shopping stores, government bodies etc. As soon as the victims enter their login details they lose their money or hack their accounts. Scams on social media are also becoming extremely prevalent especially for young ones who get easily persuaded to click links or trust new people.

My advice to everyone would be to be careful and think twice before sharing personal data online. Never share your passwords, OTP's, ATM PINs or bank account details with anyone even if they claim to be a part of some reliable organization.

One should also avoid downloading files from unfamiliar websites and get their transactions checked regularly for any fraudulent activities. Parents and teachers should educate children and students about cyber safety since knowledge is their only protection.

To conclude, scams have now become a significant threat and by keeping safe and learning precautions we can overcome this. Using strong passwords, not clicking suspicious links and verifying the authenticity of others we reduce the risk of being a victim to cybercrimes. Awareness will ultimately help in maintaining a better online environment for all.

</liketuimages>

在以前我经常会看到书本上面写的向日葵。在我的印象里面，向日葵是很大一朵。
虽然说向日葵是经常能看到介绍，但是实实在在的没有见过，到底是什么样子的？
今天经过一户小院的时候看见他们门口种了许多向日葵，才见到了真品。

其实，向日葵并没有我想象的那么大。我印象中的向日葵像是一个圆盘子那么大。
在固有的思维里面，我估计至少要20公分那么个直径。
但今天实际见到向日葵真的没有那么粗。满打满算顶多了，也就是14公分或者13公分的直径。

早上出去的时候，因为是下了雨，所以那向日葵是没有抬起头的。
等到中午下班时候经过的时候，那才真正看到他是真的是在向阳。
而且看方向好像真的是向着太阳的方向。真的是很神奇的一种植物。

因为这一家人，我之前也经过几次就没有去在意。以为是种的高粱或者是玉米。
顶了天了，最多是种的甘蔗。因为叶子都差不多是这样子。
但今天见到向日葵了，我才知道原来这几种植物的叶子长得很相似。

还有一个很奇怪的是，向日葵它竟然也像高粱一样长了一些麦穗的样子。
我不知道这种麦穗，它成熟之后是什么样的，有什么作用？
也不知道是不是瓜子，就是这些麦穗里面这些拿去炒出来的。

不过我现在是住在这里，以后他这些麦穗成熟了，也是能够看到的。
到时候我就可以看一下这些到底是怎么回事，难道会是种子？
植物真的很神奇。所以我偷偷的拍了他们家这些向日葵几张照片就溜了。

title.title: Monitoring Rural Nepal: Roads, Schools, and Hearts Rich Beyond Poverty \n
title.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTeFfYdtGXbSgwNkn7P9GupFC1h6t7rP9DpBxUdNyUkeP/img_7722.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYXDaARVWyGiHE8e3YTDNngrUMRtKe2VxhyKCQBjzqCFF/img_7693.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYWEh9Ta6StWdZvJ9GHe1iWU3215nshmcSywwKnbRYYdM/img_7708.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWesGHgARHGvGMJuhdU2r4KUSYKqZXFpa78oDdeCJXMKV/img_7724.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPTJ7WNGCguSzeNqe14weLnAKWgCGw1sm4WNeirWheV1s/img_7713.jpg)
Namaste from Madhyabindu Municipality! I work here as a local engineer, and a big part of my job involves getting out into the field to see how our municipal projects are actually coming along. Just recently, I joined an official project monitoring team led by our Deputy Mayor. Our goal was to head out for a final round of field inspections before clearing the paperwork for final project payments.

Our destination was Ward Number 14-a beautiful, incredibly rugged, and remote part of our municipality nestled deep in the hills. It was an eye-opening trip, and I wanted to share a look at what life and development really look like on the ground here.

The Road Reality: Every Rain Erases Progress

If you've ever traveled through the hills of Nepal, you know how breathtakingly beautiful they are. But as an engineer, I can tell you they are also incredibly unforgiving. The motorable routes connecting these remote villages are mostly unpaved, earthen dirt roads. Because the terrain is so fragile, a massive chunk of our municipal budget goes into a never-ending cycle: clearing away massive landslides and reshaping these tracks every single time the monsoon season hits.

Once the heavy summer rains fully set in, Ward 14 gets completely cut off from the rest of the world. It becomes an island where even rugged jeeps and motorbikes can't pass.

As planners, it forces us to face a really tough reality. We are looking at an isolated cluster of just 15 to 16 households. To give them a decent quality of life, the local government has to pour huge resources into basic infrastructure:

•  Carving out and maintaining roads
•  Building and supporting a local school
•  Setting up reliable water supply lines
•  Extending the electricity grid
When you break down the math, the cost per family is astronomically high. But leaving our own people entirely disconnected and forgotten just isn't an option.

 

 

A Primary School Lacking Basic Walls, High on Spirit

During our tour, we stopped by the local Ratna Rajya Laxmi Secondary School. Seeing the state of the classrooms was a heavy reminder of how much work we still have ahead of us. The infrastructure is incredibly bare-bones. Some of the classrooms are just unplastered, cold concrete walls with a few makeshift benches.

In another room, there aren't any desks or chairs at all. The younger kids sit right on a green carpet spread across the floor, leaning over tiny, plastic fold-up trays to practice their writing.

Yet, despite everything these kids lack, their energy and spirit are completely infectious. We happened to arrive right during their lunch break. All the students were sitting together out in the open courtyard, opening up their little metal tiffin boxes and naturally sharing whatever they had brought from home-mostly simple, comforting plates of dal bhat (rice and lentils), a little egg curry, or some green vegetables.

What really caught my heart was a stray dog standing right next to the lunch table, patiently watching the kids. Instead of shouting or chasing it away, the children kept tossing it bites of their own lunches. Materially, these families have so little, but these children have a generosity of spirit that makes them incredibly rich.

Painting the Gate: Pride in the Smallest Corners

Even with so many structural needs left unmet, you can see how much love the community has for this school. While we were there, a couple of local painters were on ladders transforming the front entrance gate with bright, joyful coats of yellow and blue paint.

They were carefully hand-painting an image of Goddess Saraswati-the Goddess of Knowledge-seated on her white swan right over the archway, alongside colorful murals of smiling students carrying their backpacks to school.

Over the years, different NGOs and international organizations have stepped in to help the school build proper toilets and take care of essential maintenance. That help is a lifeline, but seeing the community take ownership to make their school beautiful with their own hands shows you exactly where their values lie.

A Monitoring Lesson: Duty Over Sentiment

From an engineering perspective, the trip also brought a moment of raw accountability. We went to inspect a critical drainage and slope protection site, and right away, I noticed a major structural oversight. A heavy stone gabion wall had been built right in front of an existing hume pipe culvert, completely blocking the natural path of the water flow.

This wasn’t the work of an outsourced contractor trying to cut corners; it was built by a local user committee (Upabhokta Samiti) made up of the villagers themselves. They had poured their own time, sweat, and community pride into the project. They were completely focused on fulfilling the exact physical quantities listed in the Bill of Quantities (BOQ) so they could settle the project layout. Unfortunately, in their eagerness to get the work completed, they hadn't realized how the structure would fail functionally when the heavy rains hit.

The responsibility to address this fell squarely on my shoulders as the engineer on site. It was a decision I had to make with a very heavy heart. Looking at the eager, hopeful faces of the community members who had worked so hard, I felt an immense wave of public sympathy. You instinctively want to validate their physical effort and tell them they did a great job, but engineering laws don't bend for feelings. If left as it was, the blocked culvert would cause catastrophic flooding and wash out the very road they were trying to save during the monsoon.
I had to sit down with them, gently explain the hydraulic issue, and request the committee to dismantle the incorrect section to correct the mistake. At the end of the day, as tough and heartbreaking as it is to look into the eyes of locals and tell them to undo their hard work, duty comes first. Technical integrity and the long-term safety of the village have to come far ahead of temporary sentiments.
 
Time Pressure: Rushing Before the Clouds Break

We are currently moving through May, which means the clock is ticking incredibly fast for municipal engineers across Nepal. Our fiscal year wraps up around June and July, and any budget that isn't cleanly accounted for and finished will freeze.
We are under enormous pressure to push these infrastructure projects across the finish line before the monsoon rains completely take over and wash away our working window. It's a mad rush, but we have to move carefully. Every single rupee belongs to the public, and it needs to make a real difference in places like Ward 14.
 
Final Thought: Joy Resides in the Hills

If this field visit reminded me of anything, it's the beautiful resilience of the people who call these hills home.
Even when facing broken roads, unfinished classrooms, and the slow, grinding pace of rural development, the people here don't lose their warmth. They are so quick to offer a genuine smile, share their food, and look toward the future with hope.
True development might be a slow journey up these steep mountains, but the human spirit here is already standing right at the top.
Thank you so much for reading.

title.body:
<div class=text-justify>


![1000099888.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bestrakibul2/23tm9Fs3c75HCR2oxS76WrCeZ3XMc17JkNXdhUv4XPqjba3ZEEVgP8276LBNd876fB7BC.jpg)

Si quieres superarte, debes valorar el tiempo. Basta con hablar con las personas ricas y exitosas del mundo para comprobarlo. Para ellas, el tiempo era fundamental, y gracias a ello han logrado superarse.

Hay muchísimas personas ricas en el mundo que fueron muy pobres hace algún tiempo. Sin embargo, no pudieron mantener su posición por mucho tiempo. Siempre buscaron la manera de salir de esa situación.

Cuando tomaron la decisión de cambiar, con el tiempo, este esfuerzo extraordinario les ha llevado muy lejos y les ha permitido transformarse.



![1000099873.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bestrakibul2/23wMuHzwCDtRQvjSPpx6oUnvNSWxaktpNCiV5DShwxBmV88rFadL7EEEqx8GRVjb7E4oz.jpg)


He hablado con mucha gente que antes se dedicaba a la agricultura y cultivaba la tierra con vacas. Hoy en día, han invertido mucho dinero y tierras en la zona. Les pregunté el motivo de esta mejora. Me respondieron: \

. Si queremos superarnos, debemos ser conscientes de la importancia de la gestión del tiempo. Todos sabemos que si hacemos las cosas en el momento adecuado, tendremos éxito en la vida. Pero aún no hemos reconocido el poder que reside en nuestro interior. Seguimos ignorando ese poder que tenemos dentro y que puede hacer mucho por nosotros. Por eso, pasamos el día con pereza y no valoramos el tiempo. He escuchado historias de personas exitosas que siempre supieron valorar el tiempo. En este mundo, no podemos valorar un minuto ni un segundo. Pero créanme, es imposible imaginar cuánto vale un segundo. Si te estás ahogando en un río y te quedan cinco segundos, podrías dejar de respirar y morir. En ese momento, te darás cuenta de lo importantes que son cinco segundos para la vida. ![1000099880.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bestrakibul2/23z7SXKzNVFDRaUpsdW4t3MvRV4XQHuApVU9ZXcLvU3wk1KBCLk8UQTuPziU49iz2EYgE.jpg) Debemos aprender a valorar el tiempo en todos los aspectos de la vida. Si valoramos un segundo o un minuto, ese minuto nos impulsará hacia adelante en nuestro progreso. Hay quienes creen que lo que está escrito en nuestra frente o en nuestro destino se cumplirá automáticamente. Pero esto no es así. No podemos simplemente dejarnos llevar por el destino. Debemos alcanzar lo que está destinado para nosotros. Y para ello, debemos aprender a valorar el tiempo. El valor de cada segundo es inmenso. Si quieres mejorar tu situación, debes aprender a valorar cada segundo. Todas las personas que se han enriquecido y mejorado su posición le han dado un gran valor a cada segundo. Como resultado, hoy gozan de una mejor posición. Así que hoy quiero decirte: aprende a valorar el tiempo, comprende la gestión del tiempo y mejora tu situación. ![1000054243.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bestrakibul2/EoAUXZjGAPyY3oMMK4f3oHgNhH1gR25mTMmu7pBuiWx6a2eAfCbUiUbmkLz3qgzSuJv.png) # ENGLISH: ![1000099888.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bestrakibul2/23tm9Fs3c75HCR2oxS76WrCeZ3XMc17JkNXdhUv4XPqjba3ZEEVgP8276LBNd876fB7BC.jpg) If you want to improve yourself, you must value time. You can see by talking to all the rich and successful people in the world. They basically valued time the most and because of that they were able to improve themselves today. There are many, many rich people in the world. Who were very poor some time ago or some time ago. But they could not or did not maintain their position for a long time. They were always trying how to get out of this position. When they made a decision and over time they tried to change themselves. And this extraordinary effort for life has taken them very far ahead and they have changed themselves over time. ![1000099873.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bestrakibul2/23wMuHzwCDtRQvjSPpx6oUnvNSWxaktpNCiV5DShwxBmV88rFadL7EEEqx8GRVjb7E4oz.jpg) I have talked to many people. Who used to do agriculture and they used to cultivate the land with cows. But today they have bought a lot of money and land in the area. I asked them the reason for this improvement. People replied to me, learn to value time and you too can improve your position. If we want to improve ourselves then we must be aware of the issue of time management. We all need to know that if we do something at a certain time, we will be successful in our life. But we have not yet recognized the powerful soul within ourselves. We are still ignorant of the powerful soul that is inside us and that can do a lot for us. Due to which we pass the day lazily and cannot give any value to time. I have heard stories from those who have achieved success in life. They always know how to value time. In this world we cannot value a minute or a second. But believe me, it is impossible to imagine how much a second is worth in this world. When you are drowning in a river and you have five seconds left, you might stop breathing and die. At that moment, you will realize how important five seconds are for life. ![1000099880.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bestrakibul2/23z7SXKzNVFDRaUpsdW4t3MvRV4XQHuApVU9ZXcLvU3wk1KBCLk8UQTuPziU49iz2EYgE.jpg) We must learn to value time in every aspect of life. If we can value one second or one minute of time, then that one minute will take us forward for our progress. There are people who think that what is in our forehead or in our destiny will happen. But it can never be like this. We cannot just leave ourselves to our fate. We must achieve what is in our destiny. And for this, we must learn to value time. The value of every second is immense. If you want to improve your own position, then you must learn to value every second. All the people in this world who have become rich and improved their position have given a lot of value to every second. As a result, they have reached a better position today. title.title: Jeepney - More than a ride.
title.body:
/>

In the Philippines, the jeepney is more than just transportation.

For students, workers, and ordinary people trying to survive everyday life, it becomes a temporary resting place after long and exhausting days.

Every morning, jeepneys are filled with sleepy students carrying heavy bags and unfinished assignments. Some are reviewing notes before quizzes, while others are silently hoping their professor is absent. After classes, the same tired faces return, now carrying stress, deadlines, and the exhaustion of commuting under the heat.

But it is not only students.

Inside every jeepney are workers coming home from long shifts, parents thinking about responsibilities waiting for them at home, and people quietly dealing with battles nobody else knows about.

Sometimes, everyone inside is silent.

You just hear the engine, the sound of coins being passed while saying “bayad po,” and the noise of traffic outside. Yet somehow, despite the chaos, the jeepney feels comforting. For a few minutes, people get to sit down, breathe, rest their minds, or simply stare outside the window after a tiring day.

Filipino students especially know this feeling well.

The jeepney becomes the place where we recharge after sleepless nights, stressful group works, surprise recitations, and endless school requirements. Kahit siksikan, mainit, at traffic, there are still moments when the ride home feels peaceful.

And honestly, some of the funniest moments also happen there. From accidentally missing your stop because you fell asleep, hanggang sa pag-aabot ng bayad na parang chain reaction activity.

Life in the Philippines is not easy.

But the jeepney quietly reminds us that everyone is tired in different ways, and somehow, we are all just trying to get home and make it through another day.

title.title: Capítulo 5: La Visita del Vigilante
title.body:
>l repicar de la aldaba de hierro contra la madera de roble resonó en toda la planta baja, un sonido seco que pareció vibrar en los huesos de Ana. Al abrir la puerta, la figura espigada del Padre Thomas se recortaba contra la bruma grisácea que subía desde el canal. Su sonrisa era cordial, pero sus ojos, del color del acero frío, se movían con una agilidad inquietante, registrando cada rincón antes de dar el primer paso.
—Solo una visita de cortesía, Ana —dijo Thomas, dejando su sombrero sobre la mesa del vestíbulo—. En Ámsterdam, estas casas viejas suelen quejarse mucho cuando reciben inquilinos nuevos. Quería asegurarme de que el silencio no sea demasiado... pesado para ti.

### El recorrido por las sombras Thomas comenzó a caminar sin esperar invitación, moviéndose con una familiaridad que Ana no recordaba haberle otorgado. * **El Salón de los Retratos:** Entraron en la estancia principal. Las paredes estaban cubiertas de un papel tapiz de damasco tan oscuro que parecía absorber la luz de las velas. El padre se detuvo frente a un retrato de un mercader del siglo XVII cuya mirada parecía seguir cada movimiento. Thomas pasó un dedo por el marco dorado, retirando un rastro de polvo inexistente. * **El Pasillo de los Espejos:** Al subir a la primera planta, el pasillo se estrechaba. Los espejos enfrentados creaban un efecto de túnel infinito. Ana notó que Thomas no miraba su propio reflejo, sino que observaba fijamente el espacio vacío detrás de la imagen de Ana en el cristal. * **La Habitación de los Invitados:** Una alcoba con techos altísimos y vigas de madera carbonizada por un incendio antiguo. El aire aquí era notablemente más frío. Thomas se situó en el centro exacto de la habitación, cerrando los ojos por un segundo, como si escuchara un susurro proveniente de las tablas del suelo. ### Un diálogo entre sombras Thomas se detuvo frente a la ventana que daba al jardín trasero, un cuadrado de tierra yerma donde nada crecía. Ana se mantuvo cerca de la puerta, con las manos entrelazadas con fuerza. —Esta casa tiene una geometría peculiar, ¿no crees, Ana? —preguntó Thomas sin volverse—. Los ángulos no son del todo rectos. Si uno mira lo suficiente, parece que las paredes se inclinan hacia el centro, como si quisieran atrapar lo que sea que respire aquí dentro. —A veces siento que la casa me observa —admitió Ana, bajando la voz—. Como si esperara que yo cometiera un error. Thomas se giró lentamente. La luz mortecina de la tarde hacía que las cuencas de sus ojos parecieran pozos negros. —El error no es estar aquí, Ana. El error es creer que uno está solo. Dime, ¿has vuelto a oír el goteo en el ático? Ese sonido que no deja mancha de agua, pero que suena como... pasos constantes. Ana sintió un escalofrío. Ella nunca le había mencionado el ático. —¿Cómo sabe lo del sonido? —inquirió ella, dando un paso atrás. Thomas dio un paso hacia ella, acortando la distancia. Su voz bajó a un susurro que parecía vibrar en las paredes mismas. —Porque el primer inquilino no se fue por miedo a la oscuridad, sino por miedo a lo que la oscuridad le reveló sobre sí mismo. Ten cuidado con lo que buscas en los rincones olvidados de esta casa, hija mía. A veces, cuando uno llama a una puerta cerrada durante demasiado tiempo, algo del otro lado decide, finalmente, abrirla. Thomas le dedicó una última inclinación de cabeza, recuperó su sombrero y salió de la habitación, dejando tras de sí un intenso olor a incienso viejo y el eco de una advertencia que Ana sabía que no podría ignorar.

title.title: The softness of a red cloak on a familiar path
title.body: > While walking in front of the administrative building of our campus, my eyes suddenly caught my eye. As I walked a little further, I saw a beautiful jab flower tree; several gorgeous red jab flowers were blooming there. The flowers looked so beautiful in the crowd of green leaves that I had to stop there for a while. ![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmV6wsAcHyiUoH9Dqo5Z6MDLNnjD2HG2jcE4cXQeuJvd5A/image.png) These flowers are like a moment of absolute peace on the familiar streets of busy academic life. Every day, we pass in front of this building with so much haste; yet we do not even have the time to look at this small gift of nature. The petals of the flowers were absolutely fresh and vibrant, like the canvas of a skilled artist. The dark green leaves of the tree have brought out the red hue of the jab even more beautifully. ![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWJ8XFZKTXjdKmKwxqKK1TEeDAQJJzPXSD39aWifZ4niB/image.png) This beautiful scene instantly filled my mind with a strange feeling of well-being. Such natural beauty in the bosom of our familiar campus really creates a great contrast; on the one hand, the pressure of class assignments, and on the other, this gentle invitation of nature. Standing in front of the tree, I enjoyed this captivating form of nature and also took a picture of the beautiful jawa flower to keep in my memory. --- Location | DUET, Joydebpur ---|--- Photographer | @haideremtiaz --- --- Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@haideremti/the-softness-of-a-red-cloak-on-a-familiar-path-abw)
