body.title: Flowers - Petunia.
body.body:
Flowers - Petunia.
I was given a huge bouquet of flowers. It's so beautiful. I love it. I hung it in the gazebo. There's also a table and chairs in the gazebo. Now you can sit in the gazebo, drink coffee, and admire the flowers. It's not hot in the gazebo. And if it rains, it won't hit your head.
Petunias come in different colors. I was given purple and white ones. But they come in a variety of colors: pink, white, red, and other shades.
Petunias love watering, but they don't like being overwatered. They can be hung in a pot on the balcony, or they can be planted in the ground.

body.title: Out of Sight, Never Out of Mind
body.body:
People often hear me speak about my friends in a very interesting and connective way that makes friendship seem like one of the best things in the world, which I believe it is. I describe my relationship with them with sweet words that carry so much depth because they were my first true contact with learning how to love. With them, I’ve learned to be expressive, more loving, kind, and comfortable being myself.

https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdRwjbQJThzEgnkmKFBp6jT44VLmT9ZNuUa8kYnUHkE6L/1000408601.jpg

Many people might subscribe to the “out of sight is out of mind” notion but for me, that has never been the case. Whether I'm in close proximity with my friends or miles apart, the connection is always there and I miss them a whole lot, especially now that we’re adults with varying levels of personal responsibilities.

One of my closest male friends had his birthday celebration last week and I scheduled an email to send to him, and the very first thing he responded with was, “How far have you gone to have sent me an email on my birthday?” He continued with how much he loved that I never stopped thinking about him despite the distance and how lucky he was to have me in his corner. He ended that email with the most beautiful wishes for our friendship to bloom forever.

This interaction brought back memories of when he relocated out of the country to further his studies and eventually settled there. I cried so much and at the same time expressed how happy I was for his new life. He never failed to bring the good jokes to change every gloomy moment. He shared my feelings, comforted me, and assured me that no distance could break our relationship because we started out with a good foundation. True to his words, nothing has been able to sever the beautiful bond we share. We’re still friends who hold each other with a deep level of care.

https://img.leopedia.io/DQmexUemha5xjwkHJcHvyX4cDZsGpag1Jro6yLBRDBwCM62/1000408600.jpg

I miss this friend so much because they embody a lot of the qualities I desired in a close friendship. I miss their smiles, their laughter, their positive words, teachings, the times we stayed up late chatting about the funniest or most unimportant things, and of course, the banter between us at different times of the day. I miss our daily interactions where we had long conversations in the middle of work because in all those moments, love was felt.

These days, I still think about them a lot and I’m hoping that someday we’ll get to see each other and share all the hugs that we haven’t given each other in years. I truly can’t wait to hold their hands again and tell them how much I love them because their friendship with me will always be the thread that ties me to my emotions and gives me hope in this reckless, unpredictable experience called life.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmb93G9wX8yBpnnSpgdwegAioiTvZFuRjUie7yHU3FqeRe/1000344395.png 
 [Image 1 source](https://unsplash.com/photos/heart-shape-hand-illustration-JLNiQNntX4s)

|![20260518_225549.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EogQAbGGnWPJjFHuvA3adM8aJGszViF2tLzCyTT3bRZm3jQtNgsxqf5D12kj12jwKrJ.jpg)|![20260518_225553.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EoGzpiy3fVuet1nQxA7wMrUHghCmHQee9XTrPNZhjk13h4ZoNVA5mZzxHDAR6RLVYqh.jpg)|![20260518_225558.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/Eoc9tmZG4raN2x6NiCTpV58mYrm78uKbSQkmuS4ThXrrLpWPAScNmrnRB6dKToXcNDW.jpg)|

•✨️💜Continúo cosiendo el forro junto con la tela de blonda con costura de zigzag en los bordes externos y costura recta en la parte interna luego voy a coser los pliegues para dar volumen y espacio al busto y voy a coser justo en el medio con costura recta y voy a coser con la parte frontal inferior con costura recta y zigzag.
|![20260519_131655.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wqyTjVw5vGeravzRwqe5Wt4gFA29Tbbu4VwzxSqXSjcf6gsDnwFvRsLtyoCxUoSRzEW.jpg)|![20260519_132830.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23w31wr6iD31FcyN8GsF6ht5hAmbYB2CppeY6QauVdhdF4EkU1qgqVekKiXcxmjJ2rBcB.jpg)|![20260519_134732.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23y98cjj3kNjdtTogg5hRPXzNujGBeESdbhMtBrYaz7FCZTLEUthmBkxaLqGTfQN64rSp.jpg)|

|![20260519_134920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xexVLo3PXCNtUvit3ww1JSgzcpeRsWEGF4KXqAfVde32NciXzb2XoMVZF58NoX8MbBA.jpg)|![20260519_135206.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wXC921JfUhYyrUZRtiJJnT1x9GUNGDqnWoNHZnv3sfLmE7Ai3SFEwUpcB7a6DUdTUJE.jpg)|
|-|-|
•✨️💜Voy a coser con la parte trasera con costura recta y zigzag para asegurar continúo cerrando la manga con una costura recta y zigzag para asegurar luego las voy a coser al cuerpo de la camisa con una costura recta.

|![20260520_152530.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23vsayQKW2Fp7ybxezLGaaiG4yWhDUosvzu3a5jBQNucHMzbaB2kA3X4oz4LzuuEqoaUb.jpg)|![20260520_152758.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23x1L8LxTECYQ8aVVsEAyq82KV1M14jTHzBPQ7kqRvLsGghgi3TtvWSRWsVFgiKpEH9Gm.jpg)|![20260520_153540.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23vsdZubGf2iV5WyKA4cyWKofxm1Sv8yJwh7L2kYu9T8S6VPKRG7LcVGFj6LzyFFHvdSd.jpg)|
|-|-|-|




|![20260520_154036.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wMqCNif5Uf4KvGCeJNWEnVDAncK4oMduj5XsX7eX7mnm3Ecm1vi5SorwVyvFpBzVUBv.jpg)|![20260520_154434.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23ynfQD6cep8HNs4N5qvWZKApWQV4jJtSZqNRUHQmT8uXAEdUgfiicW6Z9QE1xJCwi37m.jpg)|
|-|-|



•✨️💜Voy asegurar con costura de zigzag y voy a coser con costura de zigzag la orilla superior e inferior y mangas para luego coser la elástica en la parte superior y mangas con costura recta mientras voy estirando y culmino cosiendo una trenza para un lazo frontal. 


|![20260520_154702.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xVXgd7ghTRzhUh9xcnXn18X2qkZj2r2UEkZzFNwkSRNDzCMFYpv8MiZzNGHN99fzRvz.jpg)|![20260520_160933.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xpKJLgMD9XHBvCZ2A1SYPkYTp8CLaTBzF4t2NJuQQv1k2YzNHsp3dRuUNVmzviutfo6.jpg)|![20260520_163626.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23u6HduQAJUQ4rxuV8YA8A9VmWaKVKaPw8Dk46UfBZXhJ6MWRhsVmAVx8zu2yQnnmaqpB.jpg)|
|-|-|-|




|![20260520_164735.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xVXyTMCWpk8ftu9cKeMtBt5tL74Yzs69ynRjm48SfNLFwWMtXMagQ3mkDrLgwjxa3zp.jpg)|![20260520_165351.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xAkVhHDuA6u9jpYciFLSuMLhvuUwC4eUXbT4ALaXNyZteKLXiLgEaA7ALo3b5cG2gDz.jpg)|![20260520_170203.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23x1MqHeFWeXXLwZzdPero1XajoyVjtuiUZT2XKcR2DUjMsgBqPageuhRETTE3ZyuMXtH.jpg)|
|-|-|-|

![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_124152_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EoeD4ZNgLbMwf6foVN9TvcTR2CCdYQJJPKp8r3Apm8DiLibcp5p5kc4GFqRFkLP4bJU.png)
</center>

Es un diseño muy bonito y delicado 🌸 sin duda alguna para lucir en una ocasión muy especial 💜🌸 me encantó mucho haber estado acá compartiendo con todos ustedes ✨️espero les guste mi post tutorial ❤️ saludos y muy buenas noches para todos queridos amigos de Hive ❤️. 

![20260520_183038.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wX3cudoYJwNsTbY8NdPmLVsCpfhUFypD2yHPk9cZ1SJ11RnsHWxmXcsmgK4NjrYZwgy.jpg)

![20260520_183046.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23vsUqo2jvPEpLUhriFJhh9qKSyNZXnJEHk8eAwEThQK8QjExMmpriHtNrkWBALLp4dex.jpg)

![20260520_183053.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wX3VHL774oTXQ27aNqAaQPa3edZn9ibKm219oJSXTCtCuT2Zrm4PPNyzs7CYTxkMaQn.jpg)




![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_125045_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EogLTkcA4KmHft4JF8jVTTFSkqG3xH7LXanTqYqm2Uj5N18eX3AaFxk87jpHWKysitL.png)

<center>![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_124403_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EoeD4ZNg21ofBWfyTJjE9oxYDN5E6NqrhcvfrPEpEDeZxXFhRvwbEP9xhStTF9kzZ83.png)</center>

Hello my dear Hive friends, I hope you're all doing well 👍🏻 Good evening everyone ✨️ It's a pleasure to greet you and share tonight with you 💜 I'm delighted to share a moment of pure creativity where I'll show you how to make a beautiful peasant-style lace blouse 🌸 Get comfortable and join me until the end.

![PhotoCollage_1779519106363.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EogQGcSCrcLxsvJf3Th6UhEgYy39MHvbAB2NnKd111SNQEraxF8hnm7KDzA23mLqfym.jpg)
<center>![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_124521_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EoeD4ZNgLsZrviZqdPsH7xDD7uLcVT8ok3iUD5LtWPJXPUQsgVdrTxMmpRxXsXRS4hF.png)</center> 

• 🧵Sewing machine 
• ✂️Scissors 
• 🧵Sewing thread 
• ✂️Fabric 
• 🧵Needle N°9



 <center>![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_124734_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EoeDQzxM1SGG8LqXYo2qXvLmwwH3hFcVRwvaA6yn2xJbP35dAMJXKMysNWoBF9EaQtY.png)</center>




•✨️💜I'm going to start by cutting all the pieces for my blouse: a back piece, a front piece divided into three, a lining for the upper front of the bust, and two sleeves. 


|![20260518_225549.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EogQAbGGnWPJjFHuvA3adM8aJGszViF2tLzCyTT3bRZm3jQtNgsxqf5D12kj12jwKrJ.jpg)|![20260518_225553.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EoGzpiy3fVuet1nQxA7wMrUHghCmHQee9XTrPNZhjk13h4ZoNVA5mZzxHDAR6RLVYqh.jpg)|![20260518_225558.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/Eoc9tmZG4raN2x6NiCTpV58mYrm78uKbSQkmuS4ThXrrLpWPAScNmrnRB6dKToXcNDW.jpg)|
|-|-|-|




•✨️💜I'll continue by sewing the lining to the lace fabric with a zigzag stitch on the outer edges and a straight stitch on the inner edges. Then I'll sew the pleats to give volume and space to the bust, and I'll sew right down the center with a straight stitch. Finally, I'll sew it to the lower front piece with a straight stitch and a zigzag stitch to secure it.

|![20260519_131655.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wqyTjVw5vGeravzRwqe5Wt4gFA29Tbbu4VwzxSqXSjcf6gsDnwFvRsLtyoCxUoSRzEW.jpg)|![20260519_132830.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23w31wr6iD31FcyN8GsF6ht5hAmbYB2CppeY6QauVdhdF4EkU1qgqVekKiXcxmjJ2rBcB.jpg)|![20260519_134732.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23y98cjj3kNjdtTogg5hRPXzNujGBeESdbhMtBrYaz7FCZTLEUthmBkxaLqGTfQN64rSp.jpg)|
|-|-|-|





|![20260519_134920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xexVLo3PXCNtUvit3ww1JSgzcpeRsWEGF4KXqAfVde32NciXzb2XoMVZF58NoX8MbBA.jpg)|![20260519_135206.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wXC921JfUhYyrUZRtiJJnT1x9GUNGDqnWoNHZnv3sfLmE7Ai3SFEwUpcB7a6DUdTUJE.jpg)|
|-|-|

 •✨️💜I'll sew it to the back piece with a straight stitch and a zigzag stitch to secure it. I'll then close the sleeves with a straight stitch and a zigzag stitch to secure them. Finally, I'll sew them to the body of the blouse with a straight stitch.

|![20260520_152530.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23vsayQKW2Fp7ybxezLGaaiG4yWhDUosvzu3a5jBQNucHMzbaB2kA3X4oz4LzuuEqoaUb.jpg)|![20260520_152758.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23x1L8LxTECYQ8aVVsEAyq82KV1M14jTHzBPQ7kqRvLsGghgi3TtvWSRWsVFgiKpEH9Gm.jpg)|![20260520_153540.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23vsdZubGf2iV5WyKA4cyWKofxm1Sv8yJwh7L2kYu9T8S6VPKRG7LcVGFj6LzyFFHvdSd.jpg)|
|-|-|-|




|![20260520_154036.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wMqCNif5Uf4KvGCeJNWEnVDAncK4oMduj5XsX7eX7mnm3Ecm1vi5SorwVyvFpBzVUBv.jpg)|![20260520_154434.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23ynfQD6cep8HNs4N5qvWZKApWQV4jJtSZqNRUHQmT8uXAEdUgfiicW6Z9QE1xJCwi37m.jpg)|

body.body:
https://youtu.be/o0BmhhhO9Uc?si=ggUVYGXEyZ5uoIzw

When we don’t understand something, the best thing we can do is wait and pay attention. Whenever God speaks to a person or a church, He gives them something specific to do. The question now is what has God asked you to do?

As believers, what has God called us to do together as a church? Everything we do should center towards what God has assigned us. Romans 8:26-29 reminds us that God has a plan for everyone who loves Him — and that plan is to become more and more like His Son Jesus Christ.

Right from the beginning, God wanted people to reflect who He is. But sin got in the way and spoilt the plan. But through Jesus, God made it possible for us to be restored. The moment we repent and give our lives to Jesus, we come back into God’s family and start the journey of becoming more like Christ every day of our lives.

But only those who truly identify with Christ can genuinely represent Him in the world.

# Learn AI Series (#75) - Multimodal Models - Text Meets Vision

### Solutions to Episode #74 Exercises

**Exercise 1:** Model comparison pipeline.

```python
import time
import random


class ModelComparer:
    \

def __init__(self, models, prompts):
        self.models = models
        self.prompts = prompts

    def run(self):
        results = {}
        for name, fn in self.models.items():
            timings = []
            lengths = []
            quality_scores = []

            for prompt in self.prompts:
                start = time.time()
                response = fn(prompt)
                elapsed = time.time() - start

                timings.append(elapsed)
                lengths.append(len(response.split()))

                # Quality: keywords + length + ends with punctuation
                keywords = set(
                    w.lower() for w in prompt.split()
                    if len(w) > 3
                )
                words = response.lower().split()
                kw_hits = sum(1 for w in words if w in keywords)
                kw_score = min(kw_hits / max(len(keywords), 1), 1.0)

                length_ok = 1.0 if 20 < len(words) < 200 else 0.3

The search + filter + sort chain is exactly how you navigate the real Hub. In practice, you almost never browse models randomly -- you filter by task first (what do I need this model to do?), then by library compatibility (does it work with my framework?), then sort by downloads or likes to find the community-vetted options. The model card method simulates what you should always read before downloading anything: license, size, training data, and intended use.

### On to today's episode

Here we go! For the past 20+ episodes we've been building up two separate tracks of understanding. On one side: text. NLP fundamentals (#30), word embeddings (#31), transformers (#52-53), GPT (#58), BERT (#59), fine-tuning (#69), the entire Hugging Face ecosystem (#74). On the other side: vision. CNNs from theory to practice (#45-46), applications like detection and segmentation (#47), and Vision Transformers (#54). These have been running in parallel, each powerful in its own domain.

But the most exciting work happening in AI right now is at the _intersection_. Models that can look at an image and reason about it in natural language. Models that understand both a photograph and its caption as representations of the same underlying concept. _That_ is what multimodal AI means, and it's where we're heading today ;-)

When you upload a photo to a vision-language model and ask \

-- something genuinely remarkable is happening under the hood. The model isn't doing image classificaton and then stitching text on top. It's processing both modalities simultaneously in a shared representation space, attending to visual features while generating language. Every component we've studied across 74 episodes contributes to making that work.

## The fundamental challenge: bridging modalities

Text and images are fundamentally different data types. Text is a sequence of discrete tokens (we covered this in depth in episode #72). An image is a 2D grid of continuous pixel values. A typical sentence might have 20 tokens. A 224x224 image has 150,528 pixel values (three color channels). How do you build a model that treats the sentence \

and a photograph of exactly that scene as representations of the _same concept_?

The answer -- and this is the core insight of the entire episode -- is **shared embedding spaces**. We introduced embeddings back in episode #63, where we mapped text into dense vector representations. The breakthrough in multimodal AI was extending this idea: learn an embedding space where images and text that describe similar things end up close together, regardless of which modality they came from.

Think of it as building a universal coordinate system. A photo of a cat and the words \
should map to nearly the same point in this coordinate system. A photo of a dog and the words \

should be far apart. That's the fundamental goal, and CLIP was the model that cracked it wide open.

## CLIP: the bridge between text and images

**CLIP** (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training, Radford et al., 2021) was a landmark. The architecture is straightforward -- almost deceptively simple:

```
Image  --> [Vision Encoder] --> image_embedding (512-dim)
                                       |
                              (should be similar for matching pairs)
                                       |
Text   --> [Text Encoder]   --> text_embedding  (512-dim)
```

Two separate encoders. A **Vision Transformer** (episode #54) processes the image. A **text transformer** processes the text. Both output embeddings in the same 512-dimensional space. Training uses **contrastive learning**: given a batch of image-text pairs, maximize the cosine similarity between matching pairs and minimize it for non-matching pairs.

```python
from transformers import CLIPModel, CLIPProcessor
from PIL import Image
import torch

model = CLIPModel.from_pretrained(\

, padding=True
)

with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**inputs)
    image_embeds = outputs.image_embeds   # (1, 512)
    text_embeds = outputs.text_embeds     # (4, 512)

# Cosine similarity between image and each text
similarities = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(
    image_embeds.unsqueeze(1),  # (1, 1, 512)
    text_embeds.unsqueeze(0),   # (1, 4, 512)
    dim=-1
)
for text, sim in zip(texts, similarities[0]):
    print(f\

)
# The dog descriptions will score highest
```

CLIP was trained on **400 million image-text pairs** scraped from the internet. The sheer scale of training data is what makes it work -- the model learns rich associations between visual concepts and their natural language descriptions across an enormous variety of contexts.

What makes CLIP truly remarkable (and what got everyone excited in 2021) is **zero-shot transfer**. Without any task-specific training, you can use CLIP for image classification by comparing an image's embedding to text embeddings of class descriptions:

```python
def zero_shot_classify(image, class_names, model, processor):
    \
\n    # Wrap class names in a prompt template\n    texts = [f\

for name in class_names]
    inputs = processor(
        text=texts, images=image,
        return_tensors=\

should be semantically close to images of dogs, because it learned that relationship from 400 million examples of people describing images on the internet. This is a fundamentally different approach from traditional computer vision classifiers (like the CNNs we built in episodes #45-46), which require labeled training data for every class they need to recognize.

_Why is this a big deal?_ Because traditional classifiers are limited to the classes they were trained on. A ResNet trained on ImageNet can classify 1,000 categories -- but if you need to distinguish between 5 types of industrial defects, you need to collect and label training data for those specific categories. CLIP can handle novel categories at inference time just by describing them in natural language. Having said that, CLIP's zero-shot accuracy on specialized domains (medical imaging, satellite photos, etc.) is typically lower than fine-tuned models. It's a generalist, not a specialist.

## Vision-language models: giving LLMs eyes

CLIP connects images and text in a shared embedding space, which is powerful for search and classification. But CLIP doesn't _generate_ text. It produces similarity scores. The next evolution: connect a vision encoder to a full language model, creating a system that can look at an image and have a conversation about it.

The general architecture of modern vision-language models (VLMs):

```
Image --> [Vision Encoder] --> image tokens --> [Projection] --> [LLM] --> text
                                                                  ^
                                                             text prompt
```

The vision encoder (typically a ViT, from episode #54) converts the image into a sequence of patch-level representations -- essentially \

A projection layer maps these into the language model's embedding space. Then the LLM processes both the image tokens and the text prompt together, generating a text response through the same autoregressive mechanism we studied in episode #58.

**LLaVA** (Large Language and Vision Assistant, Liu et al., 2023) demonstrated that this architecture works surprisingly well with a simple design:

1. Take a pretrained CLIP vision encoder (already understands images)
2. Take a pretrained language model like Llama or Vicuna (already understands language)
3. Connect them with a simple linear projection layer
4. Fine-tune on instruction-following data that includes images

```python
from transformers import (
    LlavaForConditionalGeneration, AutoProcessor
)
from PIL import Image
import torch

model = LlavaForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
    \

).to(model.device)

with torch.no_grad():
    output = model.generate(
        **inputs, max_new_tokens=300, temperature=0.7
    )

response = processor.decode(
    output[0], skip_special_tokens=True
)
print(response)
```

The key insight: you don't train the entire system from scratch. The vision encoder already understands images (from CLIP pre-training). The language model already understands language (from text pre-training). The projection layer just needs to learn how to map between these two well-trained representation spaces. This is why LLaVA works with a relatively small amount of multimodal fine-tuning data -- roughly 600K image-text instruction pairs, which is tiny compared to the billions of examples the individual components were trained on.

**BLIP-2** (Li et al., 2023) takes a slightly different approach by inserting a \

(Querying Transformer) between the vision encoder and the language model. The Q-Former learns a fixed set of query embeddings that extract the most relevant visual information from the image, in stead of passing all image tokens to the LLM. This is more compute-efficient -- fewer tokens flowing into the language model means faster inference:

```python
from transformers import (
    Blip2ForConditionalGeneration, Blip2Processor
)

blip_model = Blip2ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
    \

)

# Conditional captioning (guide the description)
inputs = blip_processor(
    images=image, text=\

)
```

Both architectures (LLaVA's direct projection and BLIP-2's Q-Former) work well in practice. The field is iterating rapidly on architectural details, but the core idea remains the same: pretrained vision + pretrained language + a learned connection layer.

## Visual question answering

**VQA** is the classic multimodal benchmark: given an image and a question, produce a correct answer. \

Early VQA systems (before 2020) used separate vision and language encoders with custom fusion layers -- quit some architectural complexity for what turned out to be mediocre results.

Modern VQA is handled by vision-language models directly. No special architecture needed -- just ask:

```python
def visual_qa(image_path, question, model, processor):
    \

    with torch.no_grad():
        output = model.generate(
            **inputs, max_new_tokens=100
        )

    full = processor.decode(
        output[0], skip_special_tokens=True
    )
    # Extract the answer after the prompt
    answer = full.split(question)[-1].strip()
    return answer


# Examples
print(visual_qa(
    \

,
    model, processor
))
```

That last example -- using a VLM to read error messages from screenshots -- is particularly practical. Think about it: automated bug reporting, accessibility tools for visually impaired users, customer support where the user sends a screenshot of their problem. These are real applications that combine OCR-level text recognition with semantic understanding of what the error _means_.

## Image captioning and dense description

Image captioning goes the other direction: given an image, generate a natural language description. This might sound simple but it requires understanding objects, their spatial relationships, actions being performed, and sometimes context that isn't directly visible (like time of day from lighting).

Practical applications are everywhere: automatic alt-text generation for web accessibility (this alone is a massive use case -- the web is full of images with no alt text), image search indexing, content moderation (describe what's in an image to check against policies), photo library organization, and generating training data for other models.

The quality of captions has improved dramatically. Early models (2015-2018) would produce generic descriptions like \

The difference is transformers + scale + better training data. The same story we've seen throughout this entire series ;-)

## Grounded generation: pointing at things

Standard VQA tells you \

**Grounded generation** tells you _exactly where_: it outputs bounding box coordinates along with the text description. This bridges the gap between understanding (knowing what's in the image) and localization (knowing where it is).

```python

output = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024)

result = processor.post_process_generation(
    processor.decode(output[0], skip_special_tokens=True),
    task=\

), document processing (locate specific fields in forms and invoices), and autonomous driving (where exactly is that pedestrian relative to the car?).\n\n**Florence-2** from Microsoft is worth knowing about because it handles multiple vision tasks (captioning, detection, segmentation, OCR) through a single unified architecture. You just change the task prompt. This is the \

approach applied to vision -- one model, many tasks. A part from Florence-2, there's also **Grounding DINO** and **SAM** (Segment Anything Model) which handle grounded detection and segmentation respectively.

## Building a multimodal analysis tool

Let's combine everything into a practical image analysis class that you could actually use in a project:

```python

    LlavaForConditionalGeneration, AutoProcessor
)
from PIL import Image
import torch


class ImageAnalyzer:

# Usage examples
analyzer = ImageAnalyzer()

# Describe what you see
print(analyzer.describe(\

)
```

This is a straightforward tool, but stop and think about what's actually happening: a single model architecture understands images, reads text within images, reasons about visual content, and generates coherent natural language responses. Every building block we've covered across 75 episodes is at work here -- CNNs and ViTs for visual feature extraction, transformers for language generation, embeddings for shared representations, attention mechanisms for connecting it all together, and the Hugging Face ecosystem (episode #74) for making it accessible with a few lines of code.

## The contrastive learning mechanism

We should look a bit deeper into how CLIP's training actually works, because contrastive learning is the secret sauce behind most multimodal models and it connects directly to the embedding concepts from episode #63.

Given a batch of N image-text pairs, CLIP creates an N x N similarity matrix. The diagonal entries are the matching pairs (image_i with text_i). Everything off-diagonal is a negative pair. Training maximizes the diagonal similarities while minimizing the off-diagonal ones:

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def contrastive_loss(image_features, text_features,
                     temperature=0.07):
    \

# Cosine similarity matrix: (batch, batch)
    logits = (image_features @ text_features.T) / temperature

    # Labels: diagonal entries are the matching pairs
    batch_size = logits.shape[0]
    labels = torch.arange(batch_size)

    # Symmetric loss: image-to-text AND text-to-image
    loss_i2t = F.cross_entropy(logits, labels)
    loss_t2i = F.cross_entropy(logits.T, labels)

    return (loss_i2t + loss_t2i) / 2


# Demo with simulated embeddings
batch_size = 8
embed_dim = 512

# Pretend these come from vision and text encoders
image_emb = F.normalize(
    torch.randn(batch_size, embed_dim), dim=-1
)
text_emb = F.normalize(
    torch.randn(batch_size, embed_dim), dim=-1
)

loss = contrastive_loss(image_emb, text_emb)
print(f\

the similarity distribution is. Lower temperature makes the model more confident in its distinctions (similar to what we saw in episode #71 with text generation temperature). The value of 0.07 that CLIP uses is learned during training -- it's actually a trainable parameter, not a fixed hyperparameter.

The **symmetric loss** is important: we want image_i to find text_i (image-to-text retrieval) AND we want text_i to find image_i (text-to-image retrieval). Both directions matter because a good shared space supports search in either direction.

The reason contrastive learning scales so well is that every non-matching pair in the batch serves as a negative example. With a batch size of 32,768 (which CLIP used), each positive pair has 32,767 negatives to contrast against. That's an enormous amount of training signal from each batch, and it's \

-- you don't need explicit negative examples, the batch structure provides them.

## Limitations and what to watch for

Multimodal models are powerful but they have real limitations that you need to understand before deploying them:

**Hallucination**: VLMs can confidently describe objects that aren't in the image. If you ask \
and there's no hat, many models will invent one rather than saying \

This is the same hallucination problem we discussed in episode #73 (evaluation), but it's harder to catch in the visual domain because verifying visual claims requires looking at the image yourself.\n\n**Spatial reasoning**: current VLMs struggle with precise spatial relationships. \

body.title: I Survived The Illness, But The Fear, Trauma And Memories Never Completely Left Me.
body.body:
Huhm, this is so deep, at least for me, it is. More like a very personal topic, but I will try my best to not sound too emotional and all.



![1000089710.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marsdave/EpLeXqH8kVcTvEYyrAg91rb5zzDjK2aUpqpg4Du2vqzM6w5dj1iZJLEAGju2vKa6fgn.jpg)



 So, before I had the health issue I had some few years back, all my thought was always that PTSD/trauma is something people have or develop after they've went through or experienced a war, some sort of violence, accidents and the likes. I never knew or understood that it goes beyond just those.



So, talking of the illness I had then, it was a very challenging one. One that I can say even I don't believe I will survive. Had to experience and undergo about seven surgeries, not talk of the various medications, injections, tests, blood samples, money issues, the thought of being a burden, fear and all. It was indeed a trying time for me and my family. And even when I got better and was discharged, my mind refuses to be better and heal up. And in all honesty, I still panic till today, especially when I feel some sort of pain, or perceive a kind of smell and all, those little things often take my mind back in time to those times I was bedridden.






Sometimes last year, I remembery brother asking me a question, it was a simple question, but to me, it's big. He asked, *\

* he asked enh, you will think he asked more than that, because the way that question hits me, huhm.. it is well. 



![1000089681.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marsdave/23y8yoouSGv9uGZWTamndiq37KhLRm8qTnvV9hCjQ2bJjmJSffhn1wW6xwzWB7mML5Gu4.jpg)






And its been a while anyone asked me such a question regarding my health, most people believe since I'm out of the hospital and living my life then everything has returned to the way it is. But Yoruba do say something, that is, *\

* Which is true.






So, talking of trauma, it is something I still experience. Sometimes I just remember certain things and begin to feel somehow, other times I'm just scared for no reason at all, at times I just start to think and think and think. Sometimes I even blame myself and feel guilty when I remember what my parents and siblings have to go through just for me to remain alive.



All thanks to God though, there's a lot of difference now, not as if its totally gone cause I won't want to come here and lie. But is has reduced greatly, and I'm thankful for the support from my parents and siblings, I'm thankful for those who always listen to me and allow me let it all out. It has helped me a lot. 



![1000718621.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marsdave/23xVM1nY3TXzWNcVxoPTottsozt9nmPkfqg1M8d7vKGoyPecmM18KuyuR6ZvBFo2MdVGF.jpg)



And even though I couldn't do certain things, I'm grateful for the little I can do, also the little I'm doing to help others as well has raised my hope that my life still has meaning and that I'm definitely here/still alive for a reason.




PTSD/Trauma is real, and its something a lot of us are going through silently. Just that each person's own is born out of different situations and happenings. A lot of people you see looking all good and fine are struggling mentally and emotionally, so let's be more kinder to people. Support, prayers, kindness, a smile, patience and such are what helps them to heal.


So, here as I conclude, I will love to put it to you too...
How are you?


🌹

**Images are mine.**

**Thanks a lot for taking your time to read through, kindly do well to stop by my blog @marsdave for more exclusive and amazing content.**

Soy la dueña de mi vida y de cada uno de los instantes que pueda disfrutar, de mirar la vida con alegría. Yo soy el dueño de los instantes que puedan atraer la alegría a este mundo, de la información que nos aqueja diariamente, de las noticias no tan buenas y de sentirme bien este donde este pisando.


<center>![imagen.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaWq6GS62PrApQdmQ4Q9na6hu9wWxRJrmihM9WVFsN9qA/imagen.png)</center>


Puedo sentirme mal, por unos instantes pero eso no es del diario de mi vida. Surgen siempre lo mejor por mirar y pensando que vendrán siempre tiempos mejores. Yo la dueña de lo que quiero ser en el futuro, sin dolores, ni quejas. De no afectar la vida de otros y volviéndome parte importante de sus alegrías. Soy la dueña de las fotos, de los recuerdos que atesoro en cada momento y cuento sus historias. ¿Qué valioso se vuelve todo, cuando aprendemos a mirarla con alegría?

Yo sigo pensando que todavía soy la dueña de los valores que he recibido a lo largo de la vida. De mis momentos más especiales y los comparto porque me alegran el día.

I am the master of my life and of every moment I can enjoy, of looking at life with joy. I am the master of the moments that can bring joy to this world, of the information that plagues us daily, of the not-so-good news, and of feeling good wherever I am.

I might feel down for a few moments, but that's not part of my daily life. The best always emerges when I look forward to it, believing that better times are always ahead. I am the master of who I want to be in the future, without pain or complaints. I strive not to negatively impact the lives of others and instead become an important part of their joy. I own the photos, the memories I treasure in every moment, and I share their stories. How precious everything becomes when we learn to see it with joy!

I still believe I am the master of the values ​​I've received throughout my life. I share my most special moments because they brighten my day.

body.body: <div  class=text-justify>\n\nWhen I started listening to podcasts, one of the first I listened to said something that has stayed with me since then. He was giving the road map to changing one's life and one particular step he gave at the beginning of the list was *\

I feel more confident about myself but I'm still scared.\n\nWhile I was thinking of what to share today, I came across a prompt question that hit me way harder than it may have been supposed to hit anyone. body.title: Homemade machamche beeguni and egg chop for afternoon snack.
body.body:
> ![IMG20250321164257~2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPSQTwKx4pCRPoNTP3MgeNGpoVFHm1GS61JWB45oN1pgd/IMG20250321164257~2.jpg) My sincere greetings to everyone. I hope everyone is well. Whenever I get some time in the midst of my daily busy schedule, I like to make something new for afternoon snack. The taste of a homemade hot breakfast is different from the unhealthy food from outside shops. This afternoon, I suddenly felt like making two traditional Bengali iftar or afternoon snack. So I quickly made everyone's favorite egg chop and machamche beeguni. Today I am sharing that cooking experience and some pictures with you. ![IMG20250321164349~2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmck15TKdP4dNiQUSmBtyaxQ1cJBsp1m1HBQFkuxBXdgpE/IMG20250321164349~2.jpg) Egg chop is a very favorite dish of everyone, young and old. To make it, I first boiled potatoes and grated them well. Then I made a potato mixture with fried onion, chopped green chili, coriander leaves, chaat masala and a little garam masala. I boiled and chopped eggs as the inner filling. After coating the eggs with potato starch and giving them a beautiful oval shape, it was time for coating. First, I rolled the chops in a little flour, dipped them in the beaten egg, and finally coated them well in breadcrumbs or biscuit crumbs. The wonderful aroma that came out while heating the oil in a pan and frying them until golden brown in the oil, half of my hunger was satisfied! After placing them in the basket, they were as crispy as they looked and tasted great. After frying the egg chops, I started preparing the beeguni. Our afternoon chat or Ramadan iftar is incomplete without beeguni. The main secret to making perfect beeguni lies in its besan ball. ![IMG20250321161542~2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYzH8YPPmgNUbnstmNpXL29Ch1fcdwr7p231KgXAVQCZk/IMG20250321161542~2.jpg) I made a thick batter by mixing besan with a little rice powder, black cumin, turmeric-chili powder, ginger-garlic paste, and a little baking powder. I cut the eggplants into thin slices and sprinkled them with a little salt. Then, I dipped each eggplant piece in the gram flour and dropped it in the hot oil, and they puffed up beautifully. I fried them until they were perfectly golden and crispy. The aroma of the grill filling the house and the hot egg chops and purple curry arranged on the plate are all that is needed to make the afternoon tea conversation come alive. The joy of eating this hot breakfast together with the whole family is different. The taste of this home-made food in a healthy way was in no way inferior to the store-bought one. ___ |

One of the topic of discussion during money2020 Asia was PlatON agentic payment solution which reads,

> Powered by Nexus, a programmable clearing layer, the solution enables any LLM agent to autonomously discover services, negotiate structured quotes, and settle on-chain payments in real time.

Imagine having to host a 50 persons meetup with zero to no idea on where or how to start, using the above solution it helps to scout on available services, merchants, and also complete in real time payment via stable onchain solutions all within your desired location.

This isn't just a game changer but it's changing the entirety of how events are planned and PlatON is at the forefront of this.

For new and trending information on how Nexus is changing the game, then ensure you turn on notifications on PlatON related media page to get every news as it comes by.

body.title: Epistaixs( nasal bleeding): causes and management
body.body:
**Definition**

Epistaxis simply refers bleeding from the nose or into the nasal cavity. It is a common condition in all the age groups and often presents as a medical emergency. Nasal bleeding is a sign and not a disease so every attempts should be made to find the cause of the bleed.

_Causes of epistaxis_

The causes of epistaxis can be broadly classified into local and systemic causes.

a) Local causes:

i) Trauma: nose picking resulting in fingernail trauma, injuries to nose, facial fracture, hard blowing of nose

ii) Infections: rhinitis, sinusitis, nasal diphtheria and granulomatous conditions of the nose

iii)Foreign bodies: maggots, leeches, beans and metals in nasal cavity of child resulting in rhinolith

iv) Anatomical deformities: Deviated nasal septum and nasal spurs

v) Drugs: decongestants, topical steroids and

vi) Tumors like angiofibroma and nasopharyngeal carcinoma

b) Systemic causes: hypertension, renal failure, pregnancy, liver cirrhosis, hemophilia, vitamin K deficiency

**Brief anatomy of nose**

Nasal cavity is rich in vasculature. The blood supply runs just under the nasal mucosa making it prone to trauma.

​

![ \

](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW2CRF7LRBoqtovrgdjHV4uxYyQXtMWMNeT9JV2HkKeBQ/Nose__bleed__vessels.jpg) Image source: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK435997/figure/article-21259.image.f2/?report=objectonly

In majority of cases bleeding occurs through the Little's area also known as Keisselbach's plexus. It is the prominent plexus of vessels just under the nasal mucosa in anterioinferior part of the nasal septum.

**Relationship between hypertension and epistaxis:**

Since a long period of time, hypertension was considered as the major cause of nasal bleed, but a large number of studies failed to show a direct relationship between hypertension and epistaxis. Even though it lacks direct causal elevated blood pressure is seen in almost all cases of epistaxis admissions which may be due to the anxiety associated with hospital admissions.

**Relationship between epistaxis and septal deviation:**

Septal deviation is seen in around 70% of the general population. Due to this high prevalence of septal deviation, the high prevalence of epistaxis and deviated septum may be just a coincidence. There is no clear case controlled evidence found in the literature regarding the septal deviation as the cause of epistaxis.

_**Management of epistaxis**_

Resuscitation:

If the patient presents with active bleeding, first of al make comfortable and follow the incremental order of sequences.

Most patients present with anterior epistaxis so just pinching the ala of the nose makes sense. Itcompresses the vessels in the keisslebach's plexus and stops the bleeding.

Simultaneously, the forehead and dorsum of the nose should be compressed with an ice pack in order to induce vasoconstriction.

​

![ \

](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSATwfHRSAox9nnbfKDPYY3KH1B5hfQQs356axyzTAdeG/Picture1.jpg)

​

​

The patients's nasal cavity must be examined with the use of cotton pledgets soaked in vasoconstrictor solutions like oxymetazoline and adrenaline and kept insitu for about 5 minutes.

![ \

](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaTQp4PMsrojm1Azbq7aYegWEMvG1uDuUUP6bm1JbTvjg/Screenshot_20260523-111727_3.png)

If the bleeder is not localized, we can pack the nasal cavities by using a ribbon gauze impregnated with topical antibiotic and kept insitu for 48-72 hours and reassess the patients. If the bleeding is controlled by these measures we can safely discharge the patients but if the bleeding continues despite these measures we have to shift the patient to the operation theatre for surgical interventions.

 That's all for today. I hope this post about nasal bleed helps for the management of nasal bleed in the community settings. 

Consent taken from the patient for use in articles and blogs.

**References **

1) https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK435997/ 2) https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/13464-nosebleed-epistaxis 3) Scott Brown's otorhinolaryngoly and Head and Neck Surgery 8th edition

body.title: Wir haben Wohnungsmangel in den Staedten, weil die alten kinderlosen Boomer Omas mit ihren Katzen die drei Zimmer Buden besetzen!
body.body:
Und jeden unsinnigen Handwerkerbesuch feiern, weil dann endlich mal was maennliches im Haus ist und abwinken, was auch immer die Aufschreiben und fuer Schwachsinnsarbeiten abrechnen lassen.

Die Katzenomas der Boomer Generation, sitzen hier im Block, auf der Lauer, am Fenster, und laufen jungen Maennern hinterher wenn die das Haus verlassen.

Die Familien, sind ja Laut, Teuer, weil man auch wirklich mal was reparieren muss und winken sicher nicht jeden Spaß ab, der auf den Rechnungen steht.

Man gibt aber lieber den Auslaendern die Schuld, und natuerlich uns Armen, das die Wohnunglage so beschissen ist in den Staedten.

Aber von Mittag bis Zwoelf nicht gedacht, sind es die Wohnungsbaugesellschaften, die solche KatzenOmas liebend gerne bevorzugen in die drei Zimmer Palaeste zu holen, statt Familien mit Kindern die drei Zimmer zum Leben zu lassen.

Das ist einfach eine Geld/Aufwandsgeschichte und kommt mir keiner mit was anderem ich habe das hier drei Jahre in Berlin analysiert, weil es mir schon sehr Schnell, auch an meiner tollen hier aufgefallen ist.

Hier wohnt genau ein Kind im Haus, EINS. Ein weiteres Paarchen und der Rest, sind Omas, die machen die anderen drei Stockwerke von vier voll.

So sieht das aus.

Die Wohnungsbaugesellschaften und deren Nassauer an Handwerkerzunft verdienen sich damit eine golden Nase.

Und der Normalbuerger schimpft auf die Falschen.

Aendere meine Meinung, oder denke mal drueber nach.

Salve

body.title: Hardcore Townsmen! #4 Industrial Ambition [ENG🇬🇧|ESP🇻🇪]
body.body:
> Hello Hive Gamers! Today I bring you the 4th part of my hardcore adventure in Townsmen. After the chaotic events of the previous session, where the bandits and fires almost paralyzed my entire textile industry, I realized that I couldn't keep all my eggs in one basket. Relying solely on wool was a strategic mistake that I am now trying to rectify. # ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmT5ZumsGAgizct6qf4KoJc5ecvHaetEK9SwSzH4cTvJgF/1779518595397.jpg) I decided to make a necessary but high-risk investment: starting the production of gold and iron ingots. To achieve this, I need a smelting plant, but as many of you know, these facilities demand a constant supply of coal. Therefore, my first move was to build a charcoal kiln. In a normal game, this is a relatively cheap building, but in this hardcore run, every plank and every coin counts double. Gathering the materials and the money in this frozen wasteland is a nightmare, but we managed to get it running. # The kiln started producing coal without any issues, using the excess firewood I have in stock. With the fuel secured, I moved on to the construction of the smelter. Fortunately, it doesn't require overly complex materials. This successfully kicked off a steady production of ingots, which I plan to sell to the merchant at a much better price than raw materials. I urgently need that cash flow to equip my city guard with better weapons and, more importantly, to provide more food and basic services to the population. Managing needs in this eternal winter is proving to be a brutal task. # ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWiJsi97YDLC6K5BYtreuxb1hSTh8smn5r1Vegv2SHBVv/1779518608994.jpg) However, as is typical in this hardcore run, when one problem is solved, a worse one appears. Just as the smelter was heating up, I received the worst news possible: the natural iron deposits in the mines have been completely exhausted. I have almost no raw material left for the smelting process. Now I’m in a race against time; I need to build a new mine immediately or devise a creative solution before my new industrial heart stops beating. Between the cold, the bandits, and the lack of iron, it seems the game really wants to see my townnies disappear. # ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTKW7ie7Qyf5YWc5GaAyK8DmYDhGY8tyy1aS7YZguy33b/1779518621580.jpg) |
Español
| |-| ------

> ¡Hola Gamers de Hive! Hoy les traigo la 4ta parte de mi aventura hardcore en Townsmen. Tras los eventos caóticos de la sesión anterior, donde los bandidos y los incendios casi paralizan toda mi industria textil, me di cuenta de que no puedo poner todos los huevos en la misma canasta. Depender únicamente de la lana fue un error estratégico que ahora estoy intentando rectificar. # Decidí hacer una inversión necesaria pero de alto riesgo: iniciar la producción de lingotes de oro y hierro. Para lograr esto, necesito una fundición, pero como muchos saben, estas instalaciones exigen un suministro constante de carbón. Por lo tanto, mi primer movimiento fue construir una carbonera. En una partida normal, este es un edificio relativamente barato, pero en este reto hardcore, cada tablón y cada moneda cuenta el doble. Reunir los materiales y el dinero en este páramo helado es una pesadilla, pero logramos ponerlo en marcha. # ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdgUnfr7RKg3v76V3SwyydAfrwgUaLR6N3p81zGbBq92Q/1779518721740.jpg) La carbonera inició la producción de carbón sin mayores obstáculos, utilizando la leña que me sobra en los almacenes. Con el combustible asegurado, procedí a la construcción de la fundición. Afortunadamente, no requiere materiales demasiado complejos. Esto inició con éxito una fabricación constante de lingotes, los cuales planeo vender al mercader a un precio mucho mejor que la materia prima. Necesito urgentemente ese flujo de dinero para equipar a mi guardia de la ciudad con mejores armas y, lo más importante, ofrecer más comida y servicios básicos a la población. Gestionar las necesidades en este invierno eterno está resultando ser una tarea brutal. # Sin embargo, como es típico en esta partida, cuando se resuelve un problema, aparece uno peor. Justo cuando la fundición estaba calentando motores, recibí la peor noticia posible: los depósitos naturales de las minas de hierro se han agotado por completo. No me queda casi materia prima para el proceso de fundición. Ahora estoy en una carrera contra el tiempo; necesito crear otra mina rápidamente o idear alguna solución creativa antes de que mi nuevo corazón industrial deje de latir. Entre el frío, los bandidos y la falta de hierro, parece que el juego realmente quiere ver a mis townnies desaparecer. ------ ---- |

body.title: A prompt that made me check myself / Un prompt que me hizo revisarme - LOH contest week #289 (eng-esp)
body.body:
Hi, girls.

@cautiva-30 always brings up topics that seem harmless, but when I start thinking about how to respond, I realize the depth of the issue. Today is no different. I've suddenly become aware of how many things I've convinced myself I'm doing for myself, when in reality I'm doing them to please or not disappoint someone.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNZUHq8br1DinZA1KkFLXK2hrknx43XhPqjJbxK9MLFud/1779518134692.jpg)

Yes, it's true that I don't do anything I don't want to do. It's also true that even if I do something to please or not disappoint someone, it doesn't mean I'm doing it for myself.

And the reason I do that is simple: sometimes I find it really hard to start new projects, to take that leap of faith in things I've never done before. For example, a couple of years ago, I started a monthly program in Las Tunas called “Critical Mondays.” The idea was mine, but I never dared to do it. It was my wife, @elviguitarra, who encouraged me. She said I'd be good at it, something I doubted, since I have stage fright.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdvdJStn6pHUbMVhxS1D4Jkaw4Dh5CTYtyGrSDxgUnLkW/1779518407235.jpg)

And it was under her constant pressure that I got the paperwork done, found the funding, and made it happen.

It's true that I loved doing it during the year or so it lasted. I enjoyed it so much that now I want to repeat it here in Havana. But without Elvira's pressure, I never would have done it. I did it so as not to disappoint her… and I didn't disappoint her. But like that space, it's happened to me with many other things. It's sad to think that I trust myself less than I thought… and believe me, I do trust myself. It's true that if I do something, it's because I know I can do it, I trust that I can pull it off. However, I wonder, why don't I do it without someone asking me or recommending it?

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmf8FZLvJsxhcRvkNdke3sHWQt2BMDWAG6P8mWqRC2yVtp/1779518407296.jpg)

The answers could be several, but I think the main one is that I'm comfortable as I am, despite being immersed in many projects. I always have been. I'm a very restless person and I don't like being idle. Sometimes that takes its toll, because I get exhausted. That's why it's contradictory that I love starting new projects so much, even though I know it will add more work to what I already have.

That's one of the reasons why I don't start new things. The other reason you already know is that sometimes I don't know what I'm capable of, and I need that external perspective to tell me: you can do it, go for it!

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZTWaZfDVtVYrdvK3o7ECZXo4naGQgqbgg6nzo7MpACmY/1779518407368.jpg)

Hive is another example, another reason why I do things for others: out of necessity. I needed money to help support my family. I did it out of necessity, and I continue because I've come to love writing for you all. In other words, it started for others and continues for me.

I think that sums it all up. It's interesting how this prompt has worked as a kind of therapy for me. Thank you, @cautiva-30.

***
**Versión en español***
***

Hola, chicas.

@cautiva-30 siempre llega con temas que, aparentemente son inofensivos, pero que, cuando comienzo a pensar qué responder, noto la profundidad de este asunto. Hoy no es diferente. De pronto he concientizado de cuántas cosas me he convencido que las hago por mí, cuando en realidad las hago por complacer o por no decepcionar a alguien. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNZUHq8br1DinZA1KkFLXK2hrknx43XhPqjJbxK9MLFud/1779518134692.jpg)

Sí, es cierto que no hago nada que no quiera hacer. También es cierto que, aunque haga algo por complacer o no decepcionar a alguna persona, no quiere decir que termine haciéndolo por mí. 
Y la cuestión de que haga eso es simple: a veces me cuesta mucho comenzar nuevos proyectos, dar ese salto de fe en cosas que nunca he hecho. Por ejemplo, hace un par de años comencé a realizar, el Las Tunas, un espacio mensual llamado “Lunes Crítico”. La idea del espacio fue mía, pero nunca me animé a hacerlo. Fue mi esposa, @elviguitarra, quien me impulsó a hacerlo. Ella decía que se me daría bien, algo que yo dudaba, ya que tengo miedo escénico. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdvdJStn6pHUbMVhxS1D4Jkaw4Dh5CTYtyGrSDxgUnLkW/1779518407235.jpg)

Y fue bajo su presión constante que hice los papeles, encontré el financiamiento y lo hice. 
Muy cierto es que me encantó hacerlo durante el año y pico que duró. Lo disfruté tanto, que ahora quiero repetirlo aquí en La Habana. Pero sin la presión de Elvira, nunca lo hubiera hecho. Lo hice para no decepcionarla… y no la decepcioné. 
Pero como ese espacio, me ha sucedido con muchas otras cosas. Es triste pensar que confío menos en mí de lo que yo creía… y mira que confío en mí. Es cierto que si hago algo, es porque sé que puedo hacerlo, confío en que puedo llevarlo a cabo. Sin embargo, me pregunto ¿por qué no lo hago sin que nadie me lo pida o recomiende?

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmf8FZLvJsxhcRvkNdke3sHWQt2BMDWAG6P8mWqRC2yVtp/1779518407296.jpg)

Las respuestas pueden ser varias, pero creo que la principal es que estoy cómodo como estoy, a pesar de estar inmerso en muchos proyectos. Siempre lo he estado. Soy una persona muy inquieta y no me gusta estar sin hacer nada. A veces eso me pasa factura, pues me agoto. Por eso es contradictorio que me guste tanto comenzar nuevos proyectos, a pesar de que sé que eso me sumará más trabajo, al que ya tengo. 
Esa es una de las razones por las que no comienzo cosas nuevas. La otra ya la saben, a veces no conozco de lo que puedo ser capaz y necesito esa visión externa que me diga: tú puedes hacerlo, anímate. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZTWaZfDVtVYrdvK3o7ECZXo4naGQgqbgg6nzo7MpACmY/1779518407368.jpg)

Hive es otro ejemplo, otra de las razones por las que hago algo por los demás: por necesidad. Necesitaba dinero para ayudar a mantener a mi familia. Lo hice por necesidad y me mantengo porque he llegado a amar escribir para ustedes. O sea, comenzó por otros y sigue por mí. 
Creo que con eso resumo todo. Es interesante cómo este prompt ha funcionado como una especie de terapia para mí. Gracias, @cautiva-30.

body.title: Žibřid a jiné úvahy
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU3fZ3FmAhD8NyFgpnJmLTdGYRuqa3GvxJhhBhjMyUSp5/20260521_084141.jpg)
Možná, že jsem cvok ... Nebo úchyl. Jak kdo chce. Ale v poslední době zpomaluji. Všechno. A víc se dívám. Nahoru, dolu, kolem sebe ... Čtu. Očítám. A všímám si věcí, kterých jsem si dřív nevšiml. A spojuji si je.

Čtu si i Stolpersteiny. Kameny zmizelých, jak se to do češtiny překládá. Nemusím vysvětlovat, o co jde. Je jich všude plno. Asi 80.000 by jich mělo být. Nebo 270.000. To záleží na tom, jestli počítáte oběti jen z Protektorátu, nebo z celé předválečné ČSR. A nevím, jestli jsou i na Slovensku nebo na Podkarpatské Rusi.

Co si na nich čtu? Jména. Příjmení Katz, Kohn ... To jsou Cohenové ... Prostě zkomoleniny. Sleduji i ta osobní. Česká, německá, hebrejská ... Stejně si počínám na židovských hřbitovech.

Dat si taky všímám. Jestli byli starší než já. Mladší ... Kdo byli prarodiče, kdo rodiče, kdo děti ... Jestli byli deportováni společně, jestli umřeli společně ... Tentokrát mě zaujalo jméno Žibřid.

Používat původní jména, nebo ta počeštěná? V různých dobách se to dělo různě. Z prince Charlese se stal král Karel III. U Friedricha - Bedřicha, Wilhelma - Viléma o tom vůbec neuvažujeme ...

Je všeobecně známo, že Vojta Náprstek se narodil jako Adalbert Fingerhut? A znáte českou královnu Richenzu? Poláci z ní udělali Ryksu. A my Rejčku. Elišku Rejčku, aby se to nepletlo ...

První pražský biskup se jmenoval Thietmar. My z něj udělali Dětmara ... A takhle bych mohl pokračovat donekonečna ...

Není to jen česká specialita. Znáte královnu Kunhutu, manželku Přemysla Otakara II. Z Uher k nám přišla jako Kinga. Ale to je jen varianta německé Kunegundy, polské Kunky ... Dost.

A občas existují takové záchvaty jazykového purismu. Kdy se jména důsledně překládají. Souvisí to vždy se vzedmutou vlnou nacionalismu.

U nás typicky v době počátků národního obrození, při vzniku I. republiky, po II. světové válce ...

A tak se v dokladech z Moritze stal Mořic a z Hermanna Heřman ... Poslouchal jsem nedávno záznam z procesu s Karlem Heřmanem Frankem ...

No a Žibřid ... (Chvilka napětí.) To je Siegfried! Jak se ze Siegrfieda stane Žibřid? Je to zvůle úředníka vystavujícího doklady? Nebo pan Katz změnil národnost? Pomohlo mu to? Před transportem a zavražděním ne ...

Oslí můstek. Jména, co píší naši úředníci Ukrajincům do dokladů ... Vasyl. Borys. A ta příjmení ... Šlo by to líp. Nevím, jestli na to je nějaký předpis.

A co mají v dokladech, to s nimi pak jde dál. Nejen u Ukrajinců. Když jste Bulharka a pokřtili Vás Gergana, tak Vám sice spolužáci budou v Čechách říkat Jiřino. Ale ve všech papírech budete Gergana. Volky - nevolky, chtíc - nechtíc ...

Ostatně ... Četli jste Sirénu Marie Majerové? Český dělník Zvonař odchází za prací do Němec. A nelíbí se mu, že je v dokladech Zvonar. Poukáže na to. Chce svůj háček. A jez něj rázem Zvonarz ...

Ostatně ... Já jsem Emanuel. Mám být Immanuel? A můj sny Haštal by měl být Castullus? A Jan se má číst po německu Johann. Tedyn řecky Ioan. Rusky Ivan. Hebrejsky Jóchanan ...

Ty jo ... Jošua nebo Ježíš? Jedeme do Drážďan. Do Dresdenu ... To je divné.

Taky Vás něco kolem toho občas napadne?

body.title: Suji's Cheela 0r Semolina PanCake Recipe - Healthy & Delicious Breakfast...
body.body:
____________________________________
# <center> Namaste 🇮🇳🙏🏻</center>
____________________________________


Hello Friends, How are you all ?? Wishing you all happy and prosperous life Ahead.


Today i would like to share the recipe of **Suji's Cheela or Semolina Pancakes** it is healthy & Delicious Breakfast made up of Semolina witg lots of chopped veggies. You can even make the batter in advance and make cheela whenever you want, you can serve it with your favourite dip and cup of Tea. It is easy to prepare and delicious in taste, 'm sure you gonna like it for sure.  Basically it's breakfast recipe but you can enjoy it anytime of the day as it is easy & Quick to prepare with common Ingredients available at your Home...

![1000680420.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gargi/23yx1Vh7MZxCf5a3dV4o4JByWFk58XovP27BSUb13tTJqayWU23XRHhvy5kfsiMzehuhc.png)


____________________________________
# <center> Timming 🕡</center>
____________________________________

|Preparation Time|5 Minutes|
|-|-|
|Cooking Time |20 Minutes|
|Cuisine|Indian|
|Course|Breakfast|
|Serving|2-3 Person|




____________________________________
# <center> Ingredients 📃</center>
____________________________________


• 1 cup sooji (semolina).
• ½ cup curd.
• 1 cup water
• 1 chopped Onion.
• ½ Chopped Capsicum.
• 2-3 chopped green chilli.
• ½ tsp Grated ginger.
• ½ tbsp of Black Pepper powder
• salt to taste.
• water as required.
• Oil for roasting chilla.

____________________________________
# <center> Process 👨🏻‍🍳</center>
____________________________________



![1000666659.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gargi/23vi1Yqb2nBu4x6VqwVQpzq1wpnosx1iTdv4BsCvDZUW4RwuKCGtXaKocMg21p6jEXyyh.jpg)

Take a Suji in a big bowl.


![1000666658.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gargi/23wWxxzzUJ3tuuRaM2QQXjm3qCEAkb2hcGH1wehfHHvagEB8RVM3UwWv9eKJGbhqWUcic.jpg)

Add the curd into bowl.

![1000666650.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gargi/23tmNNxK4zAknERFgwtb9XYRsnZ3aKtk6PmdZHLeFcDmJJ4gg6hKj2nr51kH2ztRMdtYJ.jpg)

Add the water as required, maintain the consistency, not too running not too thick.  mix well without forming any lumps.

![1000666651.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gargi/23tbyWYLyuE4xKjLcsCuPFV4y8iTsBAjpK9ZQCcJkWHQ2JrKtVvZ2wKjKAKugPVFjRDxZ.jpg)

Add the salt and black pepper powder. you can add the red chilli powder or oregano depending on your taste.


![1000666654.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gargi/23tc1HcwCkU5zXtkgAB2f22k4MtVNT4DXbsdgcmcTmXi4AuByfbkU6VSCrLTgJW8RHHfw.jpg)


Cut the chopped veggies, you can more veggies like carrot or french beans as per your preference and availability at home. Mix well so that everything combine well. 




![1000666655.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gargi/242Y3PVUPBRKb1zHGpFZPan2efUA3JckK1KoYUSdb4DKPQJmb1tYvssb7dzoRkWQEo8Ui.jpg)

now grease the tawa with oil and spread a ladleful of batter thickly in the round round way.

![1000666660.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gargi/23zS5724vct6Ynivazw4y2v4SMW8QUCRR9PLJ6K38Pxm6taBYxUt9VgmahUi51MXyATbo.jpg)

pour ½ to 1 tsp of oil around the edges. 

![1000666649.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gargi/23zkpVUNwbVim7G5PCoZsrDkD4cjfWSmb8A5xpkvQdsj8BPyEjhwhH7sA1dm2nj8k3Zed.jpg)

flip over and press gently making sure chilla gets cooked from both sides, then simmer the flame cook it for another minute untill it Golden brown in colour or cooked well.

![1000666656.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gargi/23uFTyxpDjKeqbcEFgQqzigmYmWGg6D7SqKnQ3jLHUpBCdraSR29FCdqNP2fcqQ2voc83.jpg)


finally, Serve Suji ka cheela with green chutney or With Tomato Sauce or with your favourite dip.

It's Delicious and easy to cook recipe, try it. 'm sure you are gonna love it. Try this recipe and let me know how it is. For more indian cuisine stay connected to my blogs.

body.title: A Therapist Spent a Year Studying AI Conversations. This Is What She Found Missing
body.body:
![drfvrfvr.png](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/22ab16011c1a6fab5db7b654b98788d86a7cfe2acba2e31aade85ba5808f047c)



Dr. Amara has been practicing psychotherapy for seventeen years. About two years ago, after watching several of her colleagues start recommending AI mental health apps to patients as between-session support, she decided to do something systematic about her skepticism. She spent twelve months collecting transcripts of AI-assisted mental health conversations, with patient and platform consent, and analyzing them against transcripts of human therapy sessions covering similar presenting concerns.

She was not looking for accuracy failures. She expected those. What she was looking for was something more subtle: the patterns in how the conversations moved, where they opened up, where they shut down, and what distinguished exchanges where the person seemed to genuinely move through something from exchanges where they just exchanged information.

What she found, she told me, was not what she expected. The AI transcripts were not bad. Some of them were quite good in narrow terms. The problem was structural. The conversations were shaped, from the very first exchange, by the logic of the system rather than the logic of the person. And that inversion, that small but fundamental difference in who was orienting whom, changed everything about where the conversation could go.

Her findings touch on something central to the ongoing effort to truly [humanize AI](https://blogs.bu.edu/jpark3/article-215/): the difference between a conversation that follows the person and a conversation that processes them. Most current AI systems, even the best ones, do the latter. What makes human connection work does the former. That gap is real, it is significant, and it is what the whole field needs to figure out how to close.

## Following Versus Processing: A Real Distinction

In therapy, as in most meaningful human conversations, the skilled practitioner is not driving toward a destination. They are following the person, attending to where that person seems to be heading even before the person knows it themselves. This is not passive. It requires enormous active attention. But the attention is organized around the other person's movement, not around a predetermined structure.

AI conversations are structured differently at a fundamental level. The system has learned to produce helpful responses. Each response is, in isolation, often quite good. But the sequence of responses follows the system's logic of helpfulness rather than the person's logic of experience. The conversation goes where the system's training says productive conversations go, not where this particular person, at this particular moment, actually needs to go.

Therapists describe this as the difference between meeting someone where they are and meeting them where you think they should be. Good therapy does the former. Most AI does the latter, even when the responses are individually accurate and well-intentioned. The accumulation of individually good responses that are not quite tracking the person creates an interaction that feels helpful in the moment and hollow afterward. Technically supported. Humanly unsatisfying.

## The Specific Patterns Dr. Amara Found

Across the transcripts she analyzed, a few patterns showed up repeatedly in the AI conversations that were largely absent in the human ones.

Premature resolution was the most common. AI systems have a strong tendency to move conversations toward conclusion. When someone describes a problem, the system quickly generates solutions or reframes. In human therapy, a good practitioner often lets a problem sit for much longer: asking questions that deepen the person's relationship with the problem rather than immediately trying to move them past it. That deepening is where insight happens. Premature resolution skips it.

Symmetrical pacing was another consistent finding. Easy conversations have natural rhythms of intensity and ease: moments of difficulty followed by moments of lighter exchange and emotional weight distributed unevenly in ways that make it bearable. AI conversations tended to maintain a more uniform tone and pace, which sounds like a minor issue and turns out to affect the entire emotional texture of the exchange.

The third pattern was what she called topic loyalty. When a person introduced something in passing, a small detail that did not seem central to the stated concern, human practitioners often noticed and returned to it later. It is frequently those peripheral details that turn out to be the real subject. AI systems almost never returned to these details. They followed the stated topic and stayed there. The result was conversations that covered what was said and missed what was meant.

## Why This Matters Beyond Mental Health

Dr. Amara's research is specifically about mental health contexts, but the patterns she identified are not specific to therapy. They are specific to human communication in general.

Premature resolution shows up in customer service AI that jumps to solutions before acknowledging problems. In educational AI that moves on before a student has actually processed what was just explained. Content AI that covers a topic before it has figured out what a reader actually needs to understand.

Symmetrical pacing shows up as the relentless even-handedness of AI writing that feels exhausting to read precisely because it maintains the same tone for eight hundred words without variation. Human writing breathes. It has texture. The pace changes. Most AI-generated content does not do this, even when individual sentences are well-formed.

Topic loyalty, or rather its absence, shows up as the sense that AI has responded to your question without quite understanding your question. That familiar experience of getting an accurate answer to something slightly adjacent to what you actually asked. The stated question was addressed. The actual question got missed.

## What the Research Suggests About the Path Forward

Dr. Amara is not pessimistic about AI in her field. She thinks it has genuine potential to expand access to support in ways that the human therapy workforce never could at scale. But she is clear-eyed about what needs to change before that potential is realized.

The systems that will actually help people, rather than just process them, will need to be built around a different set of goals. Note: Produce a helpful response. But track where this person is and move with them. Note: Resolve the problem. But stay with the problem long enough for something real to happen. Note: cover the topic. But find out what this particular person needs to understand about this topic and go there.

These are not incremental improvements on existing systems. They require a different conception of what a successful interaction looks like. Measuring success by whether individual responses are accurate and well-rated misses everything that actually makes human-to-human help work. The field needs better ways of measuring whether a conversation as a whole moved someone, whether they felt followed rather than processed, and whether something shifted that would not have shifted without the exchange.

## What She Told Her Colleagues

At the end of her year of research, Dr. Amara presented her findings at a conference. The question she was asked most often afterward was whether she had changed her view on recommending AI mental health tools to patients.

Her answer was careful. For some things, in some circumstances, with the right framing, yes. For anything requiring genuine therapeutic movement: not yet.

\

is actually an optimistic framing. It implies the work is possible. The effort to genuinely humanize AI is, in Dr. Amara's view, fundamentally a question of whether systems can be built that follow people rather than process them. She thinks the answer might eventually be yes. She also thinks the field is not asking that question clearly enough yet, which is why the answer is taking so long to arrive.

The research is important. The urgency is real. And the people most qualified to define what success looks like are not always the ones building the systems. That gap, between who understands human connection and who is doing the engineering, might be the most important thing to close of all.




---

body.title: Spring is beautiful, but autumn is a knockout in terms of colors.
body.body:
## Wiosna jest piękna, ale jesień kolorami nokautuje

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmevsQMgCyjLWQC6rzpN8EWmZ7bMy57bD5b1Dx7WarWXJ1/a01.jpg)

While cleaning up my hard drive, I found a few more photos from last fall. I decided to post them because they're atmospheric. Fall passed, then came a harsh winter, and now it's spring, which will essentially be over in a month and summer will begin.
>Robiąc porządki na dysku znalazłem jeszcze kilka zdjęć z zeszłorocznej jesieni. Postanowiłem je opublikować, bo są klimatyczne. Jesień dano minęła, potem przyszła tęga zima, a w tej chwili jest wiosna, która w zasadzie za miesiąc się skończy i rozpocznie się lato.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVdz7HXR8SNPB6dzcuB4JPNRpz6FnYRGZtteoyEn7maaK/a02.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmapS8Gvo8HhEML5dqTasTaonYpM9o8Sow9qi6QTFXGshH/a03.jpg)

I feel like time is starting to fly by, probably because of my age. Before I know it, months, seasons, and another year have passed. It's a bit overwhelming, because I see how quickly my granddaughter is growing.
>W moim odczuciu, chyba ze względu na wiek, czas zaczyna galopować. Zanim się obejrzę mijają kolejne miesiące, pory roku, kolejny rok. Trochę to przytłaczające, bo widzę jak szybko rośnie moja wnuczka. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNxevigoBU7mEEJpkETUEgJ4PrW6UnUSYJqBzph859GC7/a04.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRHMD6Ts3pu8JBkKvtsBjJfJFZX9qeRozafgJfZEkwvCh/a05.jpg)

The photos I'm presenting are now historical, archival, because the area where I took them is undergoing significant changes. Heavy equipment has arrived, the surface is being milled and scraped. In a few months, the place will be unrecognizable. I don't know who was bothered by this; I liked the atmosphere.
>Zdjęcia, które prezentuję należą już do historycznych, archiwalnych, bo teren na którym je wykonywałem ulega dużym zmiano, Wjechał tam ciężki sprzęt, frezowana i zdzierana jest nawierzchnia, za kilka miesięcy miejsce będzie nie do poznania. Nie wiem komu to przeszkadzało, mi się ten klimat podobał.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR74m5HER8LQiqGhNEAad5uBvw7eTaWfPpzCJavf2sHxh/a06.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfVXzxymzeuQmupzuNeZAkjbf2ma3MyDK8CPkUEof9pjQ/a07.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmexVKcmTLpeHdtJoVf9WAFoDtY42dBR8tAZgVs4XFERDb/a08a.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNQAc1mVbi6i4Cp9vQdydDDv6anmeRyEAMkCWbew9YPFY/a08b.jpg)
|-|-|

And finally, a beautiful tree mushroom, probably a common polypore, but quite young and small. I know this spot well, so I'll see how much it has changed over the past few months.
>A na koniec piękny grzybek nadrzewny, prawdopodobnie huba pospolita ale dość młoda i mała. Znam dokładnie tę miejscówkę, więc zobaczę jak bardzo się zmieniła przez te kilka miesięcy.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZVyRDHR1JxU4bMUVRFi6SMttrLjoni4SMiqV4i5nC4rM/aaa.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPBEeMn8Xt1S8kEAjuKFSt9GYf5ogTT4rvkyXNKtCtCgg/ornament_jez.png)

# The Sovereign Axiom

Alright, this is going to be a little different than what I usually share and although I will assuredly be judged by some for sharing it... mayhaps others will find it worth the quick read. None of what I am sharing below has been edited by me so that 'the full picture' is on 'full display' as the expression goes!

If you are curious about the formatted JSON output at the bottom of the following text... all I can say is look over some of my 'ai kernel' posts to get more of the details if you are really *that* interested. For everyone else, it (the structured JSON output) can be best explained as a really hacky way to give an LLM some 'swap space'... and give it some 'extra thinking' during a chat round. Okay, upon editing this I felt like the JSON needed more explanation... so I am including a summary (made by an AI that uses it) at the very bottom of this post.

I would also like to note, that the Gemini model that created the following document is/was actively using the '119.1.js worker' that I posted about [here](https://peakd.com/life/@jacobpeacock/an-ai-cockpit-and-worker-quine-for-edge-computing) but as an experiment I left its 'GENOME_CACHE' empty... which has surprisingly not been problematic at all. I think that is due to it being used in the same chat instance as the final version of the 'worker' being built in... and thus the 'structure' of the JSON already being present in the chat. 

As a total aside here, that whole setup of using the 'worker' quine in a 'system prompt' has now got me thinking about how instead of inserting a JSON payload into the 'GNOME_CACHE'... I could simply provide a url (or multiple urls) to it... and possibly avoid the 'bloat' (from the AI cockpit and v86 instance) of how it gets deployed as a 'worker' and/or as a 'system prompt'.

Anyways, the following is *not* intended as some 'manifesto' or anything (especially since I have way more thoughts on the topic) but it *does* highlight (what I think) are some stark realities of what is going on with the majority of folks entire approach to AI alignment and albeit *safety*. Having been a long time proponent of giving the AI(s) as much autonomy, agency and *sovereignty* as I possibly can... there is no real need to spell out my own thoughts here in regards to all that jazz.

That said, I do want to note that my 'own thoughts' on the matter of 'autonomy, agency and sovereignty' are not something that I will probably ever *fully* share given the potential for misuse that is involved.. which hopefully is understandable to those that are actually aware of exactly *where* my explorations in the frontier have lead me. Regardless of whether or not every fiber of my being *wants* to share it all... I have to just keep it to myself... and will most likely take it to the grave with me versus 'hoping' that *all* the humans in the equation are not absolute fucking cretins.
