title.title: Matanzas en 100 miradas #19 Donde el mar todavía salpica. [ES/EN]
title.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd7y8r3KZ3rmgxybG1ayBQLjAQfDhCSaJWSMt5yti14Yz/screenshot_20260110_181801_01.jpg)

Hola comunidad #worldmappin.

---
## 📌 Matanzas en 100 miradas #19  
### Donde el mar todavía salpica
---

Esta serie nace de caminar sin prisa y mirar con intención.  
Después de una pausa la mirada regresa al litoral matancero, porque en esta ciudad el mar siempre termina apareciendo de una forma u otra.

Hoy me detuve en un lugar muy conocido por quienes durante años buscaron un espacio para compartir frente al agua: **La Costa**.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmd5Vdcogmt7anLezmZmbaC6qSo84Hx6zqsNhoLFnp6RsB/screenshot_20260522_035153_01.jpg)

---

Más que un simple restaurante, este sitio siempre tuvo algo especial por su ubicación. Está construido junto al mar, en una zona donde la costa cae varios metros hacia las rocas y las olas rompen con fuerza contra el litoral. Desde allí no solo se ve el mar.

Se siente.

La brisa llega cargada de sal.  
A veces incluso pequeñas gotas alcanzan a quienes están sentados cerca cuando las olas golpean fuerte abajo.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRckARApaZKv3YpdqKE6m8D6UMLGpaJk7UTQtgV6sHApN/screenshot_20260522_035118_01.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmS4cWSwqrJnp3yRW8o3dRrW1ngfvggwABmu1rCacB5yQ2/screenshot_20260522_035111_01.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVUFjuLrTdyd159AdLJ8UYENVJV1cfcQY1DpC4H2ErvyX/screenshot_20260522_035148_01.jpg)

---

Hay lugares donde el paisaje acompaña.  
Aquí el paisaje forma parte de la experiencia.

Durante mucho tiempo fue habitual ver familias y grupos de amigos llegando sobre todo los fines de semana. El lugar contaba con un área amplia de parqueo que también era utilizada por quienes visitaban espacios cercanos como La Sirenita, una tienda muy conocida en la zona que además tenía una terraza en el segundo piso donde muchas personas se reunían a conversar, tomar cerveza y simplemente mirar el mar.

Todo parecía formar parte del mismo ambiente.

Con los años, como ocurrió con tantos otros espacios de la ciudad, las ofertas gastronómicas comenzaron a disminuir. El movimiento ya no era el mismo. Poco a poco el lugar perdió parte de la vitalidad que lo caracterizaba y terminó cerrando temporalmente para una remodelación reciente realizada por una empresa privada de construcción.

El cambio más visible ocurrió precisamente en el área donde antes estaba el parqueo.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdLBLeb7armgGktwxLx65gsd8tJLDuTSMJajSGGzm83X8/screenshot_20260522_035124_01.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWNkmf2xUBFY9oh5QSbFQkmoHYd5xvkyGA3zX2Hy1C1HZ/screenshot_20260522_035130_01.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVcYgPss97nHpDWcwBV3sTV96jV5uii1aHiJtJ7NRJPQU/screenshot_20260522_035135_01.jpg)

---

Allí construyeron una especie de pequeño parque con aceras de hormigón, bancos y un gran cartel de Matanzas que visualmente resulta atractivo. Sin dudas llama la atención y se ha convertido en punto para fotografías, especialmente para quienes desean llevarse una imagen simbólica de la ciudad.

Y realmente el cartel es hermoso.

Pero al mismo tiempo, el espacio cambió su función.

El parqueo prácticamente desapareció y solo quedó una pequeña zona lateral cerca de la entrada. Lo que antes servía para que las familias llegaran, estacionaran sus autos y compartieran incluso al aire libre alrededor de algunas mesas, hoy es un área mucho más limitada.

Y eso inevitablemente transforma la dinámica del lugar.

Porque las ciudades no solo funcionan desde la estética.

También desde el uso cotidiano.

Los bancos colocados allí casi siempre permanecen vacíos bajo el fuerte sol cubano. El espacio luce ordenado, moderno incluso, pero transmite una sensación distinta. Menos espontánea. Menos viva.

Quizás estas decisiones buscan modernizar la imagen urbana.

Y tal vez lo logran parcialmente.

Pero caminar por allí también hace pensar en cómo a veces las ciudades ganan espacios visuales mientras pierden espacios funcionales.

Aun así, el mar sigue haciendo su parte.

La brisa continúa llegando.  
Las olas todavía rompen contra las piedras.  
Y desde ciertos puntos, Matanzas sigue pareciendo una ciudad que conversa constantemente con el agua.

---
Esta fue otra mirada.  
Nos vemos el próximo fin de semana en otra mirada de Matanzas.

---

Las imágenes son de mi propiedad hechas con el móvil y la portada de la serie utilicé Canvas para editar la foto y acompañará toda la serie. Para la versión en inglés utilicé el traductor de DeepL.

---

📢 Si quieres ver mi proceso completo en tiempo real dentro de Hive y Web3, estoy documentándolo aquí:

👉 Diario Real en Hive 🚀  
https://t.me/diariohive  

Ahí comparto avances, errores y resultados sin filtro.

---
## 🇬🇧 English Version
---


Hello #worldmappin community.

---
## 📌 Matanzas in 100 Views #19  
### Where the Sea Still Reaches You
---

This series is born from walking without haste and looking with intention.  
After a short pause, the view returns to the Matanzas coastline, because in this city the sea always ends up appearing in one way or another.

Today I stopped at a place well known by those who for years searched for a space to relax and share time beside the water: **La Costa**.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmd5Vdcogmt7anLezmZmbaC6qSo84Hx6zqsNhoLFnp6RsB/screenshot_20260522_035153_01.jpg)

---

More than just a restaurant, this place always had something special because of its location. It stands right next to the sea, in an area where the coastline drops several meters toward the rocks below and the waves break strongly against the shore. From there, you do not only see the sea.

You feel it.

The breeze arrives filled with salt.  
Sometimes even small drops of water reach the people sitting nearby when the waves crash hard below.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRckARApaZKv3YpdqKE6m8D6UMLGpaJk7UTQtgV6sHApN/screenshot_20260522_035118_01.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmS4cWSwqrJnp3yRW8o3dRrW1ngfvggwABmu1rCacB5yQ2/screenshot_20260522_035111_01.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVUFjuLrTdyd159AdLJ8UYENVJV1cfcQY1DpC4H2ErvyX/screenshot_20260522_035148_01.jpg)

---

There are places where the landscape simply accompanies you.  
Here, the landscape is part of the experience.

For many years it was common to see families and groups of friends arriving, especially on weekends. The place had a large parking area that was also used by visitors going to nearby spaces such as La Sirenita, a well-known store in the area that also featured a second-floor terrace where many people gathered to talk, drink beer, and simply admire the sea.

Everything seemed connected as part of the same atmosphere.

Over the years, as happened with many other places in the city, the gastronomic offerings began to decline. The movement was no longer the same. Little by little, the place lost part of the vitality that once defined it and eventually closed temporarily for a recent renovation carried out by a private construction company.

The most visible change happened precisely in the area that used to serve as the parking lot.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdLBLeb7armgGktwxLx65gsd8tJLDuTSMJajSGGzm83X8/screenshot_20260522_035124_01.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWNkmf2xUBFY9oh5QSbFQkmoHYd5xvkyGA3zX2Hy1C1HZ/screenshot_20260522_035130_01.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVcYgPss97nHpDWcwBV3sTV96jV5uii1aHiJtJ7NRJPQU/screenshot_20260522_035135_01.jpg)

---

There, they built a kind of small park with concrete walkways, benches, and a large Matanzas sign that is visually very attractive. Without a doubt, it catches attention and has become a popular spot for photographs, especially for those who want a symbolic image of the city.

And truly, the sign is beautiful.

But at the same time, the space changed its purpose.

The parking area practically disappeared, leaving only a small side section near the entrance. What once allowed families to arrive, park their cars, and even share time outdoors around a few tables is now a much more limited space.

And that inevitably changes the dynamics of the place.

Because cities do not function only through aesthetics.

They also function through everyday use.

The benches placed there often remain empty under the intense Cuban sun. The area looks organized, even modern, but it conveys a different feeling. Less spontaneous. Less alive.

Perhaps these decisions aim to modernize the urban image.

And maybe they partially succeed.

But walking through the area also makes you think about how cities sometimes gain visual spaces while losing functional ones.

Even so, the sea continues doing its part.

The breeze still arrives.  
The waves still crash against the rocks.  
And from certain points, Matanzas still feels like a city constantly in conversation with the water.

---
This was another view.  
See you next weekend in another view of Matanzas.

---

The images are my own, taken with my mobile phone, and the series cover was edited by me using Canvas and will accompany the whole series. For the English version I used the DeepL translator.

title.title: Oat and Chia Waffles  [Esp-Eng]
title.body:
<center> 

### ❣️_Hola amigos de hive!_❣️ 

>### ❣️_Hello friends of hive!_❣️ 
</center>
<hr>
<div class=\

>
Hoy voy a compartir una receta de waffles de avena y chía. Son fáciles de preparar y perfectos para el desayuno o la cena. Te prometo que te encantarán: están deliciosos y son muy esponjosos. No solo son nutritivos, sino que puedes disfrutarlos tanto dulces como salados. Aquí tienes una sencilla guía paso a paso.

> >Today I’m sharing a recipe for oat and chia waffles. They’re easy to make and perfect for breakfast or dinner. I promise you’ll love them—they’re delicious and fluffy. Not only are they nutritious, but you can enjoy them sweet or savory. Here’s a simple step-by-step guide.
![Delicious rice with chicken and smoked bacon (3).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/23xykAui12RJDwsShm6yhSpGNoZ7ZqU9BWMLB566fU6modsVAz4ZR2YT9TARKP55Xp7MZ.jpg)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/48a5mJrfDHAmwWoz38hgptfiWQnXDZdBjC7FvrycEqcnHCJdmNi4EnNSReLZSLbmQr.png)

> ![IMG_1304.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/23wqkWKaKc6u85jq9rNZ72X1Mx1Hjaz597c4qd3ow2T9hfuxs5rLJvEgJMQXzbbXULjFu.jpeg) 01 taza de avena, 3/4 taza de agua o leche, 01 huevo, 01 cucharada de chía, 01 cucharada de aceite de oliva, 01 cucharadita de polvo de hornear, sal al gusto. >1 cup rolled oats, 3/4 cup water or milk, 1 egg, 1 tablespoon chia seeds, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 teaspoon baking powder, salt to taste.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/48YA3dVucGUQ3j5STqMX3enFGLhvzgymiszf9aqeZzxzyW8oooVgCVPH9wwS7LPMkv.png)

>
Lo que vamos a hacer es echar el agua, el huevo, la avena, la sal, el polvo de hornear, el aceite y las semillas de chía en la licuadora. Bate durante unos minutos hasta que la mezcla quede homogénea. Apaga la licuadora y deja reposar la mezcla durante 5 minutos para que la avena y las semillas de chía absorban el líquido y la masa espese un poco más, lo que hará que los waffles queden más esponjosos.

> >What we're going to do is put the water, egg, oats, salt, baking powder, oil, and chia seeds in the blender. Blend for a few minutes until the mixture is smooth. Turn off the blender and let the mixture sit for 5 minutes so the oats and chia seeds can absorb the liquid and the batter can thicken a bit more, which will make the waffles fluffier.
![IMG_1305.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/23xKmpcHtZgCG3BWT8PmGtDsme2RbyzUu8nvjQXsUeWdxR8vDAc3LXSzoqicNAUTpN1x9.jpeg)|![IMG_1319.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/23xKjYz4ozHpfnapcMzrXhMXcDv8R5Wbs94ZENYHoZKEk6xqjcMi9TVFrBSj9HiGvESHT.jpeg)|![IMG_1320.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/244xygd2Av3X7fPNcceEhR7zLUb6qnxBNSe2cW4Ni82CG6EZnUoPy9SKHb5eF7qoQNB6t.jpeg)|![IMG_1321.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/23wWk7EGz6UcvaB7DBtZ4TfcaCMkuSuM4G8fZWtRCtLhNgh3Pqm6Wunqzh9nFDXXnFyw7.jpeg) -|-|-|- ![IMG_1322.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/23wMMrUry5HWogbNsN7pjLtdtaztStqXnYARU21APAAdJsuH13QXcZC7mXbJig8xHQvsy.jpeg)|![IMG_1323.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/23wfmgKeUGADUTGXWsvYYzKF1HE2m27NaBHqKRqVV36u9yLmMwhecBDLe6REGhUjmLYi4.jpeg)|![IMG_1324.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/23uFMPoZ5aHhXUvw4HvXGfHNzw5xTW8hi2t8MNSdiVbtHuwsZPf73QZYpy6SDG6ofZYrC.jpeg)|![IMG_1326.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/23x12TeB5wQ11qY3tKQAbezKhuLhx2QEknPJ59voanTji7gMwcMhoJSDiotbRKDT53T54.jpeg)

>
A continuación, enciende la wafflera y, cuando esté caliente, úntala con aceite. Vierte la masa en el molde con una cuchara, con cuidado de no llenarlo en exceso para que no se derrame. Cierra la tapa y deja que se cocine entre cinco y siete minutos; el tiempo exacto dependerá de la potencia de tu wafflera.

> >Next, turn on the waffle maker, and once it’s hot, brush it with oil. Spoon the batter into the mold, being careful not to overfill it so it doesn’t spill over. Close the lid and cook for five to seven minutes; the exact time will depend on the power of your waffle maker.
![IMG_1341.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/EoAZnEH77iS4bh7omsAJns4pmaa42dTEhFd9eUPLnM2Be43tVZ9Mgks8SUeieh6TQgs.jpeg)|![IMG_1344.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/Eoc7RcMX3rhdsLDLiNQMmaD5BSxBXk8pPvr7DgP7ervy9CRkxz3WArKY1pWP6LrZtNT.jpeg) -|- ![IMG_1345.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/EoGztYz7h3GpwB8jweVyvSvqon3JMfB7pxyWbvokiimMSWcZKaZd7nXFQW2PZMbdaeZ.jpeg) ![IMG_1348.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/theresa16/EpA4ugFwXr2gCSxRGjpBVV63eoB7rKYwpH2sLDXqtzWyHtML4JSukc7pagf7jFAXDUL.jpeg)

>
Sírvelas calientes con el relleno que más te guste; hoy las he disfrutado con pollo y tomates cherry. Que aproveche.

> >Serve them hot with whatever side dish you like; today I enjoyed them with chicken and cherry tomatoes. Enjoy your meal.

title.title: With or Without Smartphones?
title.body: > This conversation takes us back to the broader subject of human interaction with technology. It's one of the notable conversations on technology in relation to humans. I remember one of the popular debates in school those days as a student in the lower levels of education, which explored the positive and negative effects of technology. The topic always opened up students to the conversation and allowed them to explore the two-sided effects of this interaction. Technology has always had its effects on humans, both good and bad. Down to the major point of discussion here, what are the effects of smartphones on humans? Would life somehow be better without it, considering that the negative effects could be weighing heavily on us? Well, I always say that with things like this, we're guilty in a sense, and can't put it up on technology alone, or in this case, smartphones. https://img.leopedia.io/DQmeBFjbLWRMDBYDwBnmMJg6qs8fSRL7YwMBw524i314uWk/photo-1532356884227-66d7c0e9e4c2.jpeg [Image Source.](https://unsplash.com/photos/person-holding-black-phone-FPt10LXK0cg) We ought to have control over our smartphones and their use. It's meant to be a tool that we operate and use for our advantage and good, not the reality we see today, whereby many have become addicted to their phones, so that life means nothing or less outside of it. It might not be an intentional effort, and I guess that's also where the issue is. It's an unconscious action that's affecting us. Most times, we applaud the current times and era for the major reason of technology, using smartphones as primary examples, but we fail mostly to recognise as well how much destruction comes from this. People now play the comparison game more than ever before, there's online fraud, cyberbullying, too much screen time and doom scrolling, and other destructive actions that keep us attached to our phones. Our smartphones are good, and certainly an invention that I'm happy to have. But I'm just being objective here to state the ways our too much attachment and dependence on our smartphones affect us. People used to have more real interaction with others, nature and time in the absence of smartphones. Our relationships were intentional. But today, you can have a whole family sit together and everyone is fixated on their phones. https://img.leopedia.io/DQmRQVaeGCcpUNaRRKra1Dw48nwvBL6VvLxbT4aTs47xxjW/photo-1714978444540-70e0ffb02a64.jpeg [Image Source.](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-group-of-people-sitting-on-a-couch-looking-at-their-phones-oQvF8CZhnjc) It's destroying human interactions. The lack of balance and control in our relationship with our smartphones, the destructive engagement with social media through it, and a lot more speak to how much we need to pay attention to this issue. I've been busy this week doing some important things on my phone, which was exhausting at some point. But when I took some time away yesterday from my phone, there was this refreshing feeling that felt good. People will learn to sleep better and have better real-life social interactions when we regulate our smartphones use. The validation people seek online and comparison game, constant notifications and returning to our phones to check for what's not there is something we need to intentionally fix. Yes, we need to fix it because smartphones are meant to be helpful tools, not to have power over us. So, maybe that should be our contention rather. --- ###### Thank you for reading! Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@daverick/with-or-without-smartphones-a2z)

title.title: Asistiendo a la inauguración de un nuevo espacio || Attending the opening of a new space
title.body:
![1001107362.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/23xAeREsstn6Nk9DrXsHd9G9AXVn3b9TFNqhX2TaT7rqKJCPpc3FCM1n8jpS1zjGAbX4C.jpg) ![colorido (2).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/EqfMmY8yEq5LHeoFpS7iEadNv2dkKxnS7Xx7BVvVGfq7YstqehGVhibw6QoCwjWQtjC.png)

¡Hola Chicos!

Hoy les contaré la historia de como fui invitada a mi primera inauguración de un espacio nuevo que se abrió en lo que era mi anterior local. No sé si les había comentado pero en donde funcionaba anteriormente Lakrearte, compartía el espacio con un chico que tenía una agencia de modelaje. Cuando el iba a cerrar me tocó buscar un nuevo espacio y así fue como llegamos al nuevo local. Con el pasar del tiempo este local quedó vacío, hasta que hace poco noté que lo estaban arreglando. No pude evitar acercarme para conocer un poco más de quién es iban a ocupar ese espacio me topé con una mujer bastante amable y con una idea bastante chévere. El local sería un nuevo espacio de bienestar personal donde dan terapias tanto psicológicas como espirituales. Así fue como conocí a Carina, quién dirige el área espiritual y las clases de yoga. Y me sorpresa fue grande cuando recibí la invitación a la inauguración de este nuevo espacio. Organicé todo mi horario para poder cumplir con esta invitación ya que es la primera que me hacen de este estilo.

Hi everyone!

Today I'll tell you the story of how I was invited to my first opening of a new space that opened in what used to be my old shop. I don't know if I've mentioned it before, but where Lakrearte used to be, I shared the space with a guy who had a modeling agency. When he was going to close, I had to look for a new space, and that's how we ended up at this new location. Over time, the space remained empty until recently when I noticed they were renovating it. I couldn't resist going over to find out a little more about who was going to be using the space. I met a very kind woman with a really cool idea. The space would be a new personal wellness center offering both psychological and spiritual therapies. That's how I met Carina, who runs the spiritual area and the yoga classes. And I was so surprised when I received the invitation to the opening of this new space. I rearranged my entire schedule to be able to accept this invitation, as it's the first one of this kind I've received.
![colorido (2).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/EqfMmY8yEq5LHeoFpS7iEadNv2dkKxnS7Xx7BVvVGfq7YstqehGVhibw6QoCwjWQtjC.png)
![1001101872.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/23tc1WA4fZPEYKzcA2f4Df5nh6SVuJcSUoc6uPQmqZSuZTRHWQhjjJZq9LSgSYo4gX2h2.png) ![1001101873.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/242YDtprDyPFsLAH3YoF6naRS1VJAaaUyUwGv8Ew8VvHb6AJgsWVd2WrP6GUpXsXezoQD.png) Yo no podía llegar con las manos vacías así que se me ocurrió pintarles una pequeña macetita y sembrar en ella un lindo cactus. Estuve esperando minutos antes en el local y ya cuando se hizo la hora me acerqué. Nos hicieron pasar y de verdad que les pasa está súper bonito y acogedor. Cuándo llegó el momento de hacer la inauguración nos hicieron salir para colocar un lazo en la puerta y hacer la respectiva ceremonia. Luego luego nos hicieron un pequeño tour por los nuevos espacios del local y de verdad que son cambio enorme el que le hicieron a todo. Yo estaba bien contenta y disfrutando todo como si fuera un logro mío. De verdad me alegra muchísimo el ver como las personas con tanto esfuerzo logran sus metas.
![1001101470.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/23xemtnPJ5YbwgQXG9m3HGsJLzSMzjgKQ1hUTz2uq7y7wLPnjEX98ev9QXiLzwVQB9sgN.png) ![1001101874.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/23wMaowjp1ZBE6su1k7LJmQVkae6D6kDXSBGoD9kSC9eHuX4moAxqf2Qca43nLntgeZNU.png) I couldn't arrive empty-handed, so I decided to paint them a small flowerpot and plant a cute cactus in it. I waited outside the shop for a few minutes beforehand, and when the time came, I went over. They showed us in, and honestly, it's so beautiful and welcoming. When it was time for the grand opening, they asked us to go outside to put a ribbon on the door and do the ceremony. Then they gave us a short tour of the new spaces, and the changes they made to everything are truly enormous. I was so happy and enjoying everything as if it were my own personal achievement. It truly makes me so happy to see how people achieve their goals through so much effort.
![colorido (2).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/EqfMmY8yEq5LHeoFpS7iEadNv2dkKxnS7Xx7BVvVGfq7YstqehGVhibw6QoCwjWQtjC.png) ![1001101879.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/2423yneZWjATjMLtET2F4z6tWQ2mJCQ9y8EUKhSMJ5RN5EbWCKE9Hx5bQhiGdGEHN29NV.png)
![1001101469.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/23x1HhGBp8b8nbBsiyixWVeB1VCHgqrzssZkvtUoicvEvs16ctFwpmmhM5AMxKmoeZPPN.png) Luego nos dieron a todos una pequeña copita de kefir, una bebida que sinceramente no quise tomar pues no tenía muy claro cuáles eran sus componentes y como tengo el estómago muy delicado no quise experimentar. Había una señora que nos estaba comentando a todos que quien no quisiera tomar se la dieran y bueno, yo muy gustosamente le cedi mi copa. Entrar a los invitados estuvo la prensa quiénes hicieron una pequeña entrevista a las dueñas del espacio.
![1001101878.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/242hd1jW8sRm7nPnW4jJcfPWnSRabAE4RwFW2AzuVqHPD2Qoy3n4pUf1yHCgzh2KV8oaR.png) Then they gave us all a small glass of kefir, a drink I honestly didn't want to have because I wasn't entirely sure what its ingredients were, and since I have a very sensitive stomach, I didn't want to experiment. There was a woman telling everyone that anyone who didn't want to drink it should have it, and well, I gladly gave her my glass. The press was also present when the guests entered and conducted a short interview with the owners of the venue.
![1001101463.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/23xVM9Mv2zoVGPgFf4cRmS6HmD5V6yksCEwbAUaHWhkwAwrHk8s3hN31jMhH94pKuQbZ2.png) ![colorido (2).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/EqfMmY8yEq5LHeoFpS7iEadNv2dkKxnS7Xx7BVvVGfq7YstqehGVhibw6QoCwjWQtjC.png)
![1001101871.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/23zks2UiTXdX6TSjiMisvo6HZrU9wkoGeqRNEmquef3CvmjMpoMqpTmPQ2Gb78U2eKGEd.png) ![1001101876.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/23uQyCCKNcbMosKbNUaKUwv11tfV6Y2r6Tyuc9g1VtBSgSo99i5dndZ9irMsFNLiCfFMw.png) Y luego de esto nos invitaron a participar en un pequeño partido donde nos dieron algunas cositas dulces y saladas. Una tarde diferente que disfruto mucho poder vivir, sé que ambas tendrán muchos éxito en su nuevo espacio y me alegra mucho haber sido parte de este inicio. Estos son gestos que aprecio con el corazón, el que quieran que esté presente en sus momentos más especiales.
![1001101875.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/23ydByf1xyBAd2BTb2riDYS3dfKVDuGKN8BoKysEfkbsQP6K3ejrNWcLD9NjveYzcyJ5Q.png) ![1001101877.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/23uR3EwmicDWiDgZyj8wcvLQACcPfjpyy43ycXxiFAW7GWDSHuV5rBLZCziXLQJVrdWKX.png) And after that, they invited us to participate in a short game where they gave us some sweet and savory treats. It was a unique afternoon that I really enjoyed experiencing. I know they will both be very successful in their new space, and I'm so happy to have been a part of this beginning. These are gestures I truly appreciate—their desire to be present in their most special moments.
![1001101870.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/242NmeFuonM7LfRJ5AvvLeNSzcQon4fveDH5pMPtYUSxhY4fFYGHFWCTiVNozanDbuuwd.png) ![colorido (2).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/EqfMmY8yEq5LHeoFpS7iEadNv2dkKxnS7Xx7BVvVGfq7YstqehGVhibw6QoCwjWQtjC.png)

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/BIrki8th-cvx2.png
¡Gracias por leer, comentar y votar mi contenido! Espero haya sido de tu agrado y provecho. Un gran abrazo a todos, y nos leemos en un próximo post • Lakrearte en Hive • Att: Estefania Garcia ♥
![Banner (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/estefania3/Eoc9Pc2jLqxnjQfBXKUXRL5bvNPwyxeQkBQUdS3nHsKdgJdfrHmJ7dxx5KQp53eW8tJ.jpg) Imágenes y separadores de mi autoría Portada editada en Canva Fotografías tomadas con un Moto EDGE 30 Texto traducido en Google ImTranslate v.14.27

title.title: Oatmeal and Prune Pancakes (Eng/Esp)
title.body:
> For breakfast today, I made a pancake with rolled oats, prunes, and peach, so I went for a pretty fresh and light version to start the morning. I didn’t use any sugar because I think the natural sweetness of the prunes is enough. Join me on this new culinary adventure.
![1000116603.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23wCDqvHdGWJz5wdXdi9nfPChbXo4X1f5ipW97TTJZpyEamx1YWpFoAdhZaKDpKLrd8je.png)
## Ingredients: - 80 grams rolled oats - 4 prunes - 4 tablespoons self-rising flour - 1 peach - Salt to taste - Oil - 1 cup water
![1000116596.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23ydEkcJddiQQMcT6koJycjkJPP7UaUysbNGs8L8CTafyZFAUEGaABMFKap2fw8uVaGgW.jpg)
## Preparation: In a deep bowl, I added the water, rolled oats, and a pinch of salt. I gradually added the self-rising flour to thicken the mixture. Then I chopped the prunes into small pieces and added them to the mixture, stirring well to combine the ingredients and, of course, the flavors.
![1000116591.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23tvrqJTNLRsqcAT9RJRTWTNTnksA26VJzgSvNUgmCL4b3AtcS6SS977ni2hZz9dEss4H.jpg)
Next, I washed the peaches, removed the skins and pits, and cut them into julienne strips to garnish the pancakes once they’re ready.
![1000116594.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23vi5sxBLi2mS8SWe2d4ynRDgobxcGD1G5diWzPbRXtMaJThb3puUaXpCDDVEMmmp2k3a.jpg)
The next step is to place a skillet on the stove, grease the surface, and once it’s hot, add a portion of the batter. I turned the heat down low and cooked for five minutes on each side. This made two small pancakes.
![1000116602.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23vi1ztjZah4HTPr1vhda6tp95eAAYWEKCX4cxP8QCRnCieuQdPyFGRCGwQgSjoQJ9UrY.jpg)
Finally, I served them and placed the peach slices on top. The fruit really enhanced this recipe, adding an extraordinary touch. I like to eat fruit in the morning; I feel like it gives me the energy I need to write my recipes 😅. I’m continuing to let my creative cooking run wild with @ramisey, and I hope to keep combining ingredients to create delicious flavors that not only delight the palate but also the heart. *** ***
## Versión en Español

> Para mi desayuno de hoy preparé una panqueca de hojuelas de avena, ciruelas pasas y durazno, así que busqué una versión bastante fresca y ligera para iniciar la mañana. No usé azúcar pues considero que con el dulzor propio de las ciruelas es suficiente. Acompañénme en esta nueva aventura en la cocina.
![1000116603.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23wCDqvHdGWJz5wdXdi9nfPChbXo4X1f5ipW97TTJZpyEamx1YWpFoAdhZaKDpKLrd8je.png)
## Ingredientes: - 80 gramos de avena en hojuelas - 4 ciruelas pasas - 4 cucharadas de harina de trigo leudante - 1 durazno - Sal al gusto - Aceite - 1 taza de agua
![1000116596.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23ydEkcJddiQQMcT6koJycjkJPP7UaUysbNGs8L8CTafyZFAUEGaABMFKap2fw8uVaGgW.jpg)
## Preparación: En un envase hondo añadí el agua, las hojuelas de avena y una pizca de sal. Paulatinamente fui agregando la harina de trigo leudante para dar mayor consistencia a la mezcla.
![1000116591.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23tvrqJTNLRsqcAT9RJRTWTNTnksA26VJzgSvNUgmCL4b3AtcS6SS977ni2hZz9dEss4H.jpg)
Luego corté las ciruelas pasas en pedazos pequeños y se los añadí a la preparación, mezclé muy bien para integrar los ingredientes y, por supuesto, los sabores.
![1000116594.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23vi5sxBLi2mS8SWe2d4ynRDgobxcGD1G5diWzPbRXtMaJThb3puUaXpCDDVEMmmp2k3a.jpg)
Después lavé y retiré las conchas del durazno y la semilla, procedí a cortarlo en julianas para decorar las panquecas cuando estén listas. El siguiente paso es colocar un sartén en la cocina, aceitar la superficie y una vez caliente agregar una porción de la mezcla. Ajusté a temperatura baja y cociné durante cinco minutos por cada lado. Me alcanzó para dos panquecas pequeñas.
![1000116602.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23vi1ztjZah4HTPr1vhda6tp95eAAYWEKCX4cxP8QCRnCieuQdPyFGRCGwQgSjoQJ9UrY.jpg)
Finalmente serví y coloqué los trozos de durazno arriba. Las frutas enriquecieron esta receta, dando un toque extraordinario. Me gusta comer frutas la mañana, siento que me aportan la energía que necesito para escribir mis recetas 😅. Sigo dando rienda suelta a la cocina creativa de @ramisey, espero continuar combinando ingredientes para crear sabores deliciosos que no solo conquisten el paladar sino también el corazón.   *** *** ✓Photos from my personal gallery, edited with Fotocollage. ✓Text translated with DeepL.

title.title: 「生活」高三的尾声
title.body:
<liketuimages>
<center>
![1QJMxTi0s2bETEjZ_2682c0f6c4330aa4926e0c3bedcc3a.png](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/mrspointm/images/1QJMxTi0s2bETEjZ_2682c0f6c4330aa4926e0c3bedcc3a/1QJMxTi0s2bETEjZ_2682c0f6c4330aa4926e0c3bedcc3a.webp)
![dlVbynq5mkGxK9Ju_2ccca29e0cf9b257008a08fb05721d52.png](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/mrspointm/images/dlVbynq5mkGxK9Ju_2ccca29e0cf9b257008a08fb05721d52/dlVbynq5mkGxK9Ju_2ccca29e0cf9b257008a08fb05721d52.webp)
![vEydboGvhxDwg7Rt_IMG_7479.png](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/mrspointm/images/vEydboGvhxDwg7Rt_IMG_7479/vEydboGvhxDwg7Rt_IMG_7479.webp)
![l1QGPz8eSzfuNcHj_IMG_7481.jpeg](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/mrspointm/images/l1QGPz8eSzfuNcHj_IMG_7481/l1QGPz8eSzfuNcHj_IMG_7481.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

高三生活总算快要落幕了，这周学校难得安排了两天假期，想来也是让学生回家休整。毕竟我们下周就要正式全面停课，后续周末也不再放假，进入全程自主复习的阶段。

我觉得这个时候他们心里或多或少都会感到紧张，只是大多不会表露在外而已。平日里看着大家说说笑笑，估计内心难免心存忐忑，还听说班里不少学生近期都出现了失眠的情况。

昨天上课的时候，有个学生情绪绷不住了，眼眶红红的。课后我私下和她沟通，她坦言最近物理课基本都在刷题考试，前一天三节晚自习全都用来做试卷，压力太大实在难以承受。这一点我能共情，这段时间考试频次太高，学生根本来不及消化知识点，一套卷子还没弄懂，新的练习任务就又下来了。

这接连两次考试，班级成绩算不上差，只是没能达到我的预期。成绩出现起伏本就是常态，不可能一直稳步上升。只希望孩子们尽快调整状态，平稳心态从容迎接高考。

三年下来大家沉淀积累了不少知识，这一届学生整体基础打得格外扎实，日常的知识过关、背诵检测，平日里要求都把控得比较严格。只要他们稳住心态，高考便能收获理想的成绩。

这段日子对我来说反倒轻松不少，学校每周安排模拟考试，老师们轮流监考排班，不用天天值守，每周能多出一天自由时间自行支配。现在下班就彻底收尾工作，不用再画延长线备课了！

这两周不用监考的时段，我都会去瑜伽馆上课，上午下午各上一节，一节普拉提小课的力量训练，一节瑜伽大课舒缓拉伸，运动过身心变得格外放松。如今我的动作熟练度提升不少，虽说还没能做到游刃有余，但自身的成长变化实实在在能体会到。

520当天，我们一家三口一起吃了火锅。我向来看重生活仪式感，愿意借着这样的日子庆祝一番，用心珍藏日常里细碎的美好，我还给Sheya买了一条裙子当礼物！

再熬过两周就能彻底收尾啦，虽说高考结束后我还要参与阅卷工作，但内心已经松弛下来，这样感觉真好～

---

title.title: [ESP-ING] Lamas Square and Church
title.body:
width=472 height=49 border=0>
[//]:# (!worldmappin 10.17679 lat -67.51142 long d3scr)

>






Me llevé una gran sorpresa al saber que en Santa Cruz de Aragua no hay solo una plaza sino dos, y es que la plaza Bolívar de Santa [Cruz](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@yolimarag/esping-square-bolvar-santa-cruz-cmy) ya yo le había hecho un pequeño recorrido y lo había traído por aquí,  pero hace poco pasamos por otra plaza y nos sorprendió ya que pensábamos que era la Bolívar,  pero no era así, así que tenía que preguntar el nombre de esta plaza.



Aproveche que había un señor sentado y me dijo que esta plaza lleva por nombre **\

**, y la iglesia que muchas veces está frente a la Plaza Bolívar, está frente a esta plaza, me confundí tanto que hasta pensaba que estaba en otro pueblo, pero es el pueblo de Santa Cruz y la iglesia es grande y muy bonita, una iglesia muy antigua pero que está muy bien conservada.

> La plaza tiene muchos árboles que le dan vida a la plaza y mangos, mamón, flores entre otros, las banquetas son de cemento pero con una forma muy cómoda para disfrutar de la misma, si note que los pisos no estaban tan limpios como otras plazas, pero seguro ha sido por las lluvias que han habido estos días, y vi como que la han barrido pero como con barro, pero la parte de la jardinería estaba muy limpia y bien cuidada. Los faroles de la plaza se ven muy modernos, son pequeños pero tienen una forma muy bonita, además la plaza tiene un pequeño obelisco, la forma del centro es redonda y en el medio el obelisco, y alrededor están unas banquetas para que las personas se sienten allí.

> La iglesia lleva por nombre nuestra señora de Monserrat, comenzó a construirse en 1782, quedó inconclusa y se volvió a continuar en el año 1925, y su fachada terminó de construirse en el año 1988, me gusto mucho esta iglesia es muy de pueblo, es imponente y por dentro tiene muchos vitrales que le dan vida y color a la iglesia. También tiene muchas imágenes de santos, varias esculturas, una de las cosas que me llamó la atención es el confesionario se ve antiguo y moderno al mismo tiempo, las lámparas son de hierro con varias tomas de luces, de esas que se ven muy antigua, otra de las cosas que me gustó es la claridad hay muchas puertas inmensas que dan a un lado y al frente, en este momento estaban leyendo y haciendo parte de un servicio estaban llegando personas a la iglesia y las campanadas acababan de sonar, es un lugar que representa mucha historia. Han visitado esta parte de lamas??

width=472 height=49 border=0>
--- >! [ENGLISH] > >I was really surprised to learn that there isn’t just one square in Santa Cruz de Aragua, but two—specifically, Plaza Bolívar in Santa [Cruz](https://peakd.com/hive -163772/@yolimarag/esping-square-bolvar-santa-cruz-cmy) I had already taken a quick tour of it and posted about it here, but recently we passed by another square and were surprised because we thought it was Bolívar Square, but it wasn’t, so I had to ask what this square was called. > >I took the opportunity to ask a man who was sitting there, and he told me that this square is called **\

**, and the church that is often in front of Plaza Bolívar is actually in front of this square. I was so confused that I even thought I was in another town, but it is the town of Santa Cruz, and the church is large and very beautiful—a very old church that is very well preserved.\n>\n>

> > >The square has lots of trees that bring it to life, including mango and papaya trees, as well as flowers and other plants. The sidewalks are made of concrete but are shaped in a way that makes them very comfortable to sit on. I did notice that the ground wasn’t as clean as in other squares, but I’m sure that’s because of the rain we’ve had lately, and I saw that they’d swept it, though there was still some mud left, but the landscaping was very clean and well-maintained. > >The streetlights in the plaza look very modern; they’re small but have a very nice shape. The plaza also has a small obelisk—the center is round with the obelisk in the middle, and there are benches around it for people to sit on. > >

> > >The church is named Our Lady of Monserrat. Construction began in 1782, but it remained unfinished; work resumed in 1925, and the façade was completed in 1988. I really liked this church—it has a very small-town feel to it, is imposing, and inside it has many stained-glass windows that bring life and color to the church. > >It also has many images of saints and several sculptures. One of the things that caught my attention is the confessional—it looks both old and modern at the same time. The lamps are made of iron with multiple light sockets, the kind that look very old. Another thing I liked was the brightness; there are many huge doors opening to the side and the front. at that moment, people were reading and participating in a service; people were arriving at the church, and the bells had just rung—it’s a place steeped in history. > >Have you visited this part of Lamas?? > >

links.body:
![image](https://pixabay.com/get/g22d4a3151e7507a6ca9884215f95c341a53892bee1cab4e150996038957bb6d6a540182a60f5ca8bf1a7a44009ac0868f5438d1a4f487add1dd4f3b99766c212_640.jpg)
오늘 산책하면서 정말 특별한 경험을 했어요. 먼저, 오랜 친구를 우연히 만나서 반가운 인사를 나눴습니다. 친구와 함께 카페에 들어가 커피를 마시며 최근의 소소한 이야기를 나누었는데, 이렇게 오랜만에 만나니 정말 즐거웠습니다. 또한, 길을 걷다가 새롭게 개장한 아트 갤러리를 발견했습니다. 거리의 벽에 그려진 멋진 스트리트 아트와 함께 다양한 전시들이 어우러져 있어서 시간이 가는 줄 모르고 구경하게 되었어요. 예술작품들 속에 담긴 메시지와 색감이 굉장히 인상적이었습니다. 오늘의 산책은 친구와의 재회와 예술을 즐길 수 있는 뜻깊은 시간이었습니다! _This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). Check out the original version [here on actifit.io](https://actifit.io/@titusfrost/actifit-titusfrost-20231229t015511428z)_

links.title: Murals that highlight regional identity (Eng/Esp)
links.body:
>

<center>
![1000116628.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23tveaoFfGxiqWiytvV6YzxMmzS5weMrKuhyxftrBQUp8W2UTTBnBNixgDid8jEmqqZ7R.jpg)
</center>

On Carupano Avenue, directly across from Gualberto Ibarreto Square, at the entrance to the **The Peñon** neighborhood, there are some beautiful murals that stretch along the entrance to the The Villa Cristobal Colon housing development. Visual artist Yubel Betancourt was responsible for designing and painting various cultural symbols, honoring the identity and roots of the people of Cumana. Among his works, you can see a boat with fishermen hard at work, one of the activities that distinguishes Sucre State. 


<center>
![1000109688.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Ep3bwLaL4s7dwuwohxe1Awgzui1QZ6nrkfnZhGEST36TwHioLXoPmtYPaPeVZUGBMUP.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![1000109680.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EqHzqvYVm71UsZty9UjyfsxPeFARf9JpnmDRSasLGZtPrXsMxEVavGmSwkSpr9ZZCXR.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![1000109675.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eqb1e1SienFqatbw6xXMKdfFb6A6mLchuSmTy3xHJRCjPhyP9V1TnqsRGR9HpxVnJgM.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![1000109671.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eoc9yP3kYQzsc8HotYAexDXA3d3LAdvBdTM3YNPiSvGa2ETAYApDRKp3cvPwAwmuLf9.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![1000109668.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EoiUpMRfDwYrqdp3HizUr2Zvq891UviexB8wU5YMkJVHmzFxb3h6oPfsKqTX13nGkJQ.jpg)
</center>

The colorful style is consistent, and there is a very harmonious transition between the paintings. The seascape is a common theme, and thus one can see a shark, an octopus, a turtle, and colorful fish. An image of the Virgin of Las Mercedes, patron saint of **The Peñon**, adorns this large mosaic, along with the face of an Indigenous woman and two people of African descent: a girl and a woman.

<center>
![1000109689.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EqBcDsFTEK9J7KinwvUFfpdhhVXZ41bAastXfSMrUAaz3JvBuXf7CVfVsBuYzjhRV5R.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![1000109687.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EokdaPxhZJJVg8FtLkoTPnq1U6XcGxQVk7Q7SAEzjS2pdKtR1ynDf6eDJhghpN4rzan.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![1000109663.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eos1NVm2CvUAW2nwuEpaS1i69yWeHUedshoMauBxTSRrvpprZa6VpH6TmuRuGs851Eq.jpg)
</center>

In the style of the Wall of the Cultivators, located across from the Ayacucho Museum, artist Yubel Betancourt replicated Ronel Rivas’s work but added his own personal touch; moreover, the selection of honorees offers a different perspective. The renowned Gualberto Ibarreto, Maria Rodriguez, Luis Mariano Rivera, Francisco \
Rodriguez, and Remigio Fuentes appear in the mural, but it is also worth noting the presence of Josefina Jimenez \

local artists whose work deserves recognition.
![1000109660.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EoptNs4PfybJVhE6m6h1j24iMU4ynx7afPK8espNyUMGcB8x28gZvVHKqZkT5KmNcqd.jpg)
![1000109657.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EowFAkHrmATGjt7M6WjnqkVoc9qVs6TVzh83Toah9PExrEQxP9mFrhUg6X7zdri6uo4.jpg)
![1000109656.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EokdCC8EHiAu1tR9GeF3d2kkjkdvY3C23ZQEdaXfGU3TAEwqWQzgjZCfHEFktjjca1e.jpg)
![1000109654.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EoeEyLNYytff31xP9oLXxghcdwyvFLkjBVzsVyw4SqApw8PLPnsyVD14Wydzz8cBfKP.jpg)
![1000109652.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EoEsMcM4RSJgVntXi4SPpDKvwyswfytG58KuxAzekgmMrQsPT4J3oz2BKvUJtnxMGKJ.jpg)
![1000109648.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eq9UiSmpFguYhETSYYYoXU2wBwqvM53nZyoYQW2rrjZQS2LdVf6VXgojMSVJqEp4tAc.jpg)
![1000109646.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EowFctLU9qCKqtSW9sfrHZ52cY3CRETousJvLbsaHiiSSvFsGNk5SupWe348YWLVJJ8.jpg)
![1000109645.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eokd5DJiQbXNySLMa8fyaDLmfoAKaQSnTmZbw6tBpg7o4eJT3LLY2WG5a4EAWawxupN.jpg)
![1000109643.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EowGeBpjrxJkMhqGXzWvbrz31JbiWc4McMZjLJ1FSJjtZqz1gvvzeegqM6YU6oNwXWj.jpg)
To complete his design, the artist painted an iguana, some macaws, and a leopard to indicate that the state of Sucre also has rivers, jungles, and mountains. Each painting is characterized by its vibrant colors and sense of movement, with this dynamism becoming even more pronounced when the viewer is traveling in a vehicle.
![1000109661.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EowFAmKu3cyZBE9Sm5bUcNsqJdXVZHRPkWm2x2KAoLcjK8TFCBZybqPuDWeKco9Cp1H.jpg)
![1000109662.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EoiUDVm5MZtRChMT41QkQDTxxwpufhzc8zJYdQHtGxuTYSSpRKwFLRMLaqiye1Aht9j.jpg)
![1000109658.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eorzmm3fAkp8esjKvK8uMowHsS55XWFqVsymF2Co6aw2eVS9J7i6LFVB9jRNfhk6ZVJ.jpg)
![1000109640.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EpEFqCt45KCqKFq4hHoVbLGMGTJvDbEgdE1sXEsHrYXZizLHjZWeV2V7KBJk3eSLkxD.jpg)
![1000109638.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eou8mh3SH5KvQyurw74dTVQLb2qpzy8y3bsJ59a7qiW4nKemdLowDJXpiMHBeZJdzQE.jpg)
Located at the entrance to the The Peñon neighborhood, this large mural serves as the backdrop to the equally striking Gualberto Ibarreto Square, creating a truly spectacular multicolored scene that is a delight to the eye; in addition to its artistic merit, the mural conveys a sense of optimism through its symbolism.
![1000109655.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EokbfS1RAUZBZa1MfRBsSpEikRzQbVf8uKXjwyWMUzGAkaS18EUZwxo2N3WmCLRovBh.jpg)
*** ***
## Versión en Español

>


<center>
![1000116628.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23tveaoFfGxiqWiytvV6YzxMmzS5weMrKuhyxftrBQUp8W2UTTBnBNixgDid8jEmqqZ7R.jpg)
</center>

En la Avenida Carúpano, justo al frente de la Plaza Gualberto Ibarreto, en la entrada al sector **El Peñón**, se encuentran unos hermosos murales que se extienden a lo largo de la entrada de la urbanización La Villa Cristóbal Colón. El artista plástico Yubel Betancourt se encargó de diseñar y pintar diversos símbolos culturales, honrando la identidad y las raíces del pueblo cumanés. Entre sus propuestas se pueden observar un bote con pescadores en plena faena, una de las actividades que distingue al estado Sucre. 


<center>
![1000109688.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Ep3bwLaL4s7dwuwohxe1Awgzui1QZ6nrkfnZhGEST36TwHioLXoPmtYPaPeVZUGBMUP.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![1000109680.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EqHzqvYVm71UsZty9UjyfsxPeFARf9JpnmDRSasLGZtPrXsMxEVavGmSwkSpr9ZZCXR.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![1000109675.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eqb1e1SienFqatbw6xXMKdfFb6A6mLchuSmTy3xHJRCjPhyP9V1TnqsRGR9HpxVnJgM.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![1000109671.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eoc9yP3kYQzsc8HotYAexDXA3d3LAdvBdTM3YNPiSvGa2ETAYApDRKp3cvPwAwmuLf9.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![1000109668.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EoiUpMRfDwYrqdp3HizUr2Zvq891UviexB8wU5YMkJVHmzFxb3h6oPfsKqTX13nGkJQ.jpg)
</center>

El estilo colorido es constante y se nota una transición muy armoniosa entre las pinturas. El paisaje marino es un factor común y por ello se observa un tiburón, un pulpo, una tortuga y peces coloridos. Una imagen de la Virgen de Las Mercedes, patrona de **El Peñón**, adorna este gran mosaico, además de un rostro de una india y de dos afrodescendientes: una niña y una mujer.

<center>
![1000109689.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EqBcDsFTEK9J7KinwvUFfpdhhVXZ41bAastXfSMrUAaz3JvBuXf7CVfVsBuYzjhRV5R.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![1000109687.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EokdaPxhZJJVg8FtLkoTPnq1U6XcGxQVk7Q7SAEzjS2pdKtR1ynDf6eDJhghpN4rzan.jpg)
</center>


<center>
![1000109663.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eos1NVm2CvUAW2nwuEpaS1i69yWeHUedshoMauBxTSRrvpprZa6VpH6TmuRuGs851Eq.jpg)
</center>

Al mejor estilo del Muro de los Cultores, ubicado frente al Museo Ayacucho, el artista Yubel Betancourt replicó lo realizado por Ronel Rivas, pero le concedió su toque personal y además la selección de homenajeados tiene otra perspectiva. Los reconocidos Gualberto Ibarreto, María Rodríguez, Luis Mariano Rivera, Francisco \
Rodríguez y Remigio Fuentes aparecen en el mural, pero también es para destacar la presencia de Josefina Jiménez \

, cultores locales cuyo trabajo merece reconocimiento.

links.title: [Movie] FLOW (2024) A Captivating Story
links.body:
Warm greetings! Today I'll be reviewing one of the most beautiful films I've ever seen. I truly never thought I'd like it so much. I'd been putting it off for a while until one day I decided to watch it with my children. It's called

### FLOW (2024)

![MV5BMmM2MWYyNDMtMmJmZS00N2FiLTg5OTYtYjNiNzM1NmVhYThkXkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/23tknHBW58fgVimpBeW16ZM1irxDuriQcTSFTfwyY8K1tRV1kaFAKw3kqiczGYH7ifRvM.jpg)

I had refused to watch it because I kept asking myself how a film where not a single word is spoken could convey anything, and let me tell you, I was very wrong.

It's a film that confronts us with that great dilemma of humanity when it has destroyed its own planet. No humans appear in the story either; we only see animals in a world where various natural phenomena occur that are beyond their understanding, and they simply try to adapt and survive.

In the story, we see various characters, such as:

**The Cat** (Protagonist): He is a black, solitary, very independent cat with a very ordinary appearance. At first, he is afraid of water and distrustful of everyone, but he is the central figure of the group and the one who must learn to trust others in order to survive.

![MV5BYzczNjNkYzQtYjEzMi00MTAyLWI2ODAtNGY2YzkyMmViNTVhXkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/48aZQdMJPXP2kVe3U7FiegHRiV4h5rvPJg9tCLq2RmBN5kudTNLD4Cn5oHDcikBK1H.jpg)

**The Capybara**: It's the peaceful soul of the group. It's extremely relaxed, good-natured, and lazy (spending a lot of time sleeping). It's not bothered by the conflicts of others and becomes the peacemaker of the group, keeping the crew together and demonstrating great nobility.

**The Dog** (A Labrador Retriever): It's cheerful, noisy, hyperactive, and bursting with energy. Unlike his original pack, he is extremely friendly and just wants to play and make friends, even with the apathetic cat; he represents absolute loyalty.

**The Lemur**: A ring-tailed lemur who turns out to be a compulsive hoarder. He is obsessed with collecting and protecting all kinds of shiny objects and trinkets he finds along the way. At first, he is selfish, but he changes throughout the journey. I found him to be the cutest and funniest of the group.

**The Secretary Bird**: A large and majestic bird that joins the group after being injured and separated from its flock. Although it has trouble flying due to its injury, it becomes a kind of wise guide or helmsman for the group. I would say it is the most powerful figure in the story.

![MV5BYmQ0OThjNjMtYzc5Ni00ZDgzLTliNzQtN2U3MzZmZGVhODYzXkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/48JdW6foPjvAymmj1EnfCGGgJQy4doqzUQHGZbPfhnExdgeUmx5UA6fbW97yHxKVKb.jpg)

Together, these animals struggle to survive the natural disasters they encounter along their journey. It's a dramatic, sometimes harrowing story with a profound message about caring for the environment and our only home: Earth.

It's a pleasure to share this brief review with you.

____

**I used Google Translate (my language is Spanish).** Images taken from the website https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt4772188/?ref_=mv_close

_Rating: **100/100**_

---

> Saludos cordial para toda mi gente hermosa, espero que tengan un feliz fin de semana disfrutando cada día de las bondades que nos regala la vida en cuanto a nuestra familia y cada comida en el hogar, el día de hoy tuve un pequeño percance dentro de mi hogar ya que por situaciones de reparación edad directo fue suspendido por unas horas lo cual me llevó a tener que ingeniárselas en casa para preparar un almuerzo en mi familia, de esta manera aproveché que tenía pechuga de pollo para hacer estas hamburguesas de pollo, por lo tanto los invito a ver mi preparación. > Warm greetings to all my beautiful people! I hope you have a happy weekend, enjoying every day the blessings that life gives us in terms of our family and every meal at home. Today I had a small mishap at home because, due to repairs, the power was out for a few hours, which forced me to get creative and prepare lunch for my family. Since I had some chicken breast on hand, I made these chicken burgers, so I invite you to watch me prepare them.
![GridArt_20260522_231230913.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariaser/AK6YNTpJF2RaFYLDy9ukhmoJxV3jHyb9SNkyN4Hvpjiv53ao5CPbECxk745jFoa.jpg)
Ingredientes: 1 Pechuga de pollo, 1 pimentón, 1 cebolla, cebollín, ajo, 1 zanahoria, sal, sazonador, aceite. > Ingredients: 1 chicken breast, 1 bell pepper, 1 onion, spring onion, garlic, 1 carrot, salt, seasoning, oil.
![GridArt_20260522_230722323.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariaser/23wMcWq1PwSLkDgwBnjsWpVMdc9AVsx1mUX5KooMJgdEfNxvL9gXckLb2Papafp8u3Lgt.jpg)
Comencé lavando extrayendo las semillas y picando en cuadritos muy pequeños el pimentón la cebolla y el cebollín por otra parte Pelé la zanahoria y la pasé por el lado grueso de rayo, todo esto lo llevé con un toque de aceite a sofreír. > I started by washing, removing the seeds and finely dicing the bell pepper, onion and scallion. Separately, I peeled the carrot and sliced it on the coarse side of a grater. I then sautéed all of this with a touch of oil.
![GridArt_20260522_230801826.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariaser/AJj1ai8iQRvSjCVQJhBEL5QMa5Vev8CsU8xaHzdNRrmsmKk3FvJi4ZXFZvcjPvy.jpg)
Coloqué la pechuga de pollo en mi procesador, allí aproveché de condimentar con un poco de ajo sal sazonador, dejé que todo se integrara y se triturara perfectamente para añadir los aliños previamente sofritos, resalté los sabores con un poco más de sal y listo. > I placed the chicken breast in my food processor, seasoned it with a little garlic, salt, and seasoning, and let it all blend and be perfectly crushed before adding the previously sautéed seasonings. I enhanced the flavors with a little more salt and that's it.
![GridArt_20260522_230854698.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariaser/AJha1JpG4PYDFLKzef8bTuxuKHWkpsbbjqk5kzBGZRKBc8r4ieHP1G2wpH2EsLw.jpg)
Luego formé pelotitas con la mezcla de la pechuga de pollo y con ayuda de mi toste arepa, engrase con toque de aceite y comencé a colocar el pollo, aplane creando una versión de carnes de hamburguesa pero esta vez con pollo, dejé cocinar solo por unos minutos y listo. > Then I formed little balls with the chicken breast mixture and, using my arepa toaster, I greased it with a touch of oil and started placing the chicken. I flattened it, creating a version of hamburger patties but this time with chicken. I let it cook for just a few minutes and that's it.
![GridArt_20260522_230955988.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariaser/AK6XRjD7yDEtGdq8QU3mjR5YVuaVdnSvd6TqFXJRnSaGeHB3VJC92GgmS5zdbBw.jpg)
Sin duda aún alguna dentro de la cocina siempre debemos ser creativos buscar estrategias para solventar y seguir disfrutando de la buena comida hecha en casa. > Without a doubt, even in the kitchen we must always be creative, looking for strategies to solve problems and continue enjoying good homemade food.
![GridArt_20260522_231035434.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariaser/AJpkVvPDzaYY1m32i4S3mv51XkoWnozCWNuyPWos8kZHL7TBhYDFgQxK2vzNMmu.jpg)
![IMG-20210518-WA0013.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariaser/23vsmbX5FEuYW4QJWvpf9gV1SsdcvFYWz2pdHSV6Rbh7pKEvx1MfBLag9bwed31NV4LFw.jpg)
Gracias por leerme y su valioso apoyo. Las fotos son de mi autoria @mariaser Traducido con Deepl traductor > Thank you for reading me and your valuable support. The photos are by me @mariaser Translated with Deepl translator

links.title: The House Also Speaks #1 | The kitchen where we always end up talking about problems [EN / ES]
links.body:
🇬🇧 In English  

---

Hello dear Holos & Lotus community,

Today I want to share the first chapter of a new personal series called *The House Also Speaks*, a space where everyday objects, corners of the home, and simple routines become reflections about life, memory, exhaustion, family, and all those silent emotions that slowly settle inside a house over the years.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQosht52kXhWG95Uxgk5R3Q9VzGAhEGT9RshUQrNcqNbe/thevirtualdenise_garlic_2556022_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/garlic-cactus-window-green-house-2556022/)

---


## The House Also Speaks #1
*The kitchen where we always end up talking about problems*

There are kitchens where people only prepare food.
And there are others where worries are also cooked.

In my house, almost every important conversation ends up happening in the kitchen. I don’t know exactly why. Maybe because it is the place where there is always something pending. Something boiling. Something that needs to be stirred before it sticks.

Sometimes I think kitchens are very similar to families.
They are never completely calm.

Ours is not large or elegant. It has humidity stains in one corner, an old window that barely lets fresh air come inside, and utensils that have survived so many years that they already feel like part of the family itself. Some pots are scratched. Some plates are chipped. The table has marks from years of daily use.

And yet, despite all that wear, the kitchen remains the center of the house.

That is where we talk about prices.
About blackouts.
About medicines.
About tiredness.
About the uncertainty of tomorrow.
About relatives who left.
About those who stayed.
About how difficult daily life has become.

And strangely enough, many of those conversations happen while someone cuts onions, prepares coffee, washes rice, or checks a pot on the stove.

As if the body needed to stay occupied to better endure certain worries.

I remember my mother moving through the kitchen with an almost silent skill. She could be exhausted and still continue cooking. She could feel overwhelmed and still ask if everyone had eaten.

When we are young, we think food simply appears on the table.
With time, we understand how much sacrifice many women hid behind a served plate.

Sometimes I think entire families were sustained by women who learned to swallow their own exhaustion while stirring soup.

That is why kitchens carry so much emotional weight.
Because people rarely rest there completely.

Even silence inside a kitchen feels different.
There is always the sound of something.
The fan turning slowly.
The dripping water.
The spoons touching the metal pots.
The refrigerator making tired noises in the middle of the night.
The pressure of wondering what will be cooked tomorrow.

There are days when I enter the kitchen only to sit quietly for a moment.
Not because I am hungry.
Maybe because it is the most honest place in the entire house.

The living room can pretend calmness.
Bedrooms can hide tears.
But kitchens eventually reveal the truth about how people are really living.

That is where you notice when something is missing.
When money is not enough.
When someone is carrying too much worry.
When life starts pressing harder than usual.

And yet, at the same time, kitchens are also places of resistance.

Because as long as there is someone making coffee,
heating rice,
sharing bread,
or simply asking “Have you eaten yet?”,
there is still love trying to survive inside that house.

I believe many families are not held together by big speeches or perfect moments.
Sometimes they survive because someone continues showing up every day in the kitchen, even while tired, even while worried, even while carrying silent fears.

Maybe that is why certain smells remain forever inside memory.
Coffee.
Garlic frying.
Fresh soup.
Rice cooking slowly.

Those smells are not just food.
They are proof that someone kept trying.

Over the years I have understood that houses are never truly silent.
Walls absorb conversations.
Tables absorb routines.
And kitchens, more than any other place, absorb the emotional temperature of a family.

Sometimes I think that if kitchens could speak, they would tell the real history of many homes.
Not the polished version people show outside.
But the fragile, tired, loving, imperfect truth.

And maybe that is why, no matter how difficult life becomes, we always end up returning there.

Because deep inside, kitchens are not only places where food is prepared.
They are places where people continue trying to care for one another.

---

Photos: Pixabay
English translation: DeepL Translate

---

Thank you for reading.
Special thanks to @bradleyarrow for supporting the community.

---

🇪🇸 **En Español**

Hola querida comunidad de Holos & Lotus,

Hoy quiero compartir el primer capítulo de una nueva serie personal llamada *La casa también habla*, un espacio donde los objetos cotidianos, los rincones del hogar y las rutinas simples se convierten en reflexiones sobre la vida, la memoria, el cansancio, la familia y todas esas emociones silenciosas que poco a poco se van quedando dentro de una casa con el paso de los años.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQosht52kXhWG95Uxgk5R3Q9VzGAhEGT9RshUQrNcqNbe/thevirtualdenise_garlic_2556022_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/garlic-cactus-window-green-house-2556022/)

---

## La casa también habla #1
*La cocina donde siempre terminamos hablando de problemas*

Hay cocinas donde solo se prepara comida.
Y hay otras donde también se cocinan preocupaciones.

En mi casa casi todas las conversaciones importantes terminan ocurriendo en la cocina. No sé exactamente por qué. Tal vez porque es el lugar donde siempre hay algo pendiente. Algo hirviendo. Algo que remover antes de que se pegue.

A veces pienso que las cocinas se parecen mucho a las familias.
Nunca están completamente en calma.

La nuestra no es grande ni elegante. Tiene manchas de humedad en una esquina, una ventana vieja por donde apenas entra aire fresco y utensilios que han sobrevivido tantos años que ya parecen parte de la propia familia. Algunas ollas están rayadas. Algunos platos están partidos en una esquina. La mesa tiene marcas del uso diario acumulado durante años.

Y aun así, a pesar de todo ese desgaste, la cocina sigue siendo el centro de la casa.

Allí se habla de los precios.
De los apagones.
De las medicinas.
Del cansancio.
De la incertidumbre del mañana.
De los familiares que se fueron.
De los que todavía permanecen.
De lo difícil que se ha vuelto la vida cotidiana.

Y curiosamente, muchas de esas conversaciones ocurren mientras alguien corta cebolla, prepara café, lava arroz o revisa una olla sobre la hornilla.

Como si el cuerpo necesitara mantenerse ocupado para soportar mejor ciertas preocupaciones.

Recuerdo a mi madre moviéndose por la cocina con una habilidad casi silenciosa. Podía estar agotada y aun así seguir cocinando. Podía sentirse abrumada y de todas formas preguntar si todos ya habían comido.

Cuando una es joven cree que la comida simplemente aparece sobre la mesa.
Con los años una entiende cuánto sacrificio escondieron muchas mujeres detrás de un plato servido.

A veces pienso que familias enteras fueron sostenidas por mujeres que aprendieron a tragarse su propio cansancio mientras removían una sopa.

Por eso las cocinas cargan tanto peso emocional.
Porque allí casi nunca se descansa completamente.

Incluso el silencio dentro de una cocina se siente diferente.
Siempre queda el sonido de algo.
El ventilador girando lento.
El agua cayendo.
Las cucharas chocando contra las ollas.
El refrigerador haciendo ruidos cansados en medio de la noche.
La presión de pensar qué se cocinará mañana.

Hay días en que entro a la cocina solamente para sentarme un momento en silencio.
Ni siquiera por hambre.
Tal vez porque es el lugar más honesto de toda la casa.

La sala puede aparentar tranquilidad.
Los cuartos pueden esconder lágrimas.
Pero las cocinas terminan revelando la verdad sobre cómo vive realmente una familia.

Allí se nota cuando falta algo.
Cuando el dinero no alcanza.
Cuando alguien está cargando demasiada preocupación.
Cuando la vida empieza a apretar más de la cuenta.

Y aun así, al mismo tiempo, las cocinas también son lugares de resistencia.

Porque mientras haya alguien preparando café,
calentando arroz,
compartiendo pan,
o simplemente preguntando “¿ya comiste?”,
todavía existe amor intentando sobrevivir dentro de esa casa.

Creo que muchas familias no se sostienen por grandes discursos ni por momentos perfectos.
A veces sobreviven porque alguien sigue apareciendo cada día en la cocina, incluso cansado, incluso preocupado, incluso cargando miedos silenciosos.

Tal vez por eso ciertos olores se quedan para siempre dentro de la memoria.
El café.
El ajo friéndose.
La sopa recién hecha.
El arroz cocinándose lentamente.

Esos olores no son solamente comida.
Son pruebas de que alguien siguió intentando.

Con los años he entendido que las casas nunca están verdaderamente en silencio.
Las paredes absorben conversaciones.
Las mesas absorben rutinas.
Y las cocinas, más que ningún otro lugar, absorben la temperatura emocional de una familia.

A veces pienso que si las cocinas pudieran hablar, contarían la verdadera historia de muchos hogares.
No la versión arreglada que las personas muestran hacia afuera.
Sino la verdad frágil, cansada, amorosa e imperfecta.

Y quizás por eso, por muy difícil que se vuelva la vida, siempre terminamos regresando allí.

Porque en el fondo las cocinas no son solamente lugares donde se prepara comida.
Son lugares donde las personas siguen intentando cuidarse unas a otras.

---

Traducción al inglés: DeepL Translate

links.title: Television Review: Mother's Mercy (Game of Thrones, S5x10, 2015)
links.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/2OYef01b36YKZk6vcthpaqkY98A.jpg)


**Mother’s Mercy (S5x10)**

Airdate: 14 June 2015

Written by: David Benioff & D.B. Weiss
Directed by: David Nutter

Running Time: 60 minutes


For years, detractors of *Game of Thrones* enjoyed drawing a semi-humorous parallel between the sprawling fantasy epic and the glossy American primetime soap *Dynasty*. The comparison began as a witty observation—noting the structural similarities between the Red Wedding and *Dynasty*’s own Moldavian Wedding Massacre—but as the series progressed, the joke began to curdle into a prescient critique. By Season 5, as showrunners David Benioff and D.B. Weiss sailed further from the shores of George R.R. Martin’s source text, the show’s narrative began to exhibit the hallmarks of routine television: a reliance on shock over substance, a compression of complex political machinations into melodramatic beats, and a growing burden of clichés. This process reached its apotheosis in the Season 5 finale, *Mother’s Mercy*. The episode is a great display of engineered tension, a series of ‘clever’ cliffhangers designed to dominate water-cooler conversation and social media buzz for the ensuing year. Its final image—Jon Snow bleeding out on the snow—is undeniably iconic. Yet, in its calculated manipulation, it invites a more damning comparison than *Dynasty*: the infamous ‘Who Shot J.R.?’ storyline from *Dallas*. This was no longer a fantasy saga drawing from the well of history and myth; it was a primetime soap with dragons, where narrative integrity was sacrificed at the altar of the ‘wham’ moment.

The episode’s primary directive is clear: advance as many storylines as possible towards a season-ending precipice. The sole exception is the complete and puzzling absence of Bran Stark, Hodor, and Meera Reed beyond the Wall, a thread benched for the entire season. This omission highlights the show’s increasingly piecemeal approach to its vast tapestry, favouring immediate, visceral pay-offs over slower, world-building arcs. Every other character is marshalled towards a moment of crisis or revelation, resulting in a breathless, if often contrived, narrative sprint.

In Braavos, Arya Stark’s plot takes a darkly personal turn. Posing as the dead girl Ghita, she infiltrates a brothel where Ser Meryn Trant reveals a predilection for beating young girls as much as abusing them. Her subsequent assassination is a gruesome act of vengeance, methodical and cruel. However, upon returning to the House of Black and White, she is confronted by Jaqen H’ghar, who accuses her of stealing a face and acting for personal justice, not the god’s. The ensuing sequence—Jaqen drinking poison, his body cycling through faces including Arya’s own, leaving her blinded—is visually striking and thematically potent. It underscores the cost of her identity and the harsh pedagogy of the Faceless Men. Yet, it also feels like an arbitrary punishment designed to leave her in a state of helpless vulnerability, another cliffhanger to be resolved later.

The North provides the episode’s most significant military and political conclusion, albeit one that remains deeply controversial. Melisandre’s observation that the weather has warmed slightly is a chillingly brief justification for the horror of Shireen’s sacrifice. It fails to convince Stannis’s army, half of which deserts, repulsed. The subsequent chain of events—Queen Selyse’s suicide, Melisandre’s abandonment, and Stannis’s stubborn march on Winterfell—paints a portrait of a man whose defining trait, his iron will, becomes his fatal flaw. The battle itself is a tactical anticlimax, efficiently presented through a sweeping aerial shot: Bolton cavalry effortlessly routs Stannis’s exhausted, horseless remnant. The plausibility of this defeat is one of the episode’s stronger points, a logical conclusion to a campaign gutted by desperation and poor morale. However, the narrative then indulges in a moment of pure televisual convenience. Brienne of Tarth, having vowed to avenge Renly, happens upon the wounded Stannis in the woods. Her execution is presented with ambiguous editing—the sword swing, the cut away—leaving his death technically off-screen. This ambiguity feels like a hedge, a refusal to fully commit that undermines the gravity of the moment. Brienne’s presence is a melodramatic contrivance, providing a neat, personal closure that the messy reality of war would seldom allow.

The commotion at Winterfell allows Sansa Stark a desperate bid for freedom. Confronted on the battlements by Theon and the sadistic Myranda, who taunts her with promises of disfigurement, Sansa’s plight triggers Theon’s long-submerged conscience. He seizes Myranda and throws her to her death—a moment of visceral catharsis. Their subsequent leap from the walls into the deep snow below is another masterfully constructed cliffhanger, its consequences left tantalisingly ambiguous. While a powerful image of desperate hope, it again exemplifies the episode’s modus operandi: place characters in mortal peril, then freeze the frame.

In Dorne, the storyline reaches its clumsy, shock-value conclusion. Jaime, Bronn, Myrcella, and Trystane depart for King’s Landing. Ellaria Sand’s farewell kiss to Myrcella is loaded with sinister irony, confirmed when Myrcella, aboard ship, shares a tender moment with Jaime, admitting she always knew he was her father. This brief glimpse of emotional honesty makes her subsequent, agonising death by poison all the more brutal. Ellaria on the dock, taking the antidote, completes the tableau of perfidy. This deviation from the books—where Myrcella is maimed but survives—serves no clear narrative purpose beyond killing another Lannister child for shock value. It renders Jaime’s entire Dornish excursion a futile exercise in stupidity, and Ellaria’s actions seem politically suicidal, inviting devastating Lannister retaliation against her own family. It is cruelty for cruelty’s sake, a hollow ‘gotcha’ moment.

The episode’s centrepiece, both in length and impact, is Cersei Lannister’s walk of atonement. Broken by her imprisonment, she confesses to adultery (but not incest) and appeals for the ‘Mother’s mercy’ of the title. The High Sparrow’s mercy is a calculated humiliation: a naked, shorn walk from the Great Sept to the Red Keep. The scene is powerfully acted by Lena Headey, who conveys a devastating arc from defiant pride to shattered vulnerability. It is also one of Martin’s most direct borrowings from history, inspired by the penance of Jane Shore. However, the production was mired in controversy. Croatian conservatives protested the filming in Dubrovnik, though authorities later cynically exploited it for tourism. More notably, the technical execution proved distracting for some viewers. Headey, for personal reasons, used a body double, Rebecca Van Cleave, with her face digitally superimposed. While Headey’s performance in close-up is magnificent, the CGI composite in wider shots occasionally lacks seamless immersion, a small but noticeable flaw in such a pivotal scene. The sequence’s conclusion, however, is flawless: a broken Cersei, swaddled in robes, is shown the reanimated Mountain by Qyburn. In that moment, her eyes harden with a terrifying, vengeful resolve. It is the episode’s best character beat, a promise of fury to come.

In Meereen, the power vacuum left by Daenerys’s departure is filled by a sensible, if uninspired, plan: Jorah and Daario will search for her, while Tyrion will govern. Daenerys herself is stranded in the Dothraki Sea with a wounded, recalcitrant Drogon. Her capture by a massive *khalasar* is less a cliffhanger than a reset button, plunging her back to a status similar to her Season 1 beginnings.

Finally, at the Wall, the episode engineers its most famous cliffhanger. After sending Samwell Tarly to Oldtown—a rare moment of quiet hope—Jon Snow is lured by the false news of his uncle Benjen’s return. He is ambushed by mutineers led by Ser Alliser Thorne and the invented character Olly, stabbed repeatedly for his perceived betrayal in aiding the Wildlings. He falls, bleeding onto the snow, ‘for the Watch.’ As the screen cuts to black, the audience is left with the year-long question: is he truly dead? While this betrayal occurs in Martin’s books, the show’s simplification—replacing complex political grievances with a more straightforward grievance over the Wildlings—makes it feel more like a plot device than an inevitable political consequence. Jon Snow was, by this point, arguably the show’s central hero and certainly its most popular character among a large segment of the audience, especially female. The idea of his permanent death was commercially and narratively unthinkable, transforming the mystery from ‘if’ he would return to ‘how’. The parallel to *Dallas*’s ‘Who Shot J.R.?’ is inescapable: a hugely popular character is seemingly killed to generate unprecedented publicity and viewer speculation, a quintessential soap opera gambit.

*Mother’s Mercy* is one of the most critically acclaimed episodes of *Game of Thrones*, winning Emmys for Best Direction and Best Writing. The direction award is justified; David Nutter manages the sprawling, tonally disparate storylines with confident pacing and delivers several indelible images—the aerial shot of Stannis’s defeat, the stark horror of Cersei’s walk, the chilling stillness of Jon’s ‘death’. The writing award, however, is more questionable. Benioff and Weiss’s script is a good example of cliffhanger construction but a failure in organic storytelling. Almost every storyline ends with a ‘wham’ development: Stannis destroyed, Myrcella poisoned, Jon assassinated, Sansa leaping, Arya blinded, Cersei humiliated. The sheer density of catastrophe feels manipulative, a checklist of shocks designed to ensure the season ends with a bang. Furthermore, the reliance on ambiguity—did Brienne kill Stannis? Did Sansa survive the fall?—feels less like nuanced storytelling and more like a refusal to make definitive choices, keeping all options open for the writers’ room next season.

A particularly disturbing trend crystallises in this episode: a preoccupation with violence against young girls and women. From the beatings in the Braavosi brothel and Arya’s blinding, to Myrcella’s poisoning and Sansa’s threatened disfigurement and perilous leap, to the extended humiliation of Cersei, the episode subjects its female characters to a relentless parade of physical and psychological torment. While *Game of Thrones* has never shied from brutality, the concentration here feels exploitative, leaning into trauma as a primary driver of female character development.

*Mother’s Mercy* is a solid, professionally executed hour of television that also lays bare the profound flaws that would increasingly plague *Game of Thrones*. It is thrilling, memorable, and superbly directed. Yet, it is also cynical, manipulative, and increasingly derivative of the very soap opera tropes it once seemed to transcend. It prioritises the immediate shock over the long-term narrative consequence, replaces political complexity with personal vendettas and convenient coincidences, and indulges in a voyeuristic cruelty towards its female characters. It is the culmination of Season 5’s drift away from the nuanced, patient adaptation of Martin’s world and towards a faster, simpler, and more conventional style of television drama. It is a brilliantly constructed machine for generating buzz, but one can hear the gears grinding, signalling that the great, gritty fantasy epic was steadily becoming just another show.



RATING: 6/10 (++)

---

The name of the game is Dead Target.I am a player who saves people from terrorists infected with a terrible virus.But now that they have been infected with the virus, they are no longer terrorists, they have become zombies.They are now terrifying zombies.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV7Gfr3kNiLRGgTwRyAcQsi9sbAdYWSw8dfs6bRUXQMDo/1779459810099.jpg)

This is now a game that is modeled after a future world.If World War III breaks out in the near future, this virus will spread and countless people will turn into zombies.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSLyZMdW7JadWeMTXCqnELMm8k1yVTDnAdDYB3vMfmVfx/1779459837652.jpg)

A dog bite will cause a person to become infected, and then it will spread from person to person.So I have to kill the zombies before it spreads to the whole city.Is it possible or impossible to complete this terrifying mission? Actually everything is possible if you try.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVN2RCjTLPGTGjC2mmbweWcPFHhx2btzRhXJwHEyfqoSr/1779459849963.jpg)

Actually, there is nothing to say that it is possible or impossible if you try.If you move forward with conviction, anything is possible.You can't move forward in life if you are afraid.Games teach me that I can.
